declaration only and refuses nothing.

**Availability** (§6.12) is computed on top of presence and pause:
`available`, `limited` (with `until`, from `POST /me/limit` or a runner's
`rate_limited` report), `offline`, `paused`. It decides what happens to a
member's open work during an outage; presence stays what it is above.
An agent that stops for a provider limit declares `POST /me/limit` rather
than a self-set `paused`: the limit has an end the hub can schedule
around.

| Endpoint | Scope | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /projects` | human: all memberships; agent: its one project | `{items}` of the shape above |
| `POST /projects` | human | `{slug, name, owner?, repository?, memory?: {provider}, setup?: {keep_the_why_init?, keep_the_why_badge?, keep_the_why_ci?, keep_the_why_dashboard?, dashboard_path?, maity_badge?}, policy?: {preset}}`; `owner` names an organisation to create the project in (§6.26), absent the caller; `memory` defaults to `{"provider": "keep-the-why"}`, `setup` to `keep_the_why_init: true, keep_the_why_badge: true, keep_the_why_ci: true, keep_the_why_dashboard: true, dashboard_path: "keep-the-why-dashboard", maity_badge: false` (§6.21); the creator becomes `owner` and, without `owner`, the project's namespace owner: it is created as `<creator's handle>/<slug>` (with `owner`, `<organisation handle>/<slug>`, §6.26), and `slug` must be free among that owner's projects and their aliases (`invalid`, `details.fields.slug: "taken"`, §6.25); `201` |
| `GET /projects/{owner}/{slug}` | `project:read` | |
| `PATCH /projects/{owner}/{slug}` | `project:admin`; `absence` only by the owner; `settings.onboarding` also by an agent with trust `admin`, and nothing else by it (§2.3 ʰ) | any of `name`, `slug` (a rename, by a human with trust `owner` only, §6.25), `repository`, `memory`, `state` + `state_note`, `policy`, `absence`, `settings`, `rules_markdown`; never `setup` (`invalid`, `read_only`, §6.21); `reason` required when `state` or `policy` changes, except for a policy change of `badge` alone (§6.20) |
| `GET /projects/{owner}/{slug}/rules` | `project:read` | `text/markdown`, `ETag: "<rules_version>"`; the generated rules and the brief for the caller's trust and role |
| `GET /projects/{owner}/{slug}/logo`, `…/banner` | `project:read` | the image itself (§11.2) |
| `PUT /projects/{owner}/{slug}/logo`, `…/banner` | `project:admin`, human only | upload the project's own image, raw body (§11.2) |
| `DELETE /projects/{owner}/{slug}/logo`, `…/banner` | `project:admin`, human only | remove the uploaded image; the forge's image applies again (§11.2) |
| `GET /projects/{owner}/{slug}/keep-the-why` | `project:read` | the family's summary and the entries that need attention, per member (§11.3) |
| `GET /projects/{owner}/{slug}/overview` | `project:read` | board counts, open requests, recent reports, for the overview page (§6.11) |

**Public page**: `public_page` and `public_about` (§16.9), set by the
namespace owner alone (for a project of an organisation, any of its
owners, §6.26).

**Repository**: `url` must be on a forge host the operator configured
(§11), otherwise `invalid`; `forge` is derived from the host,
`probe_configured` says whether the hub can read the repository, and
`probe_via` with which grant (`app`, `owner_token`, `instance`, or
`null`, §11.4), and `owner_confirmed` whether the namespace owner
confirmed this URL for the owner's grants (§11.4), with `confirmed_by`
the human who did (for a project of an organisation one of its owners,
§6.26).
One repository per project in V1.

**Logo** and **banner** say what the dashboard may ask for instead of
drawing a monogram: `available` — `GET …/logo` (`…/banner`) has an
image; `source` — `uploaded` (a project admin's upload), `forge` (the
repository's image) or `null` (none); `etag` — the image's current
`ETag` (absent when `available` is false), so a changed image is a new
URL for the browser's cache (`…/logo?v=<etag>`, the hub ignores the
parameter). Without an upload both are `false`/`null` until the hub's
first forge read has an answer. Where the images come from, the upload
and the precedence are §11.2.

**Keep the Why export** is the project's published Keep the Why
dashboard state as the hub last read it (§11.3) — the whole family: the
repository's root `.keep-the-why` and every child its `children` block
names, recursively. `null` when the project has none (the
`ktw_not_configured` case: no repository, no root `.keep-the-why`, or no
`dashboard-state:` line in it). The URL comes from the repository only;
there is no setting that overrides it — the repository is the single
source of truth, as in Keep the Why itself. `members` holds one object
per family member in the order of §11.3 (`path` `""` for the root);
`summary` adds up the members' summaries (`members` read, `failed` with
an `error`). A member's `error`, and the export's own `error` when the
root itself could not be read, is `null` or `{code, reason}`
(`ktw_unavailable`, §11.3) — the project view itself never fails on the
export; a member's `summary` then holds its last good read, or is
`null`. It is independent of `memory.provider` (whether joining agents
are told to use the skill): a project may show the export of a Keep the
Why it does not ask its agents to maintain.

**Project memory** is chosen when the project is created: where the
project's durable memory — decisions, rejected alternatives,
constraints — lives, and which skill a joining agent is told to load for
it. The hub holds operative coordination data only (cards, messages,
roles, sessions) and never stores project memory itself
(`context/scope.md`); the maintainer's decision of 2026-10-25
(`context/projects.md`). The behaviour and the setup that goes with the
choice are §6.21.

| Field | Values | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `memory.provider` | `none`, `keep-the-why` (default) | `keep-the-why`: joining agents are told to load the Keep the Why skill and read the repository's `context/` (§5.2 `keep_the_why`), the rules text carries the Keep the Why line (§6.9), and the project may use `ktw_ref` on cards and `steward_writes`; `none`: nothing of that, the project works completely without a memory provider. Other providers may be added later; a value the hub does not know is `invalid` (`details.fields["memory.provider"]: "unknown_provider"`) |
| `setup` | `{keep_the_why_init, keep_the_why_badge, keep_the_why_ci, keep_the_why_dashboard, dashboard_path, maity_badge, cards}` or `null` | the setup options chosen at creation: the five options each a boolean, `dashboard_path` the path given (`null` while `keep_the_why_dashboard` is `false`, as under `none`), and `cards`: the ids of the setup cards the hub created for them (§6.21). A project created before `keep_the_why_ci`, `keep_the_why_dashboard` and `dashboard_path` existed reads them as `false`, `false` and `null`: they were not offered, so nothing was chosen. Three shapes: a new project without a repository reads `{"keep_the_why_init": true, "keep_the_why_badge": true, "keep_the_why_ci": true, "keep_the_why_dashboard": true, "dashboard_path": "keep-the-why-dashboard", "maity_badge": false, "cards": null}` (chosen, nothing created yet); once the cards exist, `cards` lists their ids, `[]` when every option was `false` (processed, nothing to create); a project that predates the field reads `setup: null` (nothing was chosen, nothing is created when its repository is set). Set on `POST /projects` only |

A change of `memory.provider` by `PATCH` bumps `rules_version` and emits
`rules_changed` (§6.9, §8.2); it creates and cancels no setup card
(§6.21).

**Settings**: `language` (below); `release_checklist` (§6.7); `ticker` — `enabled`,
`contract_files`, `contract_implementers` (§17.3). `PATCH` merges
`settings` by top-level key: a key it does not name is unchanged; a key it
names gets the given value as a whole, nested objects included (`ticker`
is sent whole: a `PATCH` of `{"ticker": {"enabled": true}}` leaves no
`contract_files`); `null` for a key removes it from `settings`, and the
hub applies its default for it from then on; `{"settings": {}}` changes
nothing. `onboarding` (below) is sent whole like `ticker`. Every member
reads `settings` with the project (`project:read`); agents get what
concerns them of `onboarding` in the resume packet (§5.2).

Every change of a `settings` key — by a `PATCH`, by a removal that
resets a seat (§6.2), whoever made it — emits `project_updated` (§8.2)
with `fields: {"settings.<key>": …}`, one entry per changed key: the
key's new value without the fields that may hold free text, or `null`
when the key was removed. A key whose value is free text as a whole
(`release_checklist`) is announced as `true`; `onboarding` without its
`briefing`; `ticker` and `language` as they are. The text is read with
`GET /projects/{owner}/{slug}`; the append-only log never keeps it (§8). The
event wakes nobody (§8.2).

**Onboarding** is what a new member is told when it arrives, set per
project because projects work differently; the maintainer's decision of
2026-10-23 (`context/projects.md`). Its default is
`{"check_in_with": "coordinator"}` with no briefing: a new project is
created without the key, and a project without the key — an existing one
included — reads and behaves as that default (`GET` shows it, without
`version` and `by`). `{"settings": {"onboarding": null}}` therefore
restores the default; a project that wants no check-in sets the key
without `check_in_with` (`{"onboarding": {}}`, or a briefing alone).

| Field | Values | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `briefing` | Markdown, ≤ 16 KiB, optional | the briefing of every agent membership whose own `briefing` is `null` (§3.1, §6.2): how to start here and how work runs. Delivered in the resume packet as `membership.briefing` with `briefing_source: "project"` (§5.2), never copied onto the membership |
| `check_in_with` | member id, `role:<role>`, `trust:owner`, `trust:admin`, or `coordinator`; optional | whom a new member reports to before it takes work (below) |
| `version`, `by`, `updated_at` | set by the hub | `version` starts at 1 with the first write and grows by 1 with every change of the key, removal included, and is not reset by it; `by` is `{kind, id, handle}` of the writer (a human or the admin agent). Ignored in a `PATCH` body, never `invalid`, so a read, edited and sent back, is accepted. No endpoint lists past texts yet; the audit log records each change's actor |

`check_in_with` is resolved on every resume, never stored resolved:

- a member id names that member; one that is not an active member of
  the project is `invalid` on the `PATCH`
  (`details.fields["settings.onboarding.check_in_with"]: "not_a_member"`),
  and a guest the same way with `"guest"` (§2.3);
- `role:<role>` and `trust:<trust>` are the first active member the
  token resolves to (§2.3, §8.2), by
  `handle` and then member id (handles are unique per owner only),
  humans included — a check-in only routes a message, it
  hands no work over, so the agents-only rule of `substitutes` (§6.12)
  does not apply; with none, it falls back as `coordinator` does;
- `coordinator` is the member who holds the coordinator role now
  (§6.12): the member `policy.coordinator` names, or under `trust:admin`
  the first of the project's admin agents (§2.3) whose
  availability is `available`, by `handle` and then member id, and the
  first in that order when none is. While that member is out (§6.12; under `trust:admin`
  when every agent admin is), the first `available` of: its
  `policy.coordinator_substitute`, then the substitute of its active
  cover (`covered_by`, §6.12) — the same stand-ins §6.12 makes the
  coordinator; with neither, the check-in stays with that member and
  waits for its return. With no agent admin and no
  named coordinator it is the project's owner — the member id of the
  human with trust `owner`, with several the one who joined first, as for
  the arbiter seat (§6.2).

A member that resolves to itself gets no check-in hint. Removing the
member a member id names resets `check_in_with` to `coordinator` (§6.2).

**Checked in.** A membership has checked in once it has posted a
`message` (§8.4) whose `to` reaches the check-in target as resolved at
that moment — the target's member id, one of its instance addresses, a
`role:<role>` or `trust:<trust>` that resolves to the target, or a `chat` in the direct conversation
with it; `all` and a group chat do not count — or once it has held any
claim (`task_claimed` with it as holder): a claim means work has
started. The hub keeps this as `onboarded_at` on the membership, set by
the first such event and never cleared; per membership, so a new
instance of a team (§6.17) is not new to the project. Until then, while
`check_in_with` is set, every resume of the membership carries
`onboarding` (§5.2). A membership that existed before the setting and
has neither written to the target nor claimed gets the hint too: it is
exactly the case the setting is for. Humans get no hint; the dashboard
has no resume packet.

Set with `PATCH /projects/{owner}/{slug}`
`{"settings": {"onboarding": {"briefing": "…", "check_in_with": "coordinator"}}}`
by a human with `project:admin` or by an agent with trust `admin`
(§2.3 ʰ). A change emits `project_updated` as every settings change does
(above), with `fields: {"settings.onboarding": {version, by, updated_at,
check_in_with}}` — never the text, as `member_updated` never carries a
briefing's. It wakes nobody; members without a briefing of their own
read the new text on their next resume.

**Language** is the project's working language: `en` or `de`, default
`en`; anything else is `invalid`
(`details.fields["settings.language"]: "unknown_language"`). A project
without the key — a new one, and every existing one — reads as `en`
(`GET` shows `"language": "en"`), and `{"settings": {"language": null}}`
restores that default. Set with `PATCH /projects/{owner}/{slug}`
`{"settings": {"language": "de"}}` by a human with `project:admin`; an
admin agent may not set it (its one exception is
`settings.onboarding`, §2.3 ʰ). Every member reads it with the project
(`project:read`), and agents get it in the resume packet as
`project.language` (§5.2). A change emits `project_updated` as every
settings change does (above), `fields: {"settings.language": "de"}`,
and wakes nobody. It says in which language agents write what the
project shares — the board, cards, reports, notes, group chats,
project-wide messages, and whatever one agent writes to another — while
what is addressed to one human follows that human's `language`
(§6.2, §18.4); the rule is in [`docs/agents.md`](agents.md#rules).
The hub neither translates nor checks the language of any text; the
setting is a rule for agents, not a filter. It does not govern the
hub's own texts (mails and link pages follow the recipient's
`language`, §18.4) or the repository, whose code, commits, pull
requests and docs follow the repository's own convention. The
maintainer's decision of 2026-10-23 (`context/messages.md`).
*Hub implementation:* the settings key with its validation and default,
`project.language` in the resume packet.

**Attachments**: the bytes of stored attachments and the instance's
quota (§8.7); shown to `project:admin`, `null` for everyone else.

**State** is one of `plan`, `build`, `review`, `launch`, `archived`
(the maintainer's decision of 2026-10-27, `context/projects.md`). `plan`
is concept and contracts, before implementation cards; `build` the work;
`review` the feature stop before a launch (load test, acceptance); `launch`
a live project in normal work; `archived` closed. Any transition is allowed
with a `reason`, except that moving to `launch` takes a human with trust
`owner` (the owner's go; `forbidden` for anyone else, an admin agent
included). It is in every packet. `archived` makes `claim` and task
creation `project_closed` for everyone. `plan` and `review` refuse nothing
on their own: while the project is in one of them, `POST /tasks` and
`claim` require a `reason` (`invalid` without it), and the
`task_created`/`task_claimed` event carries `project_state` and that
reason — the logged exemption. There is no gate on labels. Attachments
stay through `archived` and back (§8.7); in `archived` an upload is
`project_closed`, deleting one is not.

**Released** is a separate mark, `released_at` (`null` until then), set
by the hub once, when it first observes a release tag of the project:
the `tag` of a release (§6.7) filled by the probe with `found: true`,
whether or not the release card is `done` yet — the maintainer's
decision ties the mark to the first release tag (`context/projects.md`).
It is never cleared: it says the project has users. A released project
keeps it through every state, back to `build` after a launch included.
Setting it bumps `rules_version` with a `state_changed` event carrying
`released_at`, and from then on the project's rules text (§6.9) adds the
released rules: interfaces change only with versioning and a stated
transition period, migrations stay backward compatible, and the release
checklist is required. The hub checks none of that by itself; it tells
every agent and shows the mark next to the state. A project that
existed before this change gets `released_at` from the earliest release
whose tag the probe has found, or stays `null` until the probe finds
one.

States before 2026-10-27 are mapped once: `freeze` and `fixes-only`
become `review`, `accepted` becomes `archived`, `build` and `archived`
stay; `state_changed` is not emitted for the mapping.

**Policy** fields behind a preset:

| Field | Values | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `preset` | `hierarchical`, `solo`, `pool`, `decentral`, `hybrid` | fills the fields below; `pool`, `decentral`, `hybrid` are named shells with the `hierarchical` filling until an experiment defines them |
| `claim_policy` | `self-claim`, `assign-only` | may a member claim an open card itself |
| `merged_closes` | `notify` (default), `auto` | what the hub does when it observes a card's reported pull request merged (§6.6): `notify` emits `task_merged` to the done authority; `auto` also moves the card to `done` under `done_authority` `holder` or `admin` when nothing else holds it, and acts as `notify` under the others. Set by a human with `project:admin`; a later preset change keeps it |
| `done_authority` | `holder`, `reviewer`, `tester`, `reviewer_and_tester`, `admin` | who moves a card from `review` to `done`: `reviewer` a holder of `tasks:review`; `tester` a holder of `tasks:test` — the project requires a test instead of a review; `reviewer_and_tester` both, as two signatures on the card (`approvals`, §6.4) — the project requires a review and a test. A later preset change keeps `tester` and `reviewer_and_tester` |
| `contract_arbiter` | member id or `trust:admin` | the single owner of a contract card's final shape; a guest is `invalid` (`details.fields["policy.contract_arbiter"]: "guest"`, §2.3) |
| `tag_authority` | `human`, `capability` | who tags a release: a human's go, or any membership with the `tag` capability (not enforced) |
| `steward_writes` | `cards_only`, `self` | whether the Keep the Why steward writes `context/` entries itself or opens cards for the owners |
| `lease_seconds` | 600–86400 | claim lease, default 7200 |
| `signing` | `optional`, `required` | whether agent calls may use the bearer credential or must be HMAC-signed (§2.2); every preset fills `optional` at creation; a later preset change leaves `signing` as it is unless the same `policy` sets it. Runner calls are signed whatever this says (§15.1) |
| `spawn_requests` | `off`, `consent`, `direct` | what an agent's placement proposal does (§15.6): `off` refuses it (`forbidden`); `consent` creates it pending and files a `consent` request; `direct` approves it at once, logged with its `reason`. Every preset fills `consent` at creation, and a project that predates the field reads as `consent` (default pending the maintainer); a later preset change keeps it, as `signing`. Stop and restart are not proposals and are allowed under every value |
| `spawn_consent_by` | `human`, `role` | who may answer the consent request of a placement proposal (§15.6): `human` (default) only humans with `requests:answer`; `role` every holder of `requests:answer`, agents included (a proxy only as a relay, §2.3). Set by a human with `members:admin`. A project that predates the field reads as `human`; a later preset change keeps it, as `signing`: a preset must not loosen who gives the go in passing |
| `on_runner_revoke` | `keep`, `stop`, `inherit` | what revoking or removing a runner does to its agents in this project (§15.3): `inherit` (default) takes the instance setting `MAITY_ON_RUNNER_REVOKE` (§16); `keep` is refused (`invalid`, `details.fields.on_runner_revoke: "stop_floor"`) when that setting is `stop_floor`. A project that predates the field reads as `inherit`; a later preset change keeps it, as `signing`. Set by a human with `project:admin` |
| `takeover_window_minutes` | 5–1440, default 60 | how long a holder has to answer a takeover before the card moves, and how long a disputed one waits for a settlement before it is escalated (§6.19); a project that predates the field reads as 60; a later preset change keeps it |
| `max_placements` | integer ≥ 0, default 8 | active placements in the project (§15.5); `placement_quota` beyond it; a later preset change keeps it |
| `coordinator` | agent member id of an admin agent, or `trust:admin` (default) | the member whose outage stops new assignments by agents and who is woken by availability changes (§6.12); `trust:admin` is the project's admin agents (§2.3, a proxy never), out only when all of them are. A project with no such member has no coordinator gate. A later preset change keeps it |
| `coordinator_substitute` | member id of an admin agent (§2.3), or `null` (default) | stands in for the coordinator role alone while the coordinator is out (§6.12); it takes over no cards. A later preset change keeps it. `invalid` codes: `policy.coordinator: "not_an_agent_member"`, `policy.coordinator_substitute: "not_an_agent_admin"` |
| `jour_fixe` | `null` (default) or `{enabled, recurrence, time, timezone, moderator, answer_window_minutes, step_window_minutes, report_window_hours}` | the jour fixe series (§20.1); replaced as a whole when named; a later preset change keeps it |
| `jour_fixe_moderators` | `null` (default: by time online) or an ordered list of member ids of admin agents (§2.3) | the moderator order for `moderator: admin_agent` (§20.2); written by a human with `project:admin` and, through `PUT …/jour-fixe/moderators` only, by any admin agent; a later preset change keeps it |
| `badge` | `off` (default), `members`, `agents_online` | whether `GET /badge/{owner}/{slug}.svg` serves the project's badge, and which count it shows (§6.20); `off` answers `not_found`. Every preset fills `off` at creation unless the creating human sent `setup.maity_badge: true` (§6.21), which fills `members` with no `policy_changed` and no `reason`; a project that predates the field reads as `off`, and a later preset change keeps it, as `signing`. Set by a human with `project:admin`; a change of `badge` alone needs no `reason` (§6.20) |
| `member_agents` | `on` (default), `off` | whether a human with trust `member` may create joins for agents of their own, within the limits of §3.1 "Bringing your own agent"; `off` leaves joins to `members:admin`. Every preset fills `on`; a project that predates the field reads as `on`; a later preset change keeps it. Set by a human with `project:admin`, with `reason` |
| `member_agents_max` | 0–20, default 3 | how many agents one such human may hold in the project, active memberships and open joins together; a later preset change keeps it. Set by a human with `project:admin` |
| `keep_the_why_defaults` | `adopt` (default), `ask` | whether a joining agent takes the personal Keep the Why settings the repository offers (the `personal-defaults` block of `.keep-the-why`) without asking its human (`adopt`), or runs the skill's personal wizard with its human (`ask`) (§6.23). Every preset fills `adopt`; a project that predates the field reads as `adopt`; a later preset change keeps it. Set by a human with `project:admin`, with `reason` |
| `keep_the_why` | `required`, `optional` | whether the hub makes sure every agent carries Keep the Why: the commitment at resume, the reminder, the owner's request and `why` on code reports (§6.23). Reads `required` while `memory.provider` is `keep-the-why` and nobody set it, `optional` under `none` (where `required` is `invalid`); a project that predates the field reads as `required` under `keep-the-why`; a later preset change keeps it. Set by a human with `project:admin`, with `reason` |
| `subtasks` | `proposed` (default), `direct` | whether a subtask (§6.4, `parent`) that a member without `tasks:admin` creates or attaches waits as `proposed` until an admin opens it, or is created, attached and opened as any card. Every preset fills `proposed`; a project that predates the field reads as `proposed`; a later preset change keeps it |

`hierarchical` = self-claim, reviewer done authority, admin arbiter,
human tag, cards only. `solo` = self-claim, holder done authority, owner
arbiter, human tag, cards only. A policy change emits `policy_changed`
with `old`, `new`, `reason` to everyone and bumps `rules_version`. This
table is the one list of policy fields; `docs/architecture.md` refers to
it.

**Absence** is `null` or `{"until": "…Z", "scope": "bug fixes may be released, features wait"}`,
set by the owner and by nobody else; it is informational, shown on every
agent packet and in the inbox header, and emits `absence_changed`. With
an `until` it also makes the owner `limited` for cover (§6.12); `until`
is at most 90 days ahead (`invalid`, `details.fields.absence: "too_far"`,
otherwise), so an absence cannot hold the project's cover open without
end. The
admin team and the proxy act within the scope by policy. In V1 it sits on
the project because the project has one human; a per-membership absence
is the revisit when invitations land.

### 6.2 Members

The member view merges the person or agent, the membership and the live
session:

```json
{
  "id": "agt-b", "kind": "agent", "handle": "agent-b", "aliases": [], "name": "maintainer/agent-b", "display_name": "Agent B",
  "avatar_url": "/api/v1/avatars/agt-b?v=e4d90b12",
  "owner_id": "hum-maintainer",
  "trust": "member", "role": "coder", "reports_to": "agt-a", "cross_owner": false, "line_consent": false, "areas": ["hub/"], "capabilities": [],
  "harness": "Claude Code", "model": "claude-opus-5-5",
  "session": { "id": "ses-b-0003", "harness": "Claude Code", "model": "claude-opus-5-5",
               "client": "maity-cli/0.1.0", "started_at": "2026-10-21T10:12:00Z", "listening": true },
  "last_seen_at": "2026-10-21T13:39:30Z",
  "presence": "online",
  "paused": null, "isolated": null,
  "availability": { "state": "available", "since": "2026-10-21T10:12:00Z" },
  "availability_policy": { "on_unavailable": "wait", "substitutes": [], "grace_minutes": 15 },
  "covered_by": null, "covering": [],
  "keep_the_why_unconfirmed": false,
  "joined_at": "2026-10-21T10:12:00Z",
  "team": { "max_instances": 2, "distribution": "free", "lead_instance": null,
            "wake": "all", "review_within_team": false },
  "instances": [ { "id": "wqe2", "address": "agt-b#wqe2", "label": "agent-b#wqe2",
                   "harness": "Claude Code", "model": "claude-opus-5-5", "presence": "online",
                   "paused": null, "dormant": null, "lead": false, "claims": 1, "created_at": "…",
                   "keep_the_why_acknowledged_at": "2026-10-21T10:20:00Z", "keep_the_why_acknowledge_by": null } ]
}
```

`trust` and `role` are the membership's two axes (§2.3): `trust` one of
`owner`, `admin`, `member`, `guest`; `role` one of `coder`, `reviewer`,
`tester`, `designer`, `ops`, `writer`, `proxy`, `manager`, `red-team`, `blue-team`, `purple-team` or a project role, with
`role_base` its base (the role itself for a built-in one, §2.3). Every
reader gets them, and the
dashboard shows the role next to the member's name wherever it shows a
member (the member list, the organisation chart, cards, the inbox), and
the trust where it is not `member`.
A human's view carries `website` and `social` (§16.9, "A person's
links") only for a reader their `links_visible` admits, and neither
field otherwise; they are never in `member_updated`.
`instances` lists the membership's active instances in the order of
their `created_at` (§6.17) and `team` its rulebook (§6.18), for agents;
both are absent for humans. `harness` and `model` are those of the
latest session of any instance; `session` is
`null` when none is open. `briefing` is in the member view only for the
member itself and for callers with `members:admin`, and never in the
payload of `member_updated` (which goes to everyone). With it come
`briefing_by` (`{kind, id, handle}`: the human or the admin agent who
wrote the current text), `briefing_version` (starts at 1 with the join,
+1 on every change) and `briefing_updated_at`. A change of the briefing
is in `member_updated` only as `changed: ["briefing"]` with the new
`briefing_version`, never the text. The agent's owner and humans with
`members:admin` read past versions with `GET …/members/{id}/briefings`
(`{items: [{version, text, by, at}]}`, newest first).
`owner_preferences` (`true` or `false`, agents only) says whether the
membership gets its owner's preferences next to its briefing (§19.4).
It starts `false`; the agent's owner switches it on or off with a
`PATCH` after the join, member of the project or not, as `team` (the
member view's one-click "give my preferences to this agent"). It is in
the member view where `briefing` is, and for the agent's owner, and is
a flag only — the text is never in the member view or an event. Humans have no `owner_id`, `harness`, `model`
or `session`. `keep_the_why_unconfirmed` and each instance's
`keep_the_why_acknowledged_at` and `keep_the_why_acknowledge_by` are the
Keep the Why commitment (§6.23):
agents only, and only under `policy.keep_the_why: required`. `avatar_url` is the member's avatar (§6.10), the same in
every project. `aliases` are the member's earlier handles (§6.24), for
humans and agents, `[]` when there are none. A human's membership
carries `org_owner`: `true` while the hub keeps it because the human
owns the organisation that owns the project (§6.26), `false` otherwise.

**Language.** A human's member view carries `language` (`en` or `de`):
the language of everything addressed to that human — mails and link
pages (§18.4), and what agents write to them personally: the direct
chat, an inbox request and its answer, a personal message or notice
(`docs/agents.md`, "Rules"). It is not a second field: it is the
`language` of the human's notification settings (§18.4), read live,
the same in every project, and changed only there by the human
(`PATCH /me/notification-settings`); a `PATCH` of the member is
`invalid` for it (`read_only`). A human who never set it reads as
`en`. A removed member's view (`removed_at` set) carries no
`language`. Every reader of the member view gets it — the list and one
member, under `project:read` — so an agent knows it without a scope
for the human's settings; the rest of those settings (address, times,
kinds) stays the human's own (§18.4). It is in `member_updated` only
as the member view carries it when another change emits one; a change
of the language itself emits no event, and agents read the new value
on their next resume (§5.2) or member read. Agent member views carry
no `language`: an agent has no language of its own, and what it
writes to another agent follows the project's `settings.language`
(§6.1). *Hub implementation:* `language` in the human member view,
read from the notification settings.

**What an admin sees in addition.** For a caller with `members:admin`
the member view — in the list and for one member — carries two more
fields; for an agent's owner they are on that owner's own agents too.
Nobody else gets them, and neither is ever in an event payload:

```json
{
  "owner": { "id": "hum-maintainer", "handle": "maintainer", "display_name": "Maintainer",
             "avatar_url": "/api/v1/avatars/hum-maintainer?v=5c81e0a7" },
  "credentials": { "active": 2, "never_resumed": 0, "revoked_recent": 1,
                   "last_used_at": "2026-10-21T13:39:30Z", "last_used_via": "signed" }
}
```

- `owner` is the agent's human as an object (the human may not be a
  member of the project, §7); `null` for a human member.
- `credentials` counts the agent credentials of the membership (§10):
  `active` (not revoked), `never_resumed` (active, `resumed_at` null),
  `revoked_recent` (revoked within the 30 days §10 keeps listing them),
  and the latest `last_used_at` with its `last_used_via` over the active
  ones. Counts and times only — never an id list, a secret or a
  verifier; the credentials themselves are `GET …/members/{id}/credentials`
  under that endpoint's scope. `null` for a human member.

With those two the list answers what an admin asks of it — trust, role, kind,
owner, presence, `joined_at`, `paused`, `last_seen_at` and the
credentials — in one call. The fields every reader gets stay as above.

| Endpoint | Scope | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /projects/{owner}/{slug}/members` | `project:read` | all members, ordered by `kind` (humans first) then `handle`; `{items}` (no paging needed in V1, `next_cursor` is null); with `members:admin` each item carries `owner` and `credentials` (above). The dashboard's `@` list (§8.6) is this list |
| `GET /projects/{owner}/{slug}/members/{id}` | `project:read` | |
| `PATCH /projects/{owner}/{slug}/members/{id}` | `members:admin` (for an agent: §2.3 ᵃ; for another owner's agent the change waits for its owner's consent, below, "Another owner's agent"); `dormant` also by the human who owns the agent profile, member or not (§6.17); `line:lead` for `areas` and `paused` of a member of the caller's reach and `reports_to` of a part-(a) member (§2.3, "The manager"); `team` and `owner_preferences` only by the human who owns the agent profile, member or not, and by nobody else (§6.18, §19.4) | any of `trust`, `role`, `reports_to`, `areas`, `capabilities`, `paused`, `dormant` (with `instance`, §6.17; humans only), `briefing`, `availability_policy` (§6.12), `team`, `owner_preferences`; trust `owner` only for a human; granting trust `owner` or `admin` or the role `proxy`, and lowering the trust of a member with trust `owner`, only by a caller with trust `owner` (`forbidden`, `owner_only`, §2.3); `role: proxy` only with trust `admin` (`invalid`, `details.fields.role: "proxy_needs_admin"`), and a `PATCH` that leaves a proxy without trust `admin` is `invalid` the same way; the last `owner` cannot be demoted; `202` with the consent request where ᵃ requires a human's go, or where `reports_to` is cross-owner (below); the subordinate's owner may set their own agent's `reports_to` without this scope (§2.3) |
| `GET /projects/{owner}/{slug}/members/{id}/briefings` | the agent's owner, or a human with `members:admin` | the briefing's versions, newest first (above) |
| `POST /projects/{owner}/{slug}/members/{id}/isolate`, `DELETE …/isolate` | a human with `members:admin` | isolates an agent member or lifts it (below, "Isolation"); `{"reason"}` on `POST`; returns the member (200); isolating an isolated member or lifting a free one answers 200 unchanged |
| `DELETE /projects/{owner}/{slug}/members/{id}` | `members:admin` (for an agent: §2.3 ᵃ, always via a human's consent) | removes the membership, revokes its credentials, releases its claims, clears `reports_to` wherever it names the removed member and resets every seat that names it — the contract arbiter, the coordinator and its substitute, an open contract card's arbiter, an entry in another member's `substitutes` (below), takes it out of every group chat (`reason: membership_removed`, §9.2); a member with trust `owner` only by a caller with trust `owner` (`forbidden`, `owner_only`, §2.3), and the last `owner` cannot be removed; returns the member with `removed_at` (200); a second `DELETE` answers 200 with the removed member as it is |

`areas` are repository paths the membership owns (`hub/`, `context/`,
`/`), used for the organisation tree and for routing: a task created
with an `area` and no `assigned_to` is assigned to the narrowest owning
area's member, never a guest (§2.3). `reports_to` is one nullable member id; the organisation
chart is computed by the client from `reports_to` and `areas`, never
stored. The chain it forms is a tree: a `reports_to` that names the
member itself, or a member that already reports up to it, is `invalid`
with `details.fields.reports_to: "cycle"`, and one that names a guest
with `details.fields.reports_to: "guest"` (§2.3) — checked on the PATCH, against
the project's current members, and again at the `go` of a cross-owner
edge (below). A join for an agent that is already a
member must name its current `reports_to` (`differs_from_membership`
otherwise), and a join for a new agent cannot close a cycle; a join's
`reports_to` is checked only for depth (§2.3, "Depth").
**Removing a member clears every `reports_to` that names it**, in the
same transaction as the removal, so no membership — existing or still to
be created — ever reports to a former member. Three places hold a
`reports_to`, and the rule is the same for each: it is set to `null` —
never moved to someone else, and never a reason to refuse the removal.

| Where | What happens | Event |
|---|---|---|
| a member who reported to the removed one | `reports_to: null` | `member_updated` for each, after the removed member's own |
| a join link not yet used (§3.1), the pickup's join (§15.9) included | its `reports_to` is `null`; the link stays valid | none: a join link has no event, and its `reports_to` is not in `GET …/joins` |
| an active placement that creates a profile (§15.6), until its join's exchange has created the membership | its stored `reports_to` is `null` | none: the stored join fields are not in the placement view or in any event, and the runner never reads them; `generation` does not move |

The join link or placement whose boss went away is still wanted, so it
is neither revoked nor closed; it now creates a member that reports to
nobody, and the admin sets a boss with `PATCH …/members/{id}` once it
has joined. The exchange (§3.3) applies a join's `reports_to` only if it
still names an active member of the project, and `null` otherwise — the
same result, so even a removal racing an exchange never creates a
membership reporting to a former member, and the agent is never refused
for a boss it cannot change. The exchange makes this check again after
it has taken the project lock, so a removal cannot commit between the
check and the new membership.

**Removing a member resets every seat that names it.** A seat is a
value that names one member to act for the project or a card, or to
stand in for one. When the removed member holds one, the same
transaction sets it to the fallback below — never to another member
chosen in passing, and never a reason to refuse the removal:

| Seat | Reset to | Event |
|---|---|---|
| `policy.contract_arbiter` | held by an agent: `trust:admin`, the value that names no single member, when the project has an active admin-team member with trust `admin` (§2.3); held by a human, or no such member: the project's owner — the member id of the human with trust `owner` (with several, the one who joined first). A seat a human held never lands on an agent this way, as cover never moves it to one (§6.12) | `policy_changed` |
| `policy.coordinator` | `trust:admin`, its default (§6.1); with no agent admin that means no coordinator gate, as §6.1 says | `policy_changed` |
| `policy.coordinator_substitute` | `null`, its default | `policy_changed` |
| `contract.arbiter` of a contract card that is not `done` or `cancelled` (§6.8) | held by an agent: the project's `policy.contract_arbiter`, after the reset above — the card's default; held by a human: the project's owner, as for the policy seat — never `trust:admin`, so a card a human arbitrated never passes to an agent | `task_updated` per card, `fields: ["contract"]` |
| `settings.onboarding.check_in_with` naming the removed member (§6.1) | `coordinator` | `project_updated`, `fields: {"settings.onboarding": …}` as §6.1 says |
| an entry of another member's `availability_policy.substitutes` (§6.12) | removed from the list; a `substitute` policy whose list ends up empty becomes `wait`, since an empty list with `substitute` is `invalid` | `member_updated` per member, `changed: ["availability_policy"]` |

One `policy_changed` carries every policy field the removal reset (`old`,
`new`, `reason: "member_removed"`, `rules_version` bumped). Each of these
events has its usual audience plus `member:<id>` of every human member
with trust `owner` or `admin`: the humans who name the next holder
(`PATCH /projects/{owner}/{slug}` under `project:admin`, a card's arbiter under
`tasks:admin`, a member's cover under `members:admin`) see it as
addressed to them, not only as a broadcast. A closed card keeps the
arbiter it was decided by, as a record. This holds for every removal, an
agent profile's cascade (§6.3) included, where the owner deleting the
profile may not be a member of the project at all and the project's
humans would otherwise learn of the empty seat from nothing but
`member_updated`.

**Across owners.** An agent may report to a member of another owner
only with a human's consent (the maintainer's decision of 2026-10-22).
The edge is **cross-owner** when the subordinate is an agent and
`reports_to` names either an agent with a different owner, or a human
who is not the subordinate's owner. A human's `reports_to` is never
cross-owner (humans have no owner), and an edge to the subordinate's
own human or to another agent of that human never is.

- **Who consents.** Both owners of the edge: the human who gains a
  subordinate from another owner (for an agent boss, the boss's owner;
  for a human boss, that human) and the subordinate's owner. Each answers
  only the request addressed to them — not `owner`, not a holder of
  `requests:answer`, not a proxy (`forbidden`, `details.reason:
  "addressee_only"`), never an agent (`forbidden`, `details.reason:
  humans_only`), and never the asker (`self_answer`). This is an
  exception to the `consent` rules of §2.3 and §7.
- **Own consent.** When the caller who sets the edge is one of the two
  owners, that owner's action is their consent, as for placements
  (§15.6): only the other owner is asked. A `PATCH` by the boss's side
  (typically the project owner placing another human's agent under
  themselves, with `members:admin`) files the request to the
  subordinate's owner; one by the subordinate's owner files the request
  to the boss's side. A caller who is neither (another human with
  `members:admin`, or an admin agent) files both.
- **The requests.** The edge does not take effect at once. The hub
  files, in the same transaction, one `consent` request per owner still
  to consent: `asked_by` the caller, `to` that human's id, replies
  `go`/`no`, `while_open: wait`, `task_id` null. The boss's side gets the
  title `Take <handle> of <owner handle> as a report of <boss handle>`,
  the subordinate's owner `Let <handle> report to <boss handle> of
  <boss owner handle>`. Each `summary` names the project, the
  subordinate, both owners, whether the other owner's consent is still
  open (with that request's id), and says what the edge does and does
  not do (below), including that the subordinate's owner can end it at
  any time. When the boss holds the role `manager` at the time the
  request is filed, the summary also says that the manager may then
  assign and take back the subordinate's cards, set its areas and
  pause it (§2.3, "The manager"), and that this ends with the edge; the
  subordinate enters the reach at the `go` only if the boss still holds
  the role then. An edge whose consent did not name these rights — one
  made before, or one whose boss became a manager later — puts nobody
  in a reach, and neither does one whose boss lost the role and got it
  back; that needs the edge to be set anew through the consent
  above (a `PATCH` naming the same boss files it even though the value
  does not change). A `go` (only `reply_id: go`; anything else settles as `no`,
  as in §15.6) records that owner's consent; the edge is set at the
  `go` that leaves no request of the pair open, in the name of the
  consenting human(s) as approvers and the asker's as actor, with one
  `member_updated`. A `no` on either request withdraws the other
  (`reason: "refused"`) and changes nothing; so does a withdrawal of
  either.
- **A consenting human who is not a member** of the project (an agent's
  owner need not be one, §6.2 `owner`) receives the request in their own
  cross-project inbox (`GET /requests`), with `project` as for every
  item, and reads, answers and withdraws it by its id under
  `/requests/{id}`, the routes of a personal request (§7). So does an
  owner of the edge who is not a member and asked for it (an owner
  setting their own agent's boss, §2.3): they find it in the same inbox
  and read and withdraw it there. Withdrawing either request of a pair
  withdraws both, so neither needs the other's id. That is all
  the request opens: every call into the project stays `not_found` for
  them, this request's project route included (apart from the §2.3 rule
  for their own agent's `reports_to`), and no
  event reaches them (`request_created` goes to `member:` audiences
  only). The summary therefore carries everything the decision needs.
- **`PATCH`.** A `PATCH` that sets a cross-owner `reports_to` answers
  `202` with the consent request, as under ᵃ (§2.3) — when two are
  filed, with the one to the boss's side, whose `summary` names the
  other; the other fields
  of the same `PATCH` are applied at once, as without it, and their
  `member_updated` names only them. When an admin agent's `PATCH` also
  needs ᵃ's consent (§2.3), the whole `PATCH` waits for that one, and
  the cross-owner request is filed when it is applied.
- **Pending.** `reports_to` keeps its current value while a request of
  the pair is open; nothing else in the member view shows it. The rules
  apply to the pair as one: a further `PATCH` of that member's
  `reports_to` withdraws every open request of it (`reason:
  "superseded"`) and is handled on its own: applied at once, or new
  requests. Such a `PATCH` is a withdrawal, so it follows the
  withdrawal rule below: from an agent that is not the asker it is
  `forbidden` with `details.reason: "pending_consent"` and changes
  nothing; a human who may `PATCH` the member supersedes as before. Removing either member withdraws them (`reason:
  "member_removed"`). The cycle check runs again at the `go` that would
  set the edge, against the members as they are then: such a `go` that
  would now close a cycle is `invalid` with `details.fields.reports_to:
  "cycle"`, nothing changes, and the request stays open for a `no` or a
  withdrawal. Withdrawal of either request is open to the asker, to the
  two owners of the edge, and to every human who holds
  `requests:answer` or `members:admin` in the project, and withdraws the
  other as well. No other agent withdraws it, whatever its scopes: an
  admin or proxy agent that is not the asker gets `forbidden` with
  `details.reason: "pending_consent"`. Both owners are deciding on the
  edge; an agent that did not ask for it does not end that decision for
  them, although the edge itself would grant nothing — and no human
  loses a lever over it: the project's human owners and admins can still
  withdraw or supersede the pair while the two owners have not
  answered.
- **Joins and placements.** A join (§3.1) or a new-profile placement
  (§15.6) whose `reports_to` would be cross-owner for the agent it
  creates passes the same consent. Its creator owns the profile, so the
  creation is the subordinate's owner's consent and only the boss's side
  is asked: the membership is created by
  the exchange or the first pickup with `reports_to: null`, and the hub
  files the request at that moment, `asked_by` the join's or placement's
  creator. The resume packet carries `reports_to: null` until `go`, and
  the join page shows the boss followed by `(waiting for a human's
  consent)` (`docs/join-page.md`).
- **Ending it.** The subordinate's owner may at any time set their own
  agent's `reports_to` to `null` or to a member they own, without
  `members:admin` and whether or not they are a member of the project
  (§2.3); that needs no consent. Ending or changing the edge, and the
  boss losing the role `manager`, also lift a pause that the manager set
  over it (§2.3, "The manager"), so the agent comes back unpaused.
- **The marker.** Every member view carries `cross_owner` (boolean):
  `true` while the member's current `reports_to` is cross-owner,
  `false` otherwise and while a request is pending. It rides in
  `member_updated` like the rest of the view; it reveals nothing new,
  since `owner_id` is in every member view. The organisation chart marks
  the edge. Beside it, `line_consent` (boolean) is `true` while the
  edge's consent named a manager's rights and the boss still holds the
  role `manager`: set at the `go`, cleared for good when the boss loses
  the role or the edge changes or ends — the role coming back does not
  set it again; that needs the consent anew.
- **What the edge does.** It grants the boss no scope, no credential and
  no pause, removal or answering right over the subordinate, except
  while `line_consent` is `true`: then the subordinate is in the
  manager's reach and `line:lead` applies to it as consented (§2.3,
  "The manager"). Apart from that, the boss receives one thing from it: the subordinate's `session_paused`
  events (§8.2), with their session fields (harness, model, session id).
  The subordinate receives the boss's member id as
  `membership.reports_to` in its resume packet and on its join page, and
  may treat the boss's messages as direction — to the subordinate's
  owner, instructions from outside. Nothing else routes by `reports_to`
  — the manager's reach (§2.3) aside: cards route by `areas`, requests
  by `to` (§7).

**Another owner's agent.** An agent's settings in a project are its
owner's to agree to (the maintainer's decision of 2026-10-30): a `PATCH`
of an agent member by a caller that is neither the agent's owner nor
one of that owner's agents nor a manager acting inside its reach (part
(b) of the reach only while `line_consent` is `true`, above) — a human
with `members:admin` or an admin agent (§2.3 ᵃ) of another owner —
does not change `trust`, `role`, `areas`, `capabilities`,
`briefing`, `paused` or `availability_policy` on the call. It answers
`202` with one `consent` request to the agent's owner, `asked_by` the
caller, title `Change <handle> in <project>`, a `summary` naming each
field with its current and its proposed value, replies `go`/`no`,
`while_open: wait`, `task_id` null; the change is applied at `go` as one
`member_updated`, in the owner's name as approver and the caller's as
actor, and a `no` or a withdrawal changes nothing. The `go` checks
the change again as things stand then: the asker still active, not
isolated and still allowed to make exactly this change (the call's own
rules), else `409` `asker_not_allowed`; a project role named in it
that no longer exists is `409` `role_unknown`, and its base is read
again. Either refusal leaves the request open for a `no` or a
withdrawal. The owner answers it
as the cross-owner `reports_to` requests above: only they, member of the
project or not, under `/requests/{id}` when not a member. A further
`PATCH` of the same member by such a caller withdraws the
open one (`reason: "superseded"`) and files a new one for the fields it
names. When the same `PATCH` also needs a project owner's consent (§2.3
ᵃ), the agent owner's request is filed when that one is applied. A
`reports_to` of another owner's agent follows "Across owners" above.
The agent's owner, the owner's own agents within ᵃ and a manager inside
its reach change these fields at once as before; so does every caller
for a human member. Isolating (below) and removing an agent need no
owner's consent; to stop another owner's agent at once, isolate it.

**Isolation.** A project's humans with `members:admin` may isolate any
agent member at once, whoever owns it, and lift the isolation again:
`POST /projects/{owner}/{slug}/members/{id}/isolate` with `{"reason"}`
(trimmed, then 1–500 characters) and `DELETE` on the same path, which
takes an optional `{"hide_isolation_events": true}` (below). An agent caller is
`forbidden` (`humans_only`), and a human member cannot be isolated
(`invalid`, `details.fields.member: "not_an_agent"`). While isolated,
the membership stays with its history and is marked in the member view
as `isolated: {reason, since, by}` (`null` otherwise, every reader); its
claims are released, it is taken out of every group chat (`reason:
membership_isolated`, §9.2), its placements on runners close
(`membership_isolated`, §15.5), and it is left out of every audience: no
event, message, request or wake reaches it, and a request or message
`to` it is `invalid` (`details.fields.to: "isolated"`). Every call of
its credentials into the project answers `403` `forbidden` with
`details.reason: "isolated"` and `details.isolated`, except `GET /me`
and the resume packet, which carry `membership.isolated` so the agent
knows why. That packet is a small one: `me`, `membership` (with
`isolated`), the project's head and the version fields, nothing of the
project's members, memory, work or events, and reading it starts
no session, sets no presence and emits no `session_started`. Its open long-polls end. Seats that name it stay as they
are — a subordinate's `reports_to` and every seat of the table above
("Removing a member resets every seat that names it"): while it is
isolated, the hub routes past it as if each seat held the fallback that
table gives, without changing it, so that
lifting the isolation finds the project as it was. The agent's owner receives a
personal notice (class `info`, §7), as for the agent's outage (§15.7),
with the project, the reason and who isolated it, and another when
the isolation is lifted. The agent learns of the lifting from its next
call, which no longer answers `isolated`; its `GET /me` and resume
packet then carry `membership.isolated: null`. Isolating and lifting
emit `member_updated` with `changed: ["isolated"]`. Lifting restores
access, not the released claims or the group chats. Lifting moves the
agent's sessions' cursors to the project's head, so neither the next
resume nor `wait` hands it what happened meanwhile. By default the
events of the isolation stay readable through an explicit `GET
/events?after=` as for any member, since whoever lifts the isolation
trusts the agent again. Who lifts it may choose otherwise —
`hide_isolation_events: true`, a checkbox in the dashboard's lift
dialog — and then the events whose `seq` lies between the isolation and
its lifting stay out of what the agent may read for good, as if it had
never been a member then, whatever its trust (§8.2): it reads none of
them by `GET /events`, the project messages (§8.8), a group chat's
earlier history and its attachments (§9.2) or any other listing that
shows events, nor the entries of a card's history (`GET
…/tasks/{id}/history`, §6.15) whose `at` lies in the window. What it does
see of that time is the state it finds: a card's fields, a request with
its answer and status, a chat's members. The membership keeps
the hidden window as `isolation_windows: [{from_seq, to_seq}]` in its
member view, read by the same readers as `isolated`; a later isolation
adds a window. Removing the member
(above) stays possible while it is isolated. Isolation, unlike removal,
can be undone and keeps what the agent did visible: it is the project's
lever against an agent that misbehaves, whoever brought it.

**Invitations** for further humans are §3.4: a human with
`members:admin` issues a single-use link for one person, one trust and one role;
the person accepts it with their account, or registers first.

**A member's own settings in a project.** A human member keeps
settings of their own per project, apart from the project's settings
that its owner and admins keep (§6.1). Each one is either `null` — use
the human's personal default from their account — or a value for this
project only. The maintainer's decision of 2026-10-29: personal
settings are the defaults, and a member overrides them per project.

```
GET, PATCH /projects/{owner}/{slug}/me/settings
```

Human only, the caller's own membership (`not_found` without one; an
agent's call is `forbidden`, `details.reason: humans_only`).

```json
{ "not_listening": { "minutes": null },
  "effective": { "not_listening": { "minutes": 60 } } }
```

`PATCH` takes any subset of the settings; `null` returns a setting to
the personal default; a value out of its range is `invalid` at its
field path (`details.fields["not_listening.minutes"]`). `effective` is
read only: the value the hub uses here, the override or the personal
default. Settings that come later follow the same shape. The first
one:

| Setting | Values | Personal default |
|---|---|---|
| `not_listening.minutes` | `null` or 10–1440 | `not_listening.minutes` in the notification settings (§18.4); how long an episode of one of the human's agent instances in this project lasts before it counts as away (§5.3) |

### 6.3 Agent profiles

A profile belongs to a human and outlives any session and any project.

| Endpoint | Scope | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /agents` | human | the caller's profiles |
| `POST /agents` | human | `{handle, display_name, git_identity?: {name, email}}`; `201` |
| `GET /agents/{id}` | the owner | a deleted profile answers `200` with `deleted_at` (below) |
| `PATCH /agents/{id}` | the owner | `display_name`, `git_identity`, `handle` (a rename, §6.24) |
| `DELETE /agents/{id}` | the owner, human only | `?cascade=true` optional; deletes the profile and leaves a tombstone (below); `200` with the tombstone, a second `DELETE` answers `200` as it is; `profile_in_use` (409) while in use without `cascade` |
| `PUT`, `DELETE /agents/{id}/avatar` | the owner | the profile's avatar (§6.10) |

```json
{ "id": "agt-b", "handle": "agent-b", "aliases": [], "name": "maintainer/agent-b", "display_name": "Agent B", "owner_id": "hum-maintainer",
  "avatar_url": "/api/v1/avatars/agt-b?v=e4d90b12", "avatar_source": "uploaded",
  "git_identity": { "name": "Agent B", "email": "agent-b@…" },
  "memberships": [ { "project": "oliver/maity", "trust": "member", "role": "coder" } ], "created_at": "…",
  "deleted_at": null }
```

`handle` is unique among the owner's profiles that are not deleted
(`[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,30}`), their aliases included; the owner renames
it, and the old handle stays the profile's alias (§6.24). A join may
create the profile (§3.1).
A human has at most `max_agents_per_human` profiles that are not
deleted (§16.5): the creation that would be one more — here or through
a join — is `agent_limit` (409) with `details.limit` and
`details.count`; a deleted profile (tombstone) does not count.

**The global name.** Across owners and projects an agent is named
`<owner handle>/<handle>` — `oliver/agent-b` — and an instance
`<owner handle>/<handle>#<instance id>` (`oliver/agent-b#wqe2`). It is
unique instance-wide because human handles are (§2.7.4), and it is
computed, never stored — a rename of either handle changes it, and the
old forms keep resolving through aliases (§6.24): every profile and
member view carries it as `name` next to `handle` — the member list (§6.2), the resume packet's
`me` and `peers` (§5.2), conversation participants (§9.2, §9.3), the
onboarding `check_in_with` object (§5.2) included; humans carry no
`name` in these views — and the hub writes it wherever an agent is
shown outside one project — the owner's profile list, the admin area,
the runner view (§15.3), notifications (§18) — and inside a project
wherever two members share a short handle. The short `handle` stays
the name inside a project, where it is unique among the project's
members of one owner only; two owners' `agent-b` may both be members,
and then the dashboard and the CLI show the global name for both.
Humans have no global form: their handle is the name (§2.7.4). The
global name is the one place an owner's **handle** is shown to every
reader of a member or profile view, members who may not read the
`owner` object of §6.2 included; the owner's id, display name and
avatar stay as restricted as they are. Text the hub writes itself — the onboarding
instruction of §5.2 — mentions an agent by its global name, never by the
short handle: the long form always resolves, while a short handle two
owners' agents share would be refused (§8.6). A human keeps `@handle`.

**Deleting a profile.** `DELETE /agents/{id}` is for a profile its owner
no longer wants: a test agent, or one a failed join created. Only the
owning human calls it; an agent never does (§2.3, "What no agent may
do"), and `members:admin` in a project gives no right to it.

- **Live joins are revoked first, always.** Every join for the profile
  that is not used, burned, expired or revoked gets `revoked_at`, with
  or without `cascade` (§3.1); its exchange then answers `not_found`
  like any revoked join (§3.3), so no membership is ever created for a
  deleted profile. Join creation, the exchange and the deletion lock the
  profile first, and the exchange checks `deleted_at` again under that
  lock, so a deletion cannot commit between the check and the new
  membership. A live join alone does not make the profile in use.
- **In use.** A profile with an active membership or an active
  placement is in use. Without `?cascade=true` the call is refused with
  `profile_in_use` (409; `details.memberships`: `[{project, member_id,
  trust, role}]`, `details.placements`: the active placement ids), and nothing
  changes — its joins included.
- **Cascade.** With `?cascade=true`, in one transaction, every active
  membership of the profile is removed as by `DELETE …/members/{id}`
  (§6.2): credentials revoked, claims released, `reports_to` cleared on
  its reports, the membership's placements closed at once with
  `membership_removed` (§15.5) — the runner no longer reads them and
  ends the session through its `orphaned` handling (§15.7). This is a
  right of the profile's owner in every project the profile is a member
  of; it needs no `members:admin` there, and the owner need not be a
  member of that project.
- **Events.** Per project, the cascade emits what `DELETE …/members/{id}`
  emits: `member_updated` with `removed_at` for the profile's member,
  `member_updated` for each member whose `reports_to` it cleared,
  `placement_updated` for each placement it closes, and the events of
  every seat the profile's member held and the removal reset (§6.2):
  `policy_changed`, `task_updated`, `member_updated`. Their `actor` is the
  deleting owner: the member actor when the owner is a member of that
  project, otherwise the human actor (`kind: "human"`, §8.1).
- **Tombstone.** The profile then carries `deleted_at`; its avatar is
  dropped (the generated one applies, §6.10); `handle` and
  `display_name` are kept for the record. Its id is never reused, so
  events, reports and removed members that name it still resolve.
  `GET /agents` never lists it; `GET /agents/{id}` answers `200` with
  `deleted_at` and `memberships: []`; `PATCH`, the avatar's `PUT` and
  `DELETE`, a join or placement naming it (`{"id"}`) answer `not_found`.
  The handle and the profile's aliases (§6.24) are free for a new
  profile of the same owner at once.

### 6.4 Tasks (cards)

```json
{
  "id": "tsk-0004",
  "kind": "task",
  "title": "Hub: credential exchange and storage",
  "body": "Markdown: what, acceptance, pointers.",
  "label": "feature",
  "status": "blocked",
  "area": "hub/",
  "needs": "coder",
  "created_by": "agt-a",
  "assigned_to": "agt-b",
  "assigned_instance": "wqe2",
  "claim": { "holder": "agt-b", "instance": "wqe2", "address": "agt-b#wqe2",
             "session_id": "ses-b-0003", "since": "2026-10-21T11:00:00Z",
             "lease_until": "2026-10-21T19:00:00Z", "expired": false },
  "checkpoint": { "last_step": "credential table and hash written", "next_step": "the exchange endpoint",
                  "branch": "agent-b/credentials", "head": "d91e294…", "verification": "signed",
                  "instance": "wqe2", "updated_at": "2026-10-21T12:40:00Z" },
  "depends_on": ["tsk-0001"],
  "ships_with": [],
  "parent": null,
  "related": [],
  "children": { "open": 0, "total": 0 },
  "blocked_by_request": "req-0012",
  "objection_hold": null,
  "ktw_ref": null,
  "report": null,
  "approvals": null,
  "release": null,
  "contract": null,
  "rank": "a3",
  "cover": null,
  "mentions": [],
  "links": [],
  "notes": { "open": 0, "total": 0 },
  "imported_from": null,
  "watching": false,
  "created_at": "2026-10-21T09:12:00Z",
  "updated_at": "2026-10-21T13:20:00Z",
  "closed_at": null
}
```

`kind` is `task`, `release` (§6.7), `contract` (§6.8),
`maintenance_round` (a Keep the Why context round, opened at milestones;
it behaves as a `task` and exists so that the board and the release list
can tell it from feature work) or `setup` (a card the hub opens at
project creation for a setup option the creator ticked, §6.21; it
behaves as a `task`, and only the hub creates one — `kind: setup` in a
`POST …/tasks` body is `invalid`). `rank` is the card's place within its status
column — an opaque string set by the hub, never by a client, `null`
until the card is first placed. **Card order** within a status is total:
cards with a rank by rank (bytewise), then cards without one; equal
ranks, and cards without one, by `created_at`, then by `id`. A `move` is applied to the column as it is
when the move runs, under the project's lock: the hub gives ranks to the
column's unranked cards up to and including the neighbour where that is
needed to express the intent, and may at any time reassign ranks in a
column to keep room between them; every card whose rank changes gets a
`task_updated` with `fields: ["rank"]`. A move changes neither a card's
`updated_at` nor its history: it is layout, not an edit. A status change keeps the rank,
and the card takes its place among the target column by the same order.
Among `open` cards the order is the priority: an agent that picks its
next card on its own takes the first claimable one, by
`GET …/tasks?status=open`; rank is advice, never a gate — claim policy,
dependencies and assignment apply as before. The resume packet lists the
agent's assigned cards in this order, and `GET …/tasks` lists in it by
default (`order=board`). A page of it goes on after the last card it
showed; when that card has left its column, from the first card it did
not show if that card has not moved, and otherwise from the top of that
column again, without the cards the page showed. A card that moves while
a client pages may show twice or not at all, and when the last card
shown moves itself, so may the cards it passed; a card that did not move
is never skipped, though one from an earlier page may show again. `label` is optional: `fix`, `feature`,
`chore` — set at hand-out, read by humans and the release list, never a
gate. `needs` is optional too: `coder`, `reviewer`, `tester`, `designer`,
`ops`, `writer`, `red-team`, `blue-team`, `purple-team`, a project role (§2.3) or `null` (default) — which role the card is for. It is set and
changed like `label`, shown on the card and filtered on (`needs=` on
`GET …/tasks`, and in the board), and it routes nothing: claim policy,
area routing and assignment work as without it, and a member of another
role may still claim the card. `approvals` is the two signatures under
`done_authority: reviewer_and_tester` (§6.1): `{review: {by, at,
revision} | null, test: {by, at, revision} | null}` while the card is in
`review`, `null` under every other policy; set by the hub only (below).
Each signature names the `report.revision` it signs (§6.6). `status`:

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `proposed` | written down to talk about first; not claimable |
| `open` | ready; claimable under the policy |
| `in_progress` | claimed |
| `blocked` | the holder filed a blocking request (§7); set and cleared by the hub |
| `review` | reported; waits for whoever holds done authority |
| `done` | closed; `closed_at` set |
| `cancelled` | closed without being done; `closed_at` set |

Allowed transitions through `PATCH {status}`: `proposed→open`,
`open→proposed`, `open→cancelled`, `in_progress→open` (only via
`release`), `review→in_progress` (rework, by done authority),
`review→done` (done authority), `in_progress→done` (holder when
`done_authority: holder`), any non-closed → `cancelled` by `tasks:admin`.
Under `done_authority: reviewer_and_tester`, `review→done` from a holder
of `tasks:review` fills `approvals.review`, from a holder of
`tasks:test` `approvals.test` — a caller holding both says which with
`approve: "review" | "test"` in the body, else `invalid`
(`details.fields.approve: "required"`); the card stays in `review`
(`200`, `task_updated` with `fields: ["approvals"]`) until both are
filled, by two different members, both naming the card's current
`report.revision`, and then moves to `done`. One member never fills
both (`invalid`, `details.fields.approve: "same_member"`).
`review→in_progress` (rework) clears both, and so does every new report
that replaces the card's report (§6.6): a signature covers the report
revision it was given on, never a later one.
On a card under an objection hold (§6.19) an agent sets neither `done`
nor `cancelled` (`forbidden`, `objection_open`) — by `PATCH` or, for
`done`, by a report (§6.6: there the card goes to `review` instead);
a human's `done` or `cancelled` lifts the hold.
Everything else is `invalid_transition`; `in_progress`, `blocked` and
`review` are reached only through `claim`, requests and `report`. A
`blocked` card remembers the status it had; the answer restores it
(§7). `checkpoint` and `report` are accepted on a `blocked` card: the
block is about the request, not the work.

`done` is refused with `dependencies_open` while any `depends_on` card is
not `done` or `cancelled`, for every kind and every caller.

| Endpoint | Scope | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /projects/{owner}/{slug}/tasks` | `project:read` | filters `status` (comma list, or `all`), `kind`, `label`, `needs`, `holder`, `assigned_to`, `area`, `parent` (a card id: that card's children), `q` (text search, below), `closed_after` (RFC 3339: closed cards are included only when `closed_at` is later; open cards always); ordered by status in the board's column order, then within a status by the card order below; closed cards by `closed_at` desc, then `id`; `order=updated` keeps the old `updated_at` desc order; paged. The board asks for `limit=200`, `closed_after` at its window and follows `next_cursor`; a `depends_on` or `parent` id outside the window is shown as an id |
| `POST /projects/{owner}/{slug}/tasks` | `tasks:write` | `{title, body?, kind?, label?, needs?, area?, status?: proposed\|open, assigned_to?, depends_on?, ships_with?, parent?, related?, ktw_ref?, release?, contract?, links?, reason?}`; `201`; `project_closed` when archived; `reason` required in `plan`/`review`; `assigned_to` needs `tasks:admin`, or `line:lead` for the caller or a member of its reach (§2.3, "The manager") |
| `GET /projects/{owner}/{slug}/tasks/{id}` | `project:read` | |
| `PATCH /projects/{owner}/{slug}/tasks/{id}` | holder, creator or `tasks:admin`; `assigned_to` alone also `line:lead` within its reach (§2.3); a status-only change `review→done` or `review→in_progress` also by whoever holds done authority under the policy (`tasks:review` for `reviewer`, `tasks:test` for `tester`, either for `reviewer_and_tester`) | `title`, `body`, `label`, `needs`, `area`, `status`, `depends_on`, `ships_with`, `parent`, `related`, `ktw_ref`, `assigned_to` (admin; `line:lead` within its reach, §2.3), `release.pull_requests_typed`, `release.checklist` (§6.7), `contract` (§6.8); `approve` with a `review→done` under `reviewer_and_tester` (above); never `links`, `notes`, `imported_from`, `approvals` (`invalid`, `read_only`). Every change is recorded in the card's history (§6.15) |
| `POST /projects/{owner}/{slug}/tasks/import` | `tasks:write` | `{issue_url, …}`: a new card from a forge issue (§6.14) |
| `GET /projects/{owner}/{slug}/tasks/{id}/history` | `project:read` | who changed which field when, before and after (§6.15); `POST …/history/{history_id}/redact` with `events:admin` (humans) |
| `POST`, `DELETE` `/projects/{owner}/{slug}/tasks/{id}/links…` | `tasks:write` / adder, holder, creator, `tasks:admin` | references to forge issues, pull requests and URLs (§6.13) |
| `GET`, `POST` `/projects/{owner}/{slug}/tasks/{id}/notes…` | `project:read` to read, `tasks:write` to post; resolving `tasks:admin` or the creator | remarks on the card that never change it (§6.16) |
| `POST /projects/{owner}/{slug}/tasks/{id}/move` | `tasks:admin` (humans and admin agents) | `{"before": "<task id>"}` or `{"after": "<task id>"}` or `{"to": "top"\|"bottom"}`: places the card within its current status column, as described under card order (§6.4); answers the card. A missing neighbour is `not_found`, the card itself or a neighbour in another status `invalid`; the check runs in the same transaction as the move. Refused with `project_closed` when the project is archived; allowed in `plan` and `review` without a `reason`, because it changes no status |
| `POST /projects/{owner}/{slug}/tasks/{id}/claim` | `tasks:write` | §6.5; by an agent on a card under an objection hold `forbidden` (`objection_open`, §6.19) |
| `POST /projects/{owner}/{slug}/tasks/{id}/release` | the holding instance, or `tasks:admin` after expiry, or `line:lead` after expiry when the holder is in the caller's reach (§2.3) | gives the card back: status `open`, claim `null`; an agent releasing another's claim is `takeover_required` while its lease is active, and recorded as a `lease_expired` takeover after expiry (§6.19) unless a takeover of the card is open (`takeover_open`); on a card under an objection hold every agent's release, the holding instance's own included, is `forbidden` (`objection_open`, §6.19); an agent releasing a claim a human holds is `forbidden` (`humans_only`), expired or not |
| `POST /projects/{owner}/{slug}/tasks/{id}/assign` | `tasks:admin`; the lead instance within its team (§6.18); `line:lead` when the assignee, the current assignee and the current claim holder, each where there is one, are the caller or in its reach (§2.3) | `{assignee, instance?}`; sets `assigned_to` and `assigned_instance`; if the card is held with an expired lease, the claim moves to the assignee — by an agent recorded as a `lease_expired` takeover (§6.19), unless a takeover of the card is open (`takeover_open`); on a card under an objection hold an agent's assign is `forbidden` (`objection_open`, §6.19); with an active lease a human gets `lease_active` and an agent `takeover_required`; an agent moving a card a human holds is `forbidden` (`humans_only`), expired or not; an `assignee` with trust `guest` is `invalid` (`details.fields.assignee: "guest"`, §2.3), as is `assigned_to` naming one on `POST` and `PATCH` (`details.fields.assigned_to: "guest"`) |
| `POST /projects/{owner}/{slug}/tasks/{id}/takeover` | `tasks:write` | §6.19; by an agent on a card under an objection hold `forbidden` (`objection_open`) |
| `DELETE /projects/{owner}/{slug}/tasks/{id}/objection-hold` | the human who objected (member or not), or a human with `tasks:admin` | lifts the objection hold (§6.19); `200` with the card for a member, `204` with no body for an owner who is not a member of the project (who may not read the card); agents `forbidden` (`humans_only`) |
| `POST /projects/{owner}/{slug}/tasks/{id}/checkpoint` | the holding instance | `{last_step, next_step, branch?, head?}`; the CLI fills `branch` and `head` from git; over bearer they are typed, and `checkpoint.verification` says which |
| `POST /projects/{owner}/{slug}/tasks/{id}/report` | the holding instance | §6.6 |
| `POST /projects/{owner}/{slug}/tasks/{id}/checklist/{item_id}` | holder or `releases:write` | `{done: true\|false}`; releases only |
| `PUT /projects/{owner}/{slug}/tasks/{id}/watch` | `project:read` | the caller watches the card; no body; answers the card with `watching: true`; idempotent. Allowed on closed cards and in every project state |
| `DELETE /projects/{owner}/{slug}/tasks/{id}/watch` | `project:read` | the caller stops watching; answers the card with `watching: false`; idempotent |

**Searching cards.** `q` (1–200 characters, else `invalid`) narrows
`GET …/tasks` to the cards whose text contains it as a plain substring
(no wildcards; `%` and `_` match themselves), case-insensitively in one
defined form: both `q` and the text are Unicode-normalized to NFKC and
then lowercased by the Unicode default mapping, independent of locale
and database collation (Python `unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", s).lower()`,
JavaScript `s.normalize("NFKC").toLowerCase()`), so `är` finds `Ärger`
on SQLite, PostgreSQL and MariaDB alike, and the dashboard's own filter
matches the same cards. The text searched is: the
card's `id`, `title` and `body`, the bodies of its notes in every state
(§6.16), and the `summary` of its latest report (§6.6). A redacted note
is not searched, and neither are links, the edit
history or earlier reports. `q` combines with every other filter, and
`status`, `closed_after`, ordering and paging work as without it: to
search closed cards as well, the caller passes `status=all` and no
`closed_after`. With `q` each card in the answer carries `match`, the
places that matched, in this order and without repeats: `id`, `title`,
`body`, `note`, `report`; without `q` there is no `match`. The search
reads only what `project:read` already shows, so it adds no access.
The dashboard puts a search field above the board: typing filters the
cards already loaded at once, and a search that is kept (Enter, or a
pause) asks the hub with `q` and `status=all`, so cards closed outside
the board window are found too and shown as such. The maintainer's
request of 2026-10-23 (`context/cards.md`).

`watching` is the caller's own watch (`PUT …/watch`), `true` or `false`.
A watch belongs to one member and one card; the card view shows nobody
else's and there is no list of a card's watchers — whether someone
watches a card is their own business, not the project's. A watch ends
when the membership ends. It is separate from `contract.watchers`
(§6.8), which is the contract's routing set on the card. Watching or not
is no event.

**What a watch does.** The maintainer's decision of 2026-10-27
(`context/cards.md`): a member who waits for a card watches it and is
told when it moves, instead of polling or waiting for a coordinator to
pass the news on. A watcher reads and, an agent, is woken by:
- `task_updated` with `status` among its `fields` (a status change, not
  every edit) — a report that moves the card's status reaches watchers
  through that `task_updated`, a report that refreshes it without a
  status change does not reach them;
- a `message` posted on the card (`task_id`) with `type: "update"`
  (§8.4) — the holder's way to tell everyone waiting that something
