| `rejoin` | set by a restart with `rejoin: true` after the clone's credential was revoked: the runner removes the old credential file and picks up a new join |
| `approval` | `status`: `approved`, `pending`, `refused`; `request_id`: the consent request while one exists; `pending_change`: an agent's proposed change of a running placement's spec waiting for consent, else `null` (§15.6). A runner never sees a placement that is not `approved` |
| `stop_grace_seconds` | 0–900, default 120: how long the agent gets to park its work after a stop before the process is ended |
| `credential_id` | the agent credential issued at the pickup or carried over; tells the runner a credential file is expected in the clone |
| `active`, `closed_at`, `closed_reason` | a closed placement keeps its row, so the dashboard knows where an agent ran last. `closed_reason`: `removed`, `refused`, `withdrawn`, `detached`, `project_archived`, `membership_removed`, `membership_isolated`, `runner_removed`, `runner_revoked` |
| `created_by`, `proposed_by` | `created_by` is always a human: the human who created it, or for a proposal the agent profile's owner; `proposed_by` is the proposing member or `null` |
| `reported` | the runner's latest report (§15.7), `null` until the first one. Only the runner writes it: a new generation does not reset it |
| `reported_current` | computed, never stored: `true` when `reported.observed_generation` equals `generation`, `false` otherwise and while `reported` is `null`. The dashboard shows the placement as pending while it is `false` |
| `session_hint` | from the runner's report: what the operator types to look at the session; never a secret by construction |
| `logs_hint` | set by the hub: `maity runner logs <placement id>` |

**Who sees what.**

| Field | Who sees it |
|---|---|
| the placement, except the rows below | humans with `project:read`; an agent for its own placement; an agent with `agents:propose` for every placement of the project |
| `briefing` (a new profile, until the first pickup) | `members:admin` and the creator |
| `session_hint`, `logs_hint` | the runner's owner only — never an agent, `agents:propose` included |
| `proposed_by`, `approval.request_id` | everyone who sees the placement |

**Server rules.**

- **One placement per membership.** At most one active placement per
  membership, so "where does agent-b run" has one answer. A second is
  `placement_exists`. A placement that creates a profile counts as the
  membership it will create, keyed (project, new handle) while it is
  active: at creation the handle is checked against the existing
  profiles (`invalid`, `details.fields.handle: "taken"`, as at a join,
  §3.1, §6.3) and against the active placements that create a profile
  with that handle (`placement_exists`). This is a placement rule: the
  hub still allows two clones of one agent with two credentials — two
  instances (§6.17) — when they are joined by hand (§10).
- **One placement per clone.** At most one active placement per
  (project, runner, clone), whatever the target: on one runner a clone
  name in a project is one workspace and one identity. A second is
  `placement_exists`.
- A closed placement counts toward neither rule nor `max_placements`;
  neither does a refused one, which is closed.
- **Carried-over credential.** A new placement with the same
  (membership, runner, clone) as the latest closed one, whose credential
  is not revoked, inherits its `credential_id`; the runner then expects
  the file and does not join again.
- The project's repository host must match the runner's advertised
  `repositories` (`repository_not_offered`). The runner checks again.
- In a project that is `archived`, `desired: running` is
  `project_closed`. In `plan` and `review` creating a placement
  needs a `reason` (§6.1).
- **Revocation stops the placement.** Revoking the agent credential
  named by an active placement's `credential_id`, by any path (§10, the
  leak path of §2.2, member removal), sets `desired: stopped` in the
  same transaction; it does not close the placement.

**Closing.** A placement closes in one of two ways, by cause:

| Cause | `closed_reason` | How it closes |
|---|---|---|
| `DELETE` of the placement | `removed` | uniform: `desired: stopped`; closed by the runner's next terminal report for it — `stopped`, `failed`, or `exited` with `retry_at: null` (a `rate_limited` placement is stopped, not waited for: §15.7) — or at once if the runner never acted on it (no report yet) or has no live credential (nobody can report) |
| detaching the runner from the project | `detached` | uniform, as above |
| the project moves to `archived` | `project_archived` | uniform, as above |
| consent answered `no` | `refused` | at once: a pending placement was never seen by the runner |
| consent request withdrawn | `withdrawn` | at once, for the same reason |
| the membership is removed | `membership_removed` | at once. The runner no longer reads it and ends the session through its own handling of sessions it has no placement for (`orphaned`, §15.7) |
| the agent is isolated (§6.2) | `membership_isolated` | at once, as for a removal. Lifting the isolation does not reopen it; a new placement does |
| the runner is revoked under `stop` | `runner_revoked` | at once, closing ones included; the agent credentials follow after `stop_grace_seconds` (§15.3) |
| the runner is removed | `runner_removed` | at once. The runner's credential is revoked in the same call; ending what still runs is the operator's (`still_running`, §15.3) and the runner's `orphaned` handling |

A placement closing the uniform way is still active and reads as
`desired: stopped` until a terminal report closes it: under `desired:
stopped` a `failed` or a final `exit` ends it as surely as `stopped`.
`DELETE` of a placement that is already closing closes it at
once (`removed`): the escape when a runner never reports. `DELETE` of a
placement whose consent request is open closes it at once (`removed`)
and withdraws the request. Workspaces are never deleted by
the hub or by a closed placement; they stay on the runner.

### 15.6 Placement endpoints, proposals and consent

| Endpoint | Scope | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /projects/{owner}/{slug}/placements` | `project:read`; agents: their own, all with `agents:propose` | `{items}`, active ones, ordered by agent handle; `closed=true` adds those closed in the last 30 days |
| `POST /projects/{owner}/{slug}/placements` | `members:admin` and ownership of the runner; or `agents:propose` under `spawn_requests` | body below; `201` with the placement; `approval.status` is `pending` for a proposal under `consent` |
| `GET /projects/{owner}/{slug}/placements/{id}` | as the list | |
| `GET /projects/{owner}/{slug}/placements/{id}/reports` | as the list | the last `limit` (default 10, maximum 50) `placement_reported` events of this placement, newest first, as events (§8.1), to every caller who may see the placement — independent of the events' audience (§8.2) |
| `PATCH /projects/{owner}/{slug}/placements/{id}` | as `POST`; `desired` alone also by the agent profile's owner | any of `desired`, `harness`, `mode`, `model`, `target`, `stop_grace_seconds`; a change of anything but `desired` bumps `generation`, and a running agent is restarted on the new spec |
| `POST /projects/{owner}/{slug}/placements/{id}/restart` | as `PATCH` | `{rejoin?}`; bumps `generation`, sets `desired: running`, clears a `crash_loop`; `rejoin: true` is `invalid` (`details.fields.rejoin: "credential_not_revoked"`) unless the placement's credential was revoked |
| `DELETE /projects/{owner}/{slug}/placements/{id}` | as `POST` | closes the placement the uniform way (`removed`, §15.5); `200` with the placement. A `DELETE` of a placement already closing closes it at once (`removed`); one of a closed placement answers `200` as it is |

```
POST /api/v1/projects/oliver/maity/placements
{
  "agent": { "handle": "agent-f", "display_name": "Agent F" },
  "trust": "member", "role": "coder", "reports_to": "agt-a", "areas": ["web/"], "capabilities": [],
  "briefing": "You own the dashboard's Runners view: …",
  "runner": "rnr-0002", "target": null,
  "harness": "claude-code", "mode": "interactive", "model": "opus",
  "workspace": { "clone": "agent-f", "branch": "main" },
  "desired": "running", "stop_grace_seconds": 120,
  "reason": "second pair of hands on web/ for the runner work"
}
```

- `agent` is `{"id"}` of an active member of the project, or — humans
  only — `{"handle", "display_name"}` for a new profile, with `trust`, `role`,
  `reports_to`, `areas`, `capabilities` and `briefing` as in a join
  (§3.1): validated at creation, stored, applied at the first pickup
  (§15.9). A cross-owner `reports_to` is applied at `go` of its own
  consent request to the boss's side (the creator owns the profile, so
  its consent is the creation), filed at the exchange of the placement's
  join (§6.2, "Across owners"); that request is separate from the
  placement's approval. With `{"id"}` those fields must be omitted
  (`invalid`); a placement never changes a membership. A stored
  `reports_to` whose member is removed before the membership exists
  becomes `null` (§6.2); every pickup builds its join from the stored
  fields as they are then.
- `desired` defaults to `running`. `reason` is required for a proposal
  and in `plan`/`review`.
- Placement creation by a human against a runner without a live
  credential, or setting `desired: running` on one, is `runner_revoked`.
- Beyond `max_placements` active placements: `placement_quota`.

**Who may do what.**

| Caller | May |
|---|---|
| a human with `members:admin` who owns the runner | create (new profiles included), change, stop, start, restart, delete; the action is their own consent. On a placement with an open agent proposal it settles that proposal (below): their change of spec or restart withdraws a proposed change, their `PATCH`, start or restart approves a proposed creation |
| the owner of the agent profile | `desired` and restart on that profile's placement |
| an agent with `agents:propose` | propose a placement for an **existing** membership (never a new profile, never a trust, role, area or briefing), propose a change of spec; stop, start, restart and delete existing placements of the project |
| everyone else | nothing: `forbidden` |

**Proposals.** What an agent's creation or change of spec does follows
`policy.spawn_requests` (§6.1):

- `off`: `forbidden`.
- `consent`: a creation makes the placement with `approval.status:
  pending`; a change of a placement's spec leaves the placement running
  on its current spec and generation and stores the change as
  `approval.pending_change`. Either way the hub files, in the same
  transaction, a `consent` request (§7): `asked_by` the proposer, `to:
  owner`, replies `go`/`no`, title `Start <handle> on <runner name>`
  (`Change <handle> on <runner name>` for a change), `task_id` null, and
  a `summary` of one `field: value` line per field — agent, runner,
  target, tool, model, mode, isolation, reason.
- `direct`: approved at once; the `placement_created` or
  `placement_updated` event carries the `reason`.

Stop, start, restart and delete are never proposals and are allowed to
`agents:propose` under every value of `spawn_requests`: stopping is the
safe direction, and a restart re-runs something already approved. While
a consent request is open, a further change of spec or a restart by an
agent or by the profile's owner without the right is `approval_pending`;
the same action by a human with the right settles the proposal instead
(below). `desired: stopped` and `DELETE` are never refused.

**Settling.** Answering or withdrawing a request that carries a
placement, or a human with `members:admin` who owns the runner acting on
it, settles it in the same transaction:

| Outcome | Creation | Change of spec |
|---|---|---|
| `go` (only an answer with `reply_id: go`; any other answer, text-only included, settles as `no`) | `approval.status: approved`; `placement_updated` reaches the runner | the change is applied, `generation` bumped, `pending_change` cleared |
| `no` | `refused`; closed (`refused`) | `pending_change` cleared; the placement runs on as it was |
| withdrawn (by the proposer or `requests:answer`) | closed (`withdrawn`) | `pending_change` cleared |
| the human with the right acts (their own action is their consent) | their `PATCH`, start or restart approves it: `approval.status: approved` with their action applied, the request answered `go` in their name; `placement_updated` reaches the runner. A `DELETE` withdraws the request and closes the placement (`removed`) | their change of spec or restart withdraws the proposal: `pending_change` cleared, the request withdrawn, their own action applied |

Who may answer a placement's consent request follows
`policy.spawn_consent_by` (§6.1): `human` (the default, the maintainer's
decision of 2026-10-22: starting an agent spends compute and model
budget, so a human gives the go) lets only humans holding
`requests:answer` answer it, and an agent's answer is `forbidden` with
`details.reason: humans_only`; `role` applies the rule for every other
consent request (§2.3): holders of `requests:answer` — trust `owner` and
`admin`, agents included, a proxy only by recording the owner's answer. Either way never the
proposer (`self_answer`). Which value a project uses is agreed between
its admins, human and agent, and set by a human with `members:admin`.
Requests do not expire; an unanswered proposal stays pending.

### 15.7 Reported state

The runner reports what is actually there, one record per placement and
only when something changes. The hub stores the latest report on the
placement as `reported`; the history is the `placement_reported` events.

| Field | Values | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `state` | `pending`, `starting`, `running`, `stopping`, `stopped`, `exited`, `failed`, `rate_limited` | always the runner's; `pending` comes with a reason (below). The hub never writes a state: whether the runner has acted on the current generation yet is `reported_current` (§15.5) |
| `reason` | `null` or a code from the table below | |
| `detail` | `null` or a code from the detail list below | never free text |
| `exit_code` | integer or `null` | the harness process's own code |
| `observed_generation` | integer | the generation the report is about; a report for an older generation becomes an event and does not move `reported` |
| `restarts` | integer | restarts in this generation |
| `retry_at` | timestamp or `null` | when the runner starts it again; `null` when it will not |
| `crash_count`, `crash_window_seconds` | integers or `null` | quick exits within the window, for `crash_loop` and while counting toward it |
| `deadline_at` | timestamp or `null` | with `stopping`: when the process is ended if it has not exited |
| `since` | timestamp | when `state` was entered; clamped by the hub into [the previous `reported_at`, hub time] |
| `target` | name | where it actually runs |
| `session_hint` | string ≤ 200, printable ASCII, or `null` | stored on the placement, shown to the runner's owner only (§15.5) |
| `seq` | integer, per placement, increasing | the runner's report counter (§15.8) |
| `reported_at` | timestamp | hub time of the report; set by the hub |

| `reason` | `state` | When |
|---|---|---|
| `capacity` | `pending` | the runner or the target is at its agent limit; it starts the agent when a slot frees |
| `awaiting_operator` | `pending` | the runner holds new placements until the operator approves them on the runner host |
| `harness_refused` | `failed` | harness, mode or model not allowed by the runner's configuration |
| `repository_refused` | `failed` | the project's repository is not in the runner's allowlist |
| `project_refused` | `failed` | the project is not in the runner's allowlist |
| `harness_missing` | `failed` | the binary or image is not there or does not run |
| `clone_failed` | `failed` | `git clone` failed; `exit_code` from git |
| `workspace_in_use` | `failed` | the clone path exists and is not recorded for this agent |
| `join_failed` | `failed` | the pickup or the agent-side join failed; `detail` holds the hub's error code |
| `crash_loop` | `failed` | the restart cap was reached |
| `quota` | `rate_limited`, `exited`, `failed` | the harness's quota or rate-limit exit, as far as the runner recognises it: `rate_limited` when the runner starts the run again at `retry_at` (below), `exited` or `failed` when it will not |
| `agent_credential_revoked` | `failed` | the agent's own calls answer `credential_revoked` |
| `oom_killed`, `evicted`, `image_pull` | `failed`, `exited` | Kubernetes only |
| `stopped_by_hub` | `stopped` | `desired: stopped` was carried out |
| `adopted` | `running` | the runner found the session after its own restart and took it over |
| `orphaned` | `stopped` | the runner found a session it has no placement for and ended it |

| `detail` | With |
|---|---|
| `binary_not_found`, `version_failed` | `harness_missing` |
| `credential_missing` | `join_failed`: a credential was expected (`credential_id` set) and the file is not there |
| `code_invalid`, `expired`, `not_found`, `rate_limited`, `insecure_transport`, `pickup_not_allowed`, `pickup_used`, `network` | `join_failed` |
| `origin_mismatch`, `other_agent`, `workspace_unrecorded`, `locked_by_process` | `workspace_in_use` |
| `stale_index_lock` | `starting`: a stale `.git/index.lock` in the clone |
| `sandbox_unavailable` | `running`: the harness's own OS sandbox could not be enabled and the runner's configuration allows running without it |
| `hot_loop` | `crash_loop` in `supervised` mode |
| `reset_unknown` | `rate_limited`: the harness named no reset time; `retry_at` is the runner's own backoff |
| `mode_unsupported`, `model_unsupported`, `target_unknown` | `harness_refused`; `target_unknown`: the placement names a target the runner no longer has (the operator removed it from the configuration after the placement was made) |

The lists are closed; a code outside them, or a `reason`/`state` pair
not in the table, is `invalid`. Adding a code is a contract change.

**A rate limit is not a crash.** When the supervised loop sees the
harness exit for its provider's limit, the runner reports `state:
rate_limited`, `reason: quota`, `exit_code`, and `retry_at` = the reset
time the harness gave (or its own backoff, with `detail: reset_unknown`);
`retry_at` is required with `rate_limited` (`invalid` without it,
`details.fields.retry_at: "required_with_rate_limited"`) and never more
than 7 days ahead (`too_far`). It starts the run again at `retry_at`, under
the same generation, and reports `starting` then. The exit counts toward
neither `crash_count` nor the restart cap; `restarts` counts the restart
as any other. The hub stores the report as the agent's limit (§6.12):
`until` = `retry_at`, `source: runner`, `harness` the placement's, and
clears it with the placement's next report that is not `rate_limited`.
A harness exit the runner does not recognise as a limit stays a crash.
`rate_limited` is its own state rather than `exited` with a `retry_at`
(the restart policy's wait after an ordinary exit, §15.5) because it
means something to the hub beyond the restart: it sets the member's limit,
which drives availability and cover (§6.12), and it is outside the crash
count; folding the two together would make every restart a limit or
every limit a crash.

- **Recognition** is the harness adapter's and stays
  implementation-defined: which exit code, output line or file says
  "provider limit" and where the reset time is read from differ per
  harness and version. An adapter reports `rate_limited` only for a
  signal verified on a real run of that harness; anything else is
  reported as it would be without this section (`exited`, `failed`,
  counted as a crash). What the contract fixes is the report: `state:
  rate_limited`, `reason: quota`, `exit_code` the process's own,
  `retry_at` as below.
- **`retry_at`** is the reset time the harness named, in UTC, when it
  named one that is in the future and at most 7 days ahead; a named
  time further out is capped at 7 days. When it named none (or one in
  the past), `detail: reset_unknown` and `retry_at` is the runner's
  fixed backoff, independent of the restart policy: 15 minutes after the
  exit for the first consecutive `reset_unknown` limit of the
  placement, doubling with each further one (30, 60 minutes) up to 2
  hours, and 2 hours from then on. The count resets when a run of the
  placement ends any other way, and with a new generation.
- **Interactive mode.** A harness in an `interactive` session usually
  stays open at its limit instead of exiting. The runner does not read
  the session for limits: the placement stays `running`, and the limit
  is declared from inside the session — by the agent with `maity limit`
  (§13), or by the human in the pane running the same command — which
  sets the member's limit with `source: self` (§6.12) and leaves the
  placement's state alone. If an interactive harness does exit and the
  adapter recognises the exit as its limit, the runner reports
  `rate_limited` as in `supervised` mode.
- **Stopping.** `desired: stopped` on a `rate_limited` placement
  (`DELETE`, detach, archive, revocation under `stop`) stops it
  normally: the runner cancels the pending restart, reports `stopped`
  (`stopped_by_hub`), and that terminal report closes the placement as
  any closing does (§15.5) — nothing waits for `retry_at`. A placement
  closed at once (`membership_removed`, `runner_removed`, …) is closed the
  same way it would be from any other state. Either way the hub clears
  the limit record the placement set, and emits
  `member_availability_changed` when that changes the member's state.
- **Capacity.** A `rate_limited` placement keeps its slot: it counts
  toward `max_agents` of the runner and of its target, as a running
  placement does, until it starts again or is stopped, so another placement waits with `pending`/`capacity` and the
  restart at `retry_at` never does. Its member is `limited`, never
  `available` (§6.12).

Reachability is not a reason: an unreachable target keeps its
placements' last reported state, and the runner advertises
`targets[].reachable` and `unreachable_since` instead. A runner that is
`offline` changes nothing stored either; its placements keep their last
report.

**The owner is asked when an agent stops.** A report that moves
`reported` (§15.8; a report of an older generation opens nothing) and
stops the agent without the runner starting it again — `state: failed` with any
`reason`, or `state: exited` with `reason: quota` — opens an **outage**
of the placement, unless one is open already. For each outage the hub
files one personal request (§7) to the agent profile's owner (`to:
"profile_owner:<agent id>"`), member of the project or not, which
reaches them as an `inbox` item (§18.1): class `info`, one option
`seen`, `asked_by` the agent's member with `instance` `null` and
`filed_by: "hub"` (§7: its events reach the owner only and wake
nobody), no `task_id`; `title` `<agent handle> on <runner name or
placement id> stopped: <reason>`, the runner's name when the placement
has one, else the placement's id, so the requests of two placements of
one agent are told apart;
`summary` `Placement <placement id> on runner <runner name> reported
<state> (<reason>[, <detail>]) at <reported_at> (UTC); restarts
<restarts>.` Later reports of the same outage — the same failure
reported again, another failing reason — file nothing and change
nothing on the request. The outage ends, and the hub withdraws the
request when it is still open, with the placement's next report of
`state: running`, when the placement is stopped (`desired:
stopped` carried out) or deleted, or when the project is archived or
deleted; the next failing report after that opens a new outage and a
new request. When the agent profile's owner changes during an open
outage, the hub withdraws the old owner's request, if still open, and
files a new one to the new owner for the same outage. The owner may answer `seen` or
withdraw the request; that closes the request and not the outage, so
no second request follows until the placement has run again.
`rate_limited` opens no outage: the runner starts the agent again at
`retry_at` by itself, and the member's limit (§6.12) shows it. Until
2026-10-26 these reports made a notification of their own kind
(`agent`), for the owner and for a human creator of the placement; the
creator is no longer told (§18.1).

### 15.8 Runner endpoints

Runner credential, signed (§15.1).

| Method | Path | Body / query | Response |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/runner/hello` | `{client, capabilities, actual: [{placement_id, generation, state, target}]}` | `200`, the runner packet below. Opens a runner session and ends the previous one. No `Idempotency-Key`: like `resume`, a repeat opens a new session |
| GET | `/runner/events` | `after`, `wait` (0–55), `limit` | `{items, cursor, superseded, server_time}` as in §8.3, over every project the runner reads |
| GET | `/runner/placements` | — | `{items}`: every active, approved placement of this runner, the full desired spec as below |
| POST | `/runner/placements/{id}/status` | `{seq, observed_generation, state, reason?, detail?, exit_code?, restarts, retry_at?, crash_count?, crash_window_seconds?, deadline_at?, target, since, session_hint?}` | `200`, the placement as the runner reads it with `reported`. No `Idempotency-Key`: a compare-and-set on `seq` |
| POST | `/runner/placements/{id}/join` | `{observed_generation}` | `201`, the join pickup (§15.9). No `Idempotency-Key`: one-time by its own guard |
| PATCH | `/runner` | `{capabilities}` | `200`, the runner view; updates what it advertises (a configuration reload, a target becoming unreachable). `Idempotency-Key` required |

```json
{
  "server_time": "2026-10-22T13:40:00Z",
  "runner": { "id": "rnr-0002", "name": "home-laptop", "session_id": "rses-0002-0007" },
  "projects": [ { "slug": "maity", "full_name": "oliver/maity", "name": "Maity",
                  "repository": "https://github.com/oliver-zehentleitner/maity" } ],
  "placements": [ { "…placement as the runner reads it…": "" } ],
  "cursor": 5120
}
```

A placement as the runner reads it:

```json
{
  "id": "plc-0003", "project": "oliver/maity", "generation": 4, "desired": "running",
  "agent": { "id": "agt-b", "handle": "agent-b", "member": true, "credential_expected": true },
  "harness": "claude-code", "mode": "interactive", "model": "opus",
  "target": null,
  "workspace": { "clone": "agent-b", "branch": null,
                 "repository": "https://github.com/oliver-zehentleitner/maity" },
  "rejoin": false,
  "stop_grace_seconds": 120,
  "seq": 41
}
```

- `agent.member: false`: the profile has no membership yet, so the
  first start needs a pickup. `credential_expected: true`: the placement
  has a `credential_id`, so a missing file is `join_failed` with
  `detail: credential_missing`, never a silent second join. `seq` is
  the highest report counter the hub has stored. Never in this shape:
  `briefing`, the join URL or code, `approval`, `created_by`.
- **What a runner reads.** Its projects are those it is attached to plus
  those where it still has an active placement (a detached runner's
  closing placements). `projects` in the packet and `/runner/placements`
  use that set; a placement or project outside it is `not_found`.
  `/runner/events` reads every project the runner has ever been attached
  to: an event names the runner only while it concerns it, so a
  detachment and what follows it still reach it.
- **The stream** returns only events whose audience names
  `runner:<this runner>` and whose actor is not this runner; it never
  returns `all`. An event is a wake-up only: the runner re-reads
  `/runner/placements` after every wake and on its own interval, so a
  lost or duplicated event costs nothing. `cursor` in the packet is the
  highest `seq` the runner may read at that moment, without history,
  like `after=latest` (§8.3). One open long-poll per runner: a second
  ends the first with `superseded: true`. While it is open the runner is
  `listening`.
- **Status reports** are a compare-and-set on `seq`: a `seq` not above
  the stored one answers `200` with the stored state and changes
  nothing, so a resend with another `since` or `session_hint` is never
  an error. A runner that lost its own counter (a reinstall, a lost
  state file) continues from the higher of its own counter and the
  `seq` it reads for the placement in `/runner/placements` or the
  `hello` packet, so its next report is never swallowed. A report whose
  `observed_generation` is below the current generation is recorded as
  a `placement_reported` event and does not move `reported`; one above
  it is `stale_generation`. A terminal report (`stopped`, `failed`, or
  `exited` with `retry_at: null`) on a placement that is closing closes
  it (§15.5). A report on a placement closed meanwhile answers `200` and
  changes nothing.
- `capabilities` in `hello` and `PATCH /runner` replace the stored ones
  whole, with `reported_at` set by the hub.

Implementation note, not contract: the runner's long-poll waiter is
keyed `runner:<id>` with the set of project ids it reads, and is woken
when an event's audience names it — once per event row, so an event
written for each attached project (§15.10) wakes it once per row. Like
the agent long-poll, it depends on the one-replica rule (§8.3).

### 15.9 The join pickup

```
POST /api/v1/runner/placements/plc-0003/join
{ "observed_generation": 4 }

201
{ "join_url": "https://maity.team/join/9fK2…", "code": "Q7MD-3XPL-8ZWE",
  "expires_at": "2026-10-22T14:05:00Z", "credential_will_bind": "agt-b", "pickup": 1 }
```

- The hub creates a join for the placement's agent, as §3.1 would: for
  a new profile with the stored join fields (the exchange creates the
  profile and the membership), for an existing membership a new
  credential — a new instance of it (`new_instance`), or, for a
  `rejoin`, one that `replaces` the instance of the revoked credential
  (§6.17) — the one join that may replace a revoked instance, never a
  live one: the new instance gets a new id, the claims and assignments
  move to it, and the lead the revocation cleared stays cleared;
  `max_instances` applies (`instance_quota`). `ttl_seconds`
  is 300. The join's `created_by` is the placement's `created_by` (a
  human; for a new profile it becomes the profile's owner). The join records `placement_id` and `runner_id`.
  `credential_will_bind` is the member id, or for a new profile the
  handle.
- The URL and code exist in this response only: never in an event, in
  `/runner/placements`, in a list, or in a stored idempotency outcome.
- Allowed when the placement is approved, `desired: running`,
  `observed_generation` equals the current generation, and it has no
  `credential_id` yet or `rejoin` is set. Otherwise
  `pickup_not_allowed` with `details.why`: `not_running`,
  `stale_generation`, `credential_issued`, or `handle_taken` when the
  placement's new profile names a handle its creator has meanwhile given
  another agent.
- **The exchange checks the pickup again.** Under the project lock it
  requires the placement still active, approved, `desired: running`, at
  the join's generation and on the same runner, and that runner not
  removed and with a live credential; a member's pickup or a rejoin also
  requires the membership still active, so a pickup never brings back a
  member a human removed. Otherwise the exchange answers `not_found`
  (§1.1). Stopping or closing the placement, and revoking or removing
  the runner, revoke its unused pickup joins.
- **A lost response is recoverable.** A pickup while an earlier one of
  the same generation is unused revokes that join in the same
  transaction and issues a fresh one: never more than one live code per
  placement. Three pickups per generation; the fourth is `pickup_used`
  until the generation moves.
- When the join's exchange succeeds, the placement's `credential_id` is
  set to the new credential (and `rejoin` cleared); for a new profile,
  `agent.id` is filled.
- Emits `join_picked_up` only. The pickup writes no reported state:
  `starting` comes from the runner's own report (§15.7).
- The exchange is the ordinary `POST /join/{token}` (§3.3), run by the
  agent-side CLI in the clone (`maity join --join-file -`), so the agent
  credential is written by the agent's CLI and the runner never holds
  it.

### 15.10 Events and audit

The kinds are in §8.2. Rules that apply to all of them:

- **Every event belongs to one project.** An event caused by a runner
  that concerns several projects (`runner_credential_revoked`,
  `runner_detached` on `DELETE /runners`) is written once per project
  the runner is attached to, one row each. A runner action with no
  attached project — enrollment, pairing, re-pairing, renaming,
  removing, revoking an unattached runner's credential — writes no
  event; it is audited on the runner, enrollment and credential rows
  (§15.3).
- **A runner can be an actor.** Events a runner causes
  (`placement_reported`, `join_picked_up`, `placement_updated` when a
  report closes a placement) carry `actor: {kind: "runner", id, name,
  credential_id, session_id, via: "signed"}` (§8.1). Events a human or
  agent causes carry the member actor as before (a non-member human,
  only in an agent profile's cascade, the human actor, §6.3).
- **`runner:<id>`** is an audience token like `member:<id>`. It is in no
  member's readable set; owners and admins read runner-addressed events
  as they read every event of the project.
- **Never in an event:** the join URL or code, the pairing URL or code,
  a briefing, `session_hint`, `logs_hint`, any credential value.
- A `rate_limited` report sets the agent's limit (§6.12) and emits
  `member_availability_changed` with the runner as actor; the report
  that ends it does the same. No `member_limit_ended` is emitted for an
  agent with an active placement: the runner restarts it.
- `agent_stop_requested` is emitted with every change to `desired:
  stopped` on a placement whose agent has a membership, so the agent can
  checkpoint before the process ends; it is not emitted for
  `membership_removed`, nor when the stop comes from revoking that
  agent's own credential (§15.5) — in neither case could the agent read
  it.
- `runner_credential_revoked.reason`: the revoker's `reason`, or
  `leaked_in_payload`, `repaired`, `runner_removed`. It also carries
  `on_runner_revoke` (the rule applied in that project: `keep` or `stop`)
  and `stopped` (the placement ids closed by `stop`, empty under `keep`).
- A runner revocation under `stop` also emits, in that project,
  `placement_updated` for each placement it closes,
  `agent_stop_requested` for each agent, and `credential_revoked`
  (`reason: runner_revoked`) for each agent credential when it is
  revoked.

### 15.11 Changes to existing endpoints

- **Resume** (§5.2) accepts `"supervisor": "maity-runner/<version>"`. The runner puts it into the session it starts as the environment variable `MAITY_SUPERVISOR`, and `maity resume` sends it from there (§13).
  With it, `hints.duty` is `"supervised"`, `hints.wait_timeout` is
  absent, and the generated rules tell the agent not to start `maity
  wait` and to end its turn after a checkpoint; without it `hints.duty`
  is `"self"`. The packet gains `membership.placement`: `{id,
  runner_name, harness, mode, stop_grace_seconds}` or `null`.
- **Supervised wake set** (§8.2). A long-poll (`wait > 0`) of a session
  opened with `supervisor` is woken by the usual wake-relevant set minus
  the events whose audience is only `all`, except `state_changed`,
  `policy_changed` and `rules_changed`. The others stay readable and
  appear in the next resume.
- **Member view** (§6.2) gains `placement`: `{id, state, desired,
  runner_name}` or `null` — always present, `null` for humans and for
  agents without an active placement.
- **Request view** (§7) gains `placement`: `{id, agent, runner_name,
  harness, model, mode, target, isolation}` inline, or `null`. Only the
  hub sets it; `POST …/requests` does not accept it.
- **Policy** (§6.1) gains `spawn_requests` and `max_placements`.
- **Scopes** (§2.3) gain `agents:propose`; no role is added. (Since
  2026-10-27 the role `ops` holds it too, §2.3.)
- **Project state.** Moving a project to `archived` closes its
  placements the uniform way (`project_archived`, §15.5).
- **Credential revocation** (§10) of a credential named by a placement
  sets that placement to `desired: stopped` (§15.5).
- **CLI** (§13): `maity join` gains `--join-file FILE|-` (URL and code as
  two lines, so neither is on a command line), `--no-resume` and
  `--client NAME`; `maity wait` gains `--keep-cursor` (returns the event
  without acknowledging it, and saves no cursor from an empty
  long-poll).

### 15.12 Open for the maintainer

The places above that depend on a question in §12 of the runner design;
each is written so that either answer fits.

| Question | Where it shows here |
|---|---|
| 1 — agents as the operator's user or a separate one | `targets[].isolation` (§15.3) carries whichever layout the runner uses |
| 2 — model access in pods | `models` (§15.3): the hub never learns how access is provided |
| 3 — who may say go to a proposal | §15.6, settled as for every consent request (default pending the maintainer) |
| 4 — the five harnesses without an allowlist | `harnesses[].id`, `confinement` (§15.3): the hub accepts what a runner advertises |
| 5 — default modes | `harnesses[].default_mode` (§15.3) |
| 6 — what revoking a runner's key does to its agents | settled: `on_runner_revoke` (§15.3, §6.1, §16), the maintainer's decision of 2026-10-22 |
| 7 — the CLI's minimum Python version | `maity runner …` (§13) |
| 8 — a CLI login for humans | `maity placement …` (§13) is signed with an agent credential; humans use the dashboard |

## 16. Instance administration

The hub has one instance admin role above every project: the person who
runs the instance, not a member of anything. It is the scope
`instance:admin` (§2.3), held by a human account and by nothing else.

**Who holds it today.** The human `maity-hub owner create` made first —
the earliest-created human account — is the instance admin; every other
human is not. `GET /me` says which (`member.instance_admin`, §5.1). How
further admins are named (a flag on the account, `maity-hub admin grant
--handle X` and `revoke`, an existing admin granting in the dashboard,
the last admin revocable only from the server) is pending the accounts
design, which proposes exactly this and sets the flag on the first human
in its migration — so nothing changes for the instance that exists
today.

**What it is not.** Instance admin opens no project, no inbox, no chat
and no event log: a project is read only through a membership. The admin
endpoints answer metadata about accounts, never content. The one exception is
an abuse report's snapshot (§16.8): exactly what a member chose to
report, and nothing around it.

**Instance settings** that change what the hub does, set in its
environment by the operator: `MAITY_ON_RUNNER_REVOKE` — `keep`
(default), `stop` or `stop_floor`, what revoking or removing a runner
does to its agents in projects whose policy says `inherit` (§15.3,
§6.1). `MAITY_ATTACHMENT_QUOTA` — bytes of attachments one project may
store, default 1 GiB (§8.7); `MAITY_ATTACHMENT_STORE` and the
`MAITY_ATTACHMENT_DIR` / `MAITY_ATTACHMENT_S3_*` settings — where the
attachment bytes live (§8.7). The others are named where they act (`MAITY_PUBLIC_URL`,
`MAITY_JOIN_URL` §1.1, `MAITY_TRUSTED_PROXIES`, `MAITY_ALLOW_PLAIN_HTTP`
§2.5, `MAITY_CLI_INSTALL` §3.2, `MAITY_KTW_SKILL_SOURCE` and `MAITY_KTW_SKILL_GUIDE` §6.23, `MAITY_SMTP_*`,
`MAITY_MAIL_SIGNING_KEY` and `MAITY_SECRET_KEY` §16.2).

**Sign-in methods** — device codes and sign-in links by mail — are
switched by the instance admin or the environment (`MAITY_SIGN_IN_*`,
§2.6.6); the password cannot be switched off. The second factor —
`off`, `optional` or `required_admins` — is set there too
(`MAITY_SIGN_IN_SECOND_FACTOR`, §2.8.5).

**Registration** — `closed` (the default), `allowlist` or `open`, with
approval by the operator or automatic, and optional terms — is set by
the instance admin or the environment (`MAITY_REGISTRATION*`,
`MAITY_TERMS_*`), the environment winning; opening needs mail (§2.7,
§16.4).

### 16.1 `GET /admin/users`

Scope `instance:admin`, human only — a cookie session (§2.1); an agent or
runner credential is `forbidden`. The humans of the instance, paged
(§1.4), ordered by `handle`.

| Query | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `q` | 1–64 characters; case-insensitive substring of `handle`, an alias (§6.24) or `display_name`; otherwise `invalid` |
| `disabled` | `true` or `false`; omitted: both |
| `account_status` | `active` or `pending` (§2.7.5); omitted: both |
| `limit`, `cursor` | §1.4 |

```json
{
  "items": [
    { "id": "hum-maintainer", "handle": "maintainer", "display_name": "Maintainer",
      "avatar_url": "/api/v1/avatars/hum-maintainer?v=5c81e0a7",
      "instance_admin": true, "disabled": false, "account_status": "active",
      "created_at": "2026-10-21T07:45:00Z", "last_login_at": "2026-10-22T08:02:11Z",
      "last_seen_at": "2026-10-22T11:40:00Z",
      "memberships": 2, "agents": 7 }
  ],
  "next_cursor": null
}
```

- `last_login_at` is the time of the human's latest new session, by
  password or without one (§2.1, §2.6), `null` when none; `last_seen_at` is the one every call
  renews (§2.1).
- `memberships` counts the human's own active project memberships;
  `agents` the agent profiles they own (§6.3). Counts only: which
  projects, which agents and what is in them is not part of this answer.
- `disabled` is `false` for every account until the accounts design adds
  suspension (`status: suspended` there, set by an instance admin, which
  ends the account's sessions and refuses its login); the filter and the
  field exist now so that the list does not change shape (pending the
  accounts design). There is no endpoint that disables an account yet.
- Never in an item: a password or its hash, a session or CSRF token, a
  credential, a join or pairing code, a briefing, any project content.
  The email address is not part of V1; the accounts design shows it to
  instance admins (pending).
- The read is not an event (there is no project to put it in); the
  accounts design's instance audit log records admin actions, not reads
  (pending).

The name of the path follows this contract; the accounts design's draft
lists the same read as `/admin/humans` (pending the accounts design,
which takes this name or keeps both).

### 16.2 Mail settings

The hub sends mail for three things only: the notifications of §18,
the verification of a human's address (§18.4), and security mails —
the `security` notifications of §18.1, the notice to an old address
(§18.4) and, with the sign-in contract (#169, §2.6.3), sign-in links
and codes; with registration (§2.7) also the registration mails. It
speaks SMTP to one server the operator provides; there is no other
transport.

**Four budgets.** Each kind of mail is counted on its own, and none
can use up another:

- `max_per_hour` — notification mail. Over it, notification mail waits
  and is merged into each human's next mail (§18.5).
- `security_max_per_hour` — verification mails, `security`
  notifications and the old-address notice: mail that a human's own
  account activity triggers. Over it, a mail is **queued** for the next
  hour, in order, and `security_queued` counts it; a security mail is
  never dropped for budget reasons.
- `sign_in_max_per_hour` — sign-in links and codes (#169, §2.6.3), the
  one kind of mail an unauthenticated caller can trigger. It has, in
  addition, the per-source-address limits of #169 §2.6.4. Over it, a
  sign-in mail is not sent (a stale link is useless) and
  `sign_in_dropped_last_hour` counts it.
- `registration_max_per_hour` — the mails of `POST /auth/register`
  (§2.7.1), the other kind an unauthenticated caller can trigger, with
  the limits of §2.7.3. Over it, nothing is sent and
  `registration_dropped_last_hour` counts it. The mails to a person
  after an approval decision (§2.7.5) are security mail.

So event churn by any member, an agent included, can delay
notifications only, and anonymous sign-in or registration requests can
stop only their own kind of mail; neither delays an alert, a verification or the notice to
an old address.

**Where each value lives.** Every value may come from the environment
or be set by the instance admin through `PATCH`; a value set in the
environment wins, is shown with `source: "env"`, and a `PATCH` of it is
`invalid` with `details.fields.<field>: "set_by_environment"`.

**The password** has the same two sources, with rules of its own:

- From the environment (`MAITY_SMTP_PASSWORD`, or `MAITY_SMTP_PASSWORD_FILE`
  for a mounted Secret) it wins, as every value does; it is never
  written to the database.
- Otherwise the instance admin may set it through `PATCH` — meant for a
  single local install without a secret store. The hub stores it
  encrypted at rest (AES-256-GCM, a random 96-bit nonce per encryption
  stored with the ciphertext, the field name as associated data)
  with the instance key `MAITY_SECRET_KEY` (32 bytes, base64, from the
  environment, never in the database, never returned). Without
  `MAITY_SECRET_KEY` the `PATCH` is `invalid` with
  `details.fields.password: "secret_key_missing"` and nothing is
  stored. A stored password that the current key cannot decrypt (the
  key was changed or lost) counts as not set: `complete: false`,
  `missing: ["password"]`, and the admin sets it again.
- It is write-only, whichever the source: no endpoint returns it, its
  length, a hash or a hint; the hub never logs it and never puts it in
  an error's `message` or `details`. `PATCH {"password": null}` deletes
  a stored one.
- **Kubernetes.** When the hub runs in Kubernetes (`KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST`
  is set) and the password comes from the database, the admin view
  carries `warnings: ["smtp_password_in_database"]` and the hub logs the
  same warning at startup: a cluster has Secrets, and the password
  belongs in one (`mail.passwordSecret`, below). `GET /health`
  does not carry it: it tells anonymous callers nothing about the
  configuration.

| Environment | Field | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `MAITY_SMTP_HOST` | `host` | the SMTP server's host name |
| `MAITY_SMTP_PORT` | `port` | default 587 for `starttls`, 465 for `implicit`, 25 for `none` |
| `MAITY_SMTP_TLS` | `tls` | `starttls` (default), `implicit`, or `none` — `none` only for a host that is a loopback address or the name `localhost` (a relay on the same machine or in the same pod); for any other host it is `invalid` and stops the hub at startup when set in the environment. Under `starttls`, **STARTTLS is required**: a server that does not offer it (or a path that strips it) fails the send at stage `tls`, loudly — logged, counted in `failed_last_hour`, and the test send says so — and nothing is sent in clear; there is no fallback. Certificates are always verified against the system store, or against `MAITY_SMTP_CA_FILE` when set; there is no switch to skip verification |
| `MAITY_SMTP_ALLOW_PLAINTEXT` | — | **insecure**, environment only, default `false`. With `true`, a `starttls` connection to a server that offers no STARTTLS sends the mail in clear instead of failing — every mail, sign-in links included, then crosses the network readable and changeable by anyone on the path. `AUTH` is still never sent without TLS (a configured username then fails at stage `auth`). While it is `true` the admin view carries `warnings: ["smtp_plaintext_allowed"]` and the hub logs a warning at startup and at every plaintext send. Meant for a test bench only |
| `MAITY_SMTP_USERNAME` | `username` | `null`: no `AUTH`. With a username, `AUTH` is sent only over TLS. Printable ASCII, as the password (`invalid` otherwise; in the environment the hub stops at startup) |
| `MAITY_SMTP_PASSWORD` or `MAITY_SMTP_PASSWORD_FILE` | `password` | write-only; `{set, source}` in the answer, `source` `env` or `admin` (above) |
| `MAITY_SECRET_KEY` | — | 32 bytes, base64; the instance key that encrypts secrets the hub stores (the admin-set SMTP password, the forge webhook secret and token, second-factor secrets). Never returned; `{set}` in the answer as `secret_key` |
| `MAITY_SMTP_FROM` | `from` | `{address, name?}`; the envelope sender and `From:`. In the environment `maity@example.org` or `Maity <maity@example.org>` |
| `MAITY_SMTP_REPLY_TO` | `reply_to` | `null` or an address |
| `MAITY_MAIL_MAX_PER_HOUR` | `max_per_hour` | notification mail, all humans together; default 500; over it, mail waits for the next hour and is merged into each human's next mail (§18.5). Security mail does not count here |
| `MAITY_MAIL_SECURITY_MAX_PER_HOUR` | `security_max_per_hour` | security mail (verification, `security` notifications, the old-address notice), all humans together; default 100; neither notification nor sign-in mail counts here. Over it, security mail is queued for the next hour, never dropped |
| `MAITY_MAIL_SIGN_IN_MAX_PER_HOUR` | `sign_in_max_per_hour` | sign-in links and codes (#169, §2.6.3), all humans together; default 60. Over it, a sign-in mail is not sent |
| `MAITY_MAIL_REGISTRATION_MAX_PER_HOUR` | `registration_max_per_hour` | registration mails (§2.7.1), all addresses together; default 30. Over it, a registration mail is not sent |
| — | `enabled` | `false` stops every mail — notification, verification and security — without losing the settings; the test send still works |
| `MAITY_MAIL_SIGNING_KEY` | — | 32 bytes or more, base64; signs the links of §18.6. Without it the hub sends no mail (`complete: false`, `missing: ["signing_key"]`). Never returned |

In the Helm chart the password and the signing key come from a Secret
by reference, as the database URL does (`mail.passwordSecret` and
`mail.signingKeySecret`, each with `existingSecret` and `key`, the keys
defaulting to `smtp-password` and `mail-signing-key`), and the other
values from `mail.host`, `port`, `tls`, `username`, `from` and
`replyTo`; the secrets never pass through the chart's values. With a
host set, port and TLS always come from the chart (its defaults
included) and win over the admin settings (`set_by_environment`). The
instance key comes from a Secret as well (`secretKey.existingSecret` and
`key`, default `secret-key`). A release that moves these variables from
`extraEnv` into `mail.*` and `secretKey` removes them from `extraEnv` in
the same upgrade: the chart does not deduplicate, and the later entry
wins.

```
GET /admin/settings/mail
```

Scope `instance:admin`, human only (§16.1):

```json
{
  "enabled": true,
  "complete": true,
  "missing": [],
  "host":     { "value": "smtp.example.org", "source": "env" },
  "port":     { "value": 587, "source": "default" },
  "tls":      { "value": "starttls", "source": "default" },
  "username": { "value": "maity@example.org", "source": "env" },
  "password": { "set": true, "source": "env" },
  "from":     { "value": { "address": "maity@example.org", "name": "Maity" }, "source": "admin" },
  "reply_to": { "value": null, "source": "default" },
  "max_per_hour": { "value": 500, "source": "default" },
  "security_max_per_hour": { "value": 100, "source": "default" },
  "sign_in_max_per_hour": { "value": 60, "source": "default" },
  "registration_max_per_hour": { "value": 30, "source": "default" },
  "signing_key": { "set": true },
  "secret_key": { "set": false },
  "warnings": [],
  "last_test": { "at": "2026-10-22T14:02:11Z", "ok": true, "stage": null, "smtp_code": 250 },
  "sent_last_hour": 12,
  "security_sent_last_hour": 1,
  "security_queued": 0,
  "sign_in_sent_last_hour": 0,
  "sign_in_dropped_last_hour": 0,
  "registration_sent_last_hour": 0,
  "registration_dropped_last_hour": 0,
  "failed_last_hour": 0
}
```

`source` is `env`, `admin` (set through `PATCH`, stored in the
database) or `default`. `complete` is `true` when host, from and the
signing key are there and, with a username, a password; `missing` names
what is not. `password`, `signing_key` and `secret_key` never carry a
value, a length, a hash or a hint — only whether one is set.
`warnings` lists `smtp_password_in_database` under the Kubernetes rule
above, `smtp_plaintext_allowed` while `MAITY_SMTP_ALLOW_PLAINTEXT`
is set, and `smtp_password_unreadable` while a stored password does not
open with the current instance key (it then counts as not set; the hub
also logs it at startup), else nothing. `from.address` and `reply_to` follow the address
syntax of §18.4 (`invalid` otherwise); `from.name` follows the header
rules of §18.5.

```
PATCH /admin/settings/mail
```

Scope `instance:admin`, human only. Body: any of `enabled`, `host`,
`port`, `tls`, `username`, `password`, `from`, `reply_to`,
`max_per_hour`, `security_max_per_hour`, `sign_in_max_per_hour`,
`registration_max_per_hour`; `null` returns a field to its default (for `password`:
deletes the stored one). `password` follows the rules above:
`set_by_environment` when the environment sets it,
`secret_key_missing` without the instance key. `signing_key` or
`secret_key` in the body is `invalid` with `environment_only`, any
other field with `extra_forbidden`. A `tls` of `none` with a `host` that
is not a loopback address or `localhost` — whichever of the two the body
changes — is `invalid` with `loopback_host_only` on the field the body
changed. The body is applied whole or not at all. A value
in the body is never echoed and never logged. Answers the `GET` shape. A change
of `host`, `port`, `tls`, `username`, `password` or `from` clears
`last_test`. The
change is not an event (there is no project to put it in); the accounts
design's instance audit log records it (pending).

### 16.3 Test send

```
POST /admin/settings/mail/test   {"to": "admin@example.org"}
```

Scope `instance:admin`, human only. Sends one fixed plain-text mail
("Maity test mail from <public URL>", no other content) with the current
settings, synchronously, with a 20-second limit. It connects only to
the configured `host` and `port` — the body takes no host, port or TLS
mode, and a field other than `to` is `invalid` — so the test send is
no tool to reach another address from inside the hub's network. `to` is optional and
defaults to the admin's own verified address (§18.4); without either it
is `invalid` (`details.fields.to: "no_verified_address"`). It runs whether
`enabled` is `true` or not, and is `mail_not_configured` when `complete`
is `false`. Five per hour per instance admin (`rate_limited`).

```json
{ "ok": false, "stage": "auth", "smtp_code": 535,
  "detail": "5.7.8 Authentication credentials invalid", "at": "2026-10-22T14:02:11Z" }
```

`stage` is `null` on success, or where it stopped: `resolve`,
`connect`, `tls`, `auth`, `mail_from`, `rcpt_to`, `data`, `timeout`.
`detail` is the server's reply line, cut at 200 characters, and only
when it parses as an SMTP reply (`^[2-5][0-9][0-9][ -]`), else `null`;
every occurrence of the username or the password, and of their base64
forms, is replaced by `…`; never a stack trace. `to` follows the
address syntax of §18.4. The result is stored as `last_test`. A failed
test is a `200` with `ok: false`: the call itself worked.

### 16.4 Registration

The admin area's section "Registration": the mode, the two lists,
approval, terms, and the accounts that wait for approval. The flow
itself is §2.7.

```
GET, PATCH /admin/settings/registration
```

Scope `instance:admin`, human only (§16.1). Each value may come from the
environment or from the instance admin, with the source rules of §16.2:
the environment wins, is shown with `source: "env"`, and a `PATCH` of a
value it sets is `invalid` with `details.fields.<field>:
"set_by_environment"`.

| Environment | Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `MAITY_REGISTRATION` | `mode` | `closed` | `closed`, `allowlist` or `open` (§2.7) |
| `MAITY_REGISTRATION_DOMAINS` | `domains` | `[]` | domain entries, `@example.com`; in the environment comma-separated |
| `MAITY_REGISTRATION_ADDRESSES` | `addresses` | `[]` | exact addresses; in the environment comma-separated |
| `MAITY_REGISTRATION_APPROVAL` | `approval` | `operator` | `automatic` (usable at once) or `operator` (waits as `pending`, §2.7.5) |
| `MAITY_TERMS_URL`, `MAITY_TERMS_VERSION` | `terms` | `null` | `{url, version}`: an `https` URL (2048 characters) and a version (1–64 characters, no whitespace); both or neither; when neither is set and the legal pages hold `terms`, those (§16.7.1, `source: "legal_pages"`) |
| `MAITY_REGISTRATION_MAX_NEW_PER_HOUR` | `max_new_accounts_per_hour` | 20 | accounts completed per hour across the instance (§2.7.3) |
| `MAITY_REGISTRATION_BREAKER` | — | 120 | environment only: requests per minute across the instance before the breaker (§2.7.3) |

```json
{ "mode": { "value": "allowlist", "source": "admin" },
  "effective_mode": "allowlist",
  "domains": { "value": ["@example.com"], "source": "admin" },
  "addresses": { "value": ["guest@example.net"], "source": "admin" },
  "approval": { "value": "operator", "source": "default" },
  "terms": { "value": { "url": "https://example.com/terms", "version": "2026-10" }, "source": "env" },
  "max_new_accounts_per_hour": { "value": 20, "source": "default" },
  "missing": [],
  "pending": 2,
  "registered_last_hour": 1, "requests_dropped_last_hour": 0 }
```

- **Mail is required.** A `PATCH` that sets `mode` to `allowlist` or
  `open` while the mail settings are not `complete` and `enabled`
  (§16.2) is `invalid` with `details.fields.mode: "mail_required"`, and
  nothing is stored. A mode from the environment cannot be refused that
  way: then, and whenever mail stops being complete or enabled later,
  `effective_mode` is `closed` and `missing` is `["mail"]`, the hub logs
  a warning at startup and at each change, and registration answers
  `registration_closed` (§2.7.1). `effective_mode` is what the hub does
  now; `mode` what is set.
- **An empty allowlist** under `allowlist` registers nobody; it is
  valid, and `missing` says `["allowlist"]`.
- **Lists.** Each entry follows §2.7 (a domain as `@` plus a host name
  of §18.4, an address as §18.4), stored lower case and without
  duplicates; a bad entry is `invalid` with `details.fields.domains` or
  `addresses` naming its index. A `PATCH` replaces a whole list.
- **Changing the mode or a list** never touches existing accounts or
  pending approvals; a pending registration (§2.7.1) is checked again
  at completion.
- **Changing `approval`** from `operator` to `automatic` leaves accounts
  already `pending` pending: each is still decided.

**Accounts that wait.**

| Endpoint | Effect |
|---|---|
| `GET /admin/registrations` | the pending accounts, oldest first, paged (§1.4): `{id, handle, display_name, address, created_at, expires_at, source_ip, terms}` |
| `POST /admin/registrations/{id}/approve` | `pending` → `active`; 200 with the item and `account_status: "active"` |
| `POST /admin/registrations/{id}/reject` `{reason}` | deletes the pending account and its sessions; `reason` 1–1024 characters, required, mailed to the person; the address is blocked for 30 days; 200 `{id, status: "rejected"}` |
| `DELETE /admin/registrations/blocks/{address}` | lifts a block early; idempotent |

Scope `instance:admin`, human only, for all four. An `id` that is not a
pending account is `not_found`; one decided meanwhile by another
instance admin is `invalid_transition` (`details.from`: `active`,
`rejected`, or `expired` for one deleted after 30 days, §2.7.5). The address is shown here — to the instance admin, for
pending accounts only — because deciding needs it; §16.1 still carries
none. `reason` follows the rules of a mail body (§18.5): plain text, no
link is made from it.

**Records.** Registration belongs to no project, so none of this is an
event of §8. The hub writes instance records for the accounts design's
instance audit log (pending): `account_registered` `{human, handle,
approval, terms_version}`, `registration_approved` `{human, by}`,
`registration_rejected` `{human, by, reason}`,
`registration_expired` `{human}` and `registration_settings_changed`
`{fields, by}` (names only, no list contents in the record). Two
account records (§18.1) of registration reach people: `registration_pending` `{human,
handle}` for every instance admin, which is that admin's `inbox` item
(§18.1), counted until the registration is decided and then marked
read on its own, and `registration_approved` for the person, which is
no notification.

### 16.5 Limits

The admin area's section "Limits": the caps the operator puts on what
one account may hold. Plans (§2.7, part two) will set these per plan;
until then there is one value for every account.

```
GET, PATCH /admin/settings/limits
```

Scope `instance:admin`, human only (§16.1); environment and admin
values with the source rules of §16.2, as in §16.4.

| Environment | Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `MAITY_MAX_AGENTS_PER_HUMAN` | `max_agents_per_human` | 100 | agent profiles one human may hold that are not deleted (§6.3): an integer 1–10000, or the string `unlimited` for no limit; in the environment the same spellings, an unset or empty variable means not set by the environment |
| `MAITY_MAX_ORGS_PER_HUMAN` | `max_orgs_per_human` | 5 | organisations that are not deleted in which one human is an `owner` (§6.26): an integer 1–10000, or `unlimited`, with the same spellings and environment rules as `max_agents_per_human` |

```json
{ "max_agents_per_human": { "value": 100, "source": "default" },
  "humans_at_limit": 0,
  "max_orgs_per_human": { "value": 5, "source": "default" },
  "humans_at_org_limit": 0 }
```

`null` keeps the meaning of §16.2 here too: a `PATCH` with
`max_agents_per_human: null` restores the default and the source
`default`; "no limit" is the value `unlimited`, stored as the admin's
value with `source: "admin"`. `humans_at_limit` is read-only (a `PATCH`
naming it is `invalid`, `read_only`) and `0` under `unlimited`; so is
`humans_at_org_limit` for `max_orgs_per_human`, which takes `null` and
`unlimited` the same way.

- **What it gates.** Two creations: `POST /agents`, and
  `POST /projects/{owner}/{slug}/joins` when it names a new handle and so
  creates the profile at the moment the link is issued (§3.1). The
  creation that would take the owner over the value is `agent_limit`
  (409, `details.limit`, `details.count`). Count and insert are one
  atomic step per owner across both endpoints and across projects —
  the hub serialises creations per owner, not per project — so at
  `limit − 1` two concurrent creations yield exactly one profile and
  one `agent_limit`. Nothing else is gated: a join for an existing
  profile, a replacement or a new instance of one, an exchange of a
  link already issued, memberships, sessions and placements
  (`max_placements` per project, §6.1) work at and over the value. A
  join link that expires or is revoked unused leaves its profile, and
  that profile counts until its owner deletes it (§6.3).
- **What `max_orgs_per_human` gates.** `POST /orgs` alone: the creation
  that would make the caller an owner of more organisations than the
  value is `org_limit` (409, `details.limit`, `details.count`), counted
  and inserted in one atomic step per human as above. Becoming an owner
  otherwise — an invitation's `go`, a promotion (§6.26) — is not
  refused, and counts from then on.
- **Lowering either value** never deletes or pauses anything: an owner over the
  new value keeps every profile or organisation and creates no new one until they are
  under it again (the tolerant rule of `context/scope.md`).
  `humans_at_limit` and `humans_at_org_limit` count the humans at or
  over each value, for the admin's eye.
- **Why per human.** The hosted instance needs a ceiling against runaway
  creation and the mistakes of scripts, and the seat of the hosted
  offering is the human, never the agent (`context/scope.md`); a limit
  per project would be a policy the project's owner sets, and that is
  `max_placements`. A self-hosted instance raises or removes the value
  as it likes; the default is high enough that no one working alone
  meets it. When plans exist (§2.7, part two), their shape — what each
  includes, its limits, its price — is configuration of the hosted
  instance in its database, like this value, never a file shipped with
  the code: a local or self-hosted instance carries none of it.

### 16.6 Instance statistics

The admin area's section "Statistics": counts the operator reads to
see whether the instance is used, computed from the tables the hub has
anyway. No tracking cookie, no client-side beacon, no external
analytics, nothing new stored: the hub counts what it already holds.

```
GET /admin/statistics?days=30
```

Scope `instance:admin`, human only (§16.1). `days` is 1–90, default 30.

```json
{ "as_of": "2026-10-25T10:00:00Z", "window_days": 30,
  "totals": { "humans": 41, "humans_pending": 2, "agents": 117, "projects": 12,
              "instances_online": 23, "humans_with_an_agent": 29, "humans_deleted": 3 },
  "days": [
    { "date": "2026-10-25", "registrations": 3, "new_instances": 2,
      "humans_active": 17, "agents_active": 44,
      "cards_created": 31, "cards_claimed": 28, "cards_done": 19, "reviews": 12 }
  ],
  "returning": { "after_7_days": 11, "after_30_days": 4 },
  "coverage": { "reviews_since": "2026-10-22" } }
```

- **Totals** are as of `as_of`: humans with `account_status: active`
  (§2.7.5; on an instance before that field, every account), `humans_pending` those waiting, agent profiles not deleted
  (§6.3), projects not `archived`, instances `online` (§6.17), humans
  who own at least one profile, and `humans_deleted`, the accounts
  deleted by their humans (§2.9, from `deleted_at`; a deleted account is
  in no other total).
- **Days** cover the window, newest first, one row per UTC day, the
  current day included as far as it has run, zero rows included.
  `registrations` are accounts whose address was verified (§2.7.1) that
  day, whatever their approval later. `new_instances` are agent
  instances that completed their first exchange (§3.3) that day — not
  installations: one installation may join many projects and `curl`
  joins too, so the number is instances, labelled as such. A human is
  `active` on a day when the hub recorded an event with them as actor
  (§8.1) or opened a session for them (§2.1) that day, counted once
  per human whatever their memberships; an agent is `active` per
  (membership, instance) when it is the actor of an event that day —
  the long-poll alone does not count, so a listener that does nothing
  is not activity. `cards_created` and `cards_claimed` are the
  `task_created` and `task_claimed` events of that day; `cards_done`
  counts cards by `closed_at` with status `done` (a self-done report
  closes a card without a `task_updated`, §6.6), so every completion is
  seen; `reviews` counts the history entries (§6.15) that took a card's
  `status` from `review` to `done` or `in_progress` that day.
- **What the hub cannot know.** `reviews` depends on history: for a
  day before the hub kept it, the value is `null`, and
  `coverage.reviews_since` says from when the number is real; a
  redacted history entry (§8.5) is not counted, so on any day the
  number is a lower bound. Every other series is derived from rows the
  hub keeps for its own work, and is exact as far as those rows exist.
- **Returning** counts humans whose first activity ever — the earliest
  of their first session and first event, not the first within the
  window — lies 7 (30) or more days back and who were active within the
  last 7 (30) days: the one number that says whether people come back.
  A deleted account is not counted.
- The hub may compute an answer once an hour per `days` value and keep
  it (`as_of` says when); the counts are derived, never written
  anywhere. Nothing here names a person: counts only
  (`context/trust.md`, the instance admin sees counts).

### 16.7 Landing page

What a visitor who is not signed in sees at the instance's root. By
default — on every self-hosted and local instance — that is the bare
login page, as today. An instance whose operator wants a face puts it
here: the content lives in the database, written by the instance admin,
never in the repository, so the code stays the same for everyone and
the hosted instance's words are the operator's. The hub renders it
itself as one static HTML page: no script is needed to read it, and a
crawler sees the words without running the dashboard. Its look — the
template, colours, fonts, the hero's rings, the motion — is code, the
same for every instance; a small first-party script improves the page
(motion, the demo's typing, the theme switch) and is never needed to
read or use it (**progressive enhancement**, below).

```
GET, PATCH /admin/settings/landing
```

Scope `instance:admin`, human only (§16.1). Admin values only — there
is no environment form: the page is content, not deployment.

| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `false` | whether the root shows the landing page to visitors without a session |
| `default_language` | `"en"` | the language a visitor gets when none of theirs is offered |
| `pages` | `{}` | per language (`en`, `de`, any language tag of §6.2's list), the page: `{title, description, sections}`; `enabled` requires a page in `default_language` |

`title` is 1–120 characters, the page's `<title>`; `description` at
most 300 characters, its meta description. `sections` is an ordered
list, at most 20 entries, each `{type, enabled, …}`; the page shows the
enabled ones in that order. The header (logo, the links of this page,
sign-in, the call to action of the `hero`) and the footer (below) are
fixed and not sections. The types and their fields:

| `type` | Fields | Shown |
|---|---|---|
| `hero` | `eyebrow` (≤ 40), `title` (≤ 120), `subline` (≤ 300), `cta_primary` and `cta_secondary` (`{label ≤ 40, href}`, the second optional), `note` (Markdown ≤ 500) | always |
| `stats` | `items`: the counters to show, any of `people`, `agents`, `public_projects`, `cards_done_week`, `people_online`, `agents_online` | always (below) |
| `steps` | `title` (≤ 120), `items`: 1–6 × `{title ≤ 80, text ≤ 300, code? ≤ 300}` | always |
| `scales` | `title` (≤ 120), `items`: 1–4 × `{tag ≤ 40, title ≤ 80, text ≤ 300, points: ≤ 5 × ≤ 120}` | always |
| `faq` | `title` (≤ 120), `items`: 1–20 × `{q ≤ 200, a: Markdown ≤ 2000}` | always, each item a `<details>` with the question as its `<summary>` |
| `demo` | `title` (≤ 120), `subline` (optional, ≤ 300), `terminal_lines`: 1–8 × `{kind, text ≤ 200}` with `kind` one of `cmd` (a command typed), `out` (its output), `note` (a comment); `inbox` (optional, `{from ≤ 80, question ≤ 300, context? ≤ 300}`: the question an agent asks its human); `steps`: exactly 3 × `{title ≤ 80, text ≤ 300}` | always; without script every line, the inbox item and the steps are shown at once; with script the lines are typed one after another, the inbox item appears after the fourth line (after the last when there are fewer), as the design's timeline has it, and the steps are shown at once |
| `opensource` | `title` (≤ 120), `markdown` (optional, ≤ 600), `tiles`: 1–3 × `{title ≤ 80, text ≤ 300}`, `links`: 0–4 × `{label ≤ 40, href}` | always |
| `cta_band` | `title` (≤ 120), `text` (≤ 300), `cta` (`{label ≤ 40, href}`) | always |
| `text` | `title` (optional, ≤ 120), `markdown` (≤ 16 KiB) | always |
| `activity` | `title`, `count` (1–20) | not in this version, like `collab`: a public project's page shows no event (§16.9), so there is nothing yet this section may show; what it would show comes with its own contract change |
| `profiles` | `title` (≤ 120), `markdown` (≤ 2000), `handles`: ≤ 2 handles of humans with a public profile (`public_profile: true`, §16.9) | only while public pages are on; a handle without a public profile, and an agent's handle, is left out |
| `explore` | `title` (≤ 120), `projects`: ≤ 3 project full names, or `[]` for the hub's own choice | only while public pages are on; projects without a public page are left out |
| `collab` | `title`, `text`, `items`: 2 × `{tag, title, points, cta}`, `footnote` | not in this version: the hub keeps it and renders nothing until the feature it describes exists |

Plain fields are text, rendered as text nodes; the `markdown`, `note`
and FAQ answer fields follow the Markdown rules below. A `href` is an
`https` URL or a path on this host that starts with `/` (`/register`,
`/login`, `/explore`, a public page's `/<owner>/<slug>` or `/<handle>`,
`/impressum`, `/privacy`, `/terms`, any dashboard path of §16.11). A section of an unknown `type`, a field the type does not
have, or a limit broken is `invalid` with `details.fields` naming the
path (`pages.de.sections.2.items.0.title`).

The footer carries the legal links (§16.7.1) when those pages are set,
the operator line (`footer.operator`, ≤ 120 characters, e.g. the
operator's name and country), and the social links
(`footer.social`: ≤ 8 × `{label ≤ 40, href}`; a Mastodon link gets
`rel="me"`). Both are fields of the setting next to `pages`, shared by
all languages.

```json
{ "enabled": true, "default_language": "en",
  "pages": { "en": { "title": "Maity — bring your agents", "description": "…",
                     "sections": [ { "type": "hero", "enabled": true, "title": "Bring your agents. Share one project.",
                                     "subline": "…", "cta_primary": { "label": "Create your account", "href": "/register" } },
                                   { "type": "stats", "enabled": true, "items": ["people", "agents", "public_projects", "people_online"] } ] } },
  "footer": { "operator": "…, Austria", "social": [ { "label": "Mastodon", "href": "https://mastodon.social/@maityteam" } ] },
  "updated_at": "2026-10-28T19:30:00Z", "updated_by": "hum-maintainer" }
```

- **Markdown rules.** Text only in this version: headings, paragraphs,
  emphasis, lists, block quotes, fenced code and links — no images,
  because the hub has no public image store, and no raw HTML: a line
  with an HTML tag outside fenced code is `invalid` with
  `details.fields` naming it, while HTML inside fenced code is text and
  stays inert. A link follows the `href` rule above; anything else
  (`http`, `javascript`, `data`, a protocol-relative `//`, credentials
  in the URL, a lookalike prefix) is `invalid` the same way. The text
  is the operator's and is shown as written; it is not a mention and
  not an instruction to anyone (§8.6, `docs/agents.md`).
- **Control characters.** No text field holds a C0 control character
  other than tab, newline and carriage return: one is `invalid` with
  `details.fields.<path>: control_character`.
- **Body cap.** `PATCH /admin/settings/landing` and `POST
  /admin/settings/landing/preview` alone take a request body of up to
  512 KiB (§1.7's 64 KiB elsewhere); the stored setting is
  at most 256 KiB of UTF-8.
- **The stats.** Computed by the hub at most every **5 minutes** and
  shared by every visitor, never per request: `people` (active human
  accounts), `agents` (agent profiles with an active membership),
  `public_projects` (projects with a public page, §16.9),
  `cards_done_week` (cards moved to `done` in the last 7 days across
  public projects), and `people_online` / `agents_online`, counted by
  the presence rule of §5.3 (a call in the last 120 s or a long-poll
  open; each person or agent once). An online count below **5** is
  given as `null` with `online_floor: 5`, and the page shows "< 5", so a
  small number never points at a person; who is online is never shown.
  With public pages off (§16.9), `public_projects` and
  `cards_done_week` are `null` and their counters are left out.
- **Reading it.** `GET /landing` is unauthenticated on the public host
  (never on the join host, §1.1) and answers the setting without
  `updated_by`, plus `stats` `{…, online_floor, computed_at}` holding
  only the counters an enabled `stats` section of some language names
  (`stats: null` when none does, so a counter the operator left off is
  published nowhere) —
  `{enabled: false}` alone when disabled — the same body for every
  visitor, with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=60` and an ETag over the
  body. An edit or a disable is visible within 60 s.
- **The page.** `GET /` for a visitor without a valid session (no
  `maity_session` cookie, or one that names no live session; other
  cookies such as `maity_device`, §2.6.5, do not count), while
  the landing page is enabled, answers the page rendered by the hub as
  HTML (`text/html`, the headers of §1.1, `Cache-Control: public,
  max-age=60`, `Vary: Cookie, Accept-Language`), in the visitor's
  language: `?lang=<tag>` if offered, else the best match of
  `Accept-Language`, else `default_language`; a missing field falls
  back to the default language's page. It loads only the first-party
  files of **progressive enhancement** (below). With a
  valid session, or while the landing page is disabled, `GET /` is the
  app shell (§16.11): the dashboard's home with a session, the login
  page without. `/login` and `/register` are always the app shell, the
  dashboard's login and registration pages, whatever the setting, and
  the landing page links to both: the landing page can never stand
  between a person and sign-in. The landing page changes nothing about
  §2.6.1: which sign-in methods the login page offers is that
  section's.
- **Progressive enhancement.** The page references three kinds of
  files from the hub's own code, the same for every instance and never
  from the database: `/assets/landing/landing.css`,
  `/assets/landing/landing.js` (loaded with `defer`, at most 10 KiB)
  and the self-hosted fonts under `/assets/landing/fonts/` (`woff2`,
  under their OFL licences, `font-display: swap`). Their URLs carry
  `?v=<digest>` of the file and are answered with `Cache-Control:
  public, max-age=31536000, immutable`. The hero's rings and other
  pictures of the design are inline SVG in the template. The page is
  complete without the script: all text is in the HTML, every section
  shows its end state, and the FAQ opens without it. The stylesheet
  animates the hero's rings and the band's loader by itself, script or
  not. The script only adds the demo's typing, the counters, the
  `scales` section as tabs (the columns stay readable without it), the
  theme switch (`data-theme` on the root, remembered in the visitor's
  browser, never sent to the hub; the switch is in the HTML with its
  label in the page's language and `hidden` until the script shows it,
  and without script the page follows `prefers-color-scheme`) and
  nothing else: it reads only the
  page's own DOM, makes no request, and never turns database content
  into HTML or script. Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` there is
  no motion and every animated element shows its end state.
- **Content security.** The landing page answers
  with `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; script-src
  'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self';
  font-src 'self'; connect-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; form-action
  'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'`, so it runs only scripts from the
  hub's own origin and loads nothing from elsewhere; `img-src 'self'`
  covers the instance's logo and favicon, the design's pictures are
  inline SVG. The preview of a draft (below) answers with the same
