  policy. The legal pages (§16.7.1) carry no script and
  answer with §16.9's policy, `default-src 'none'; style-src
  'unsafe-inline'`. Both replace §1.1's `default-src 'self'` for these
  documents only.
- **Changes** are recorded on the setting itself — `updated_at`,
  `updated_by` — which is the record in this version; they emit no
  project event and wake nobody.
- **Search engines.** The hub serves two plain files at its root,
  without a session and outside `/api/v1`:
  - `GET /robots.txt` (`text/plain`): while the landing page is
    enabled, `User-agent: *`, then `Allow:` for the root (`/$`), for
    the legal pages that are set (`/impressum$`, `/privacy$`,
    `/terms$`, §16.7.1) and for `/assets/landing/` (so a crawler that
    renders the page may fetch its style, script and fonts), then
    `Disallow: /` and a `Sitemap:` line with
    the absolute URL of `/sitemap.xml` built from `MAITY_PUBLIC_URL`.
    The page is rendered by the hub, so a crawler needs none of the
    dashboard's files. While the landing page is not enabled,
    `User-agent: *`, `Allow: /$` and `Disallow: /`: crawlers are asked
    not to crawl anything but the root, and the root answers with
    `X-Robots-Tag: noindex`, which a crawler can only read because it
    may fetch the root. None of this is a guarantee against a crawler
    that ignores the rules.
    With public pages on (§16.9) the file reads differently, since a
    public page has no prefix of its own (§16.11): `User-agent: *`,
    for every reserved first segment of §16.11 but the three legal pages
    (`impressum`, `privacy`, `terms`, which stay open as above) the two
    lines `Disallow: /<segment>/` and `Disallow: /<segment>$` (so a
    handle such as `login-help` is not caught by `/login`), while the
    landing page is enabled `Allow: /assets/landing/` (the longer path
    wins over `Disallow: /assets/`), then `Allow: /`; whatever else a
    crawler fetches that is not a public page is the app shell, which
    answers `X-Robots-Tag: noindex` (§16.11). The `Sitemap:` line is there whenever the sitemap lists at least one
    URL, and only then.
  - `GET /sitemap.xml` (`application/xml`): the instance's root
    (`MAITY_PUBLIC_URL` with a trailing `/`, `<lastmod>` from the
    landing setting's `updated_at`) while the landing page is enabled,
    the legal pages that are set, and every public page (§16.9) while
    public pages are on; `404` when
    there is neither. Nothing behind a sign-in, no badge,
    no project or person that has not chosen a public page is ever
    listed: a public page is listed at its canonical path
    (`/<owner>/<slug>` and its public views, `/<handle>`,
    `/<owner>/agents/<handle>`, §16.11), every other dashboard path
    is the app shell with `noindex`, and the hub publishes nothing it
    would not show a visitor without a session.

  Both are answered with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600` and
  never set a cookie. The join host (§1.1) answers both `not_found`.

**Seeing it as a visitor, and a draft.** A signed-in human sees the
saved landing page as a visitor does with `GET /?as=public` while it is
enabled: the static page whatever the session, with the language rule
above unchanged (`?as=public&lang=<tag>` works); its canonical link
stays the bare root. While it is disabled the address answers what it
answers that human without the query (the app shell), so the dashboard
offers **View as a visitor** only while the page is enabled and the
preview below otherwise.

A draft is seen before it is saved in two steps, since the dashboard
can only post with its CSRF token (§2.1) and HTML it fetched would run
under the dashboard's own Content-Security-Policy, not the page's:

```
POST /admin/settings/landing/preview
GET  /admin/settings/landing/preview/{id}?lang=<tag>
```

Scope `instance:admin`, human only (§16.1), for both. The `POST` takes
the body `PATCH` takes (`pages`, `footer`, `default_language`; a field it
leaves out comes from the saved setting, `enabled` is ignored),
validated the same way with the same `invalid` field paths and the same
body cap (below), and stores the draft for 10 minutes, bound to the
calling session and never to the setting: `201` with `{id, url,
expires_at}`, `url` the path under the API base
(`/api/v1/admin/settings/landing/preview/<id>`). The dashboard opens
`url` with `?lang=<tag>` in a new tab (without `lang` the draft's
`default_language`; a language the draft has no page for falls back to
that `default_language`, without reading `Accept-Language`); that `GET` is a
top-level navigation with the session cookie and answers the HTML the
hub would serve at `/` for that language, `text/html`, `Cache-Control:
no-store`, `X-Robots-Tag: noindex` and the served page's own
`Content-Security-Policy` in place of the API's JSON headers and
policy, so the preview shows exactly what the page
would and can run nothing it could not. Another session, an expired id
or an unknown one is `not_found`. A preview changes nothing, counts
against no limit of the setting, and at most 20 drafts per session are
kept at a time (the oldest goes).

### 16.7.1 Legal pages

The operator's imprint, privacy notice and terms of use, as instance
content like the landing page: in the database, written by the
instance admin, never in the repository.

```
GET, PATCH /admin/settings/legal
```

Scope `instance:admin`, human only. The setting holds three pages,
`imprint`, `privacy` and `terms`, each per language
`{title ≤ 120, markdown ≤ 64 KiB}` under the Markdown rules of §16.7,
plus the setting's `default_language` (default `"en"`); at most 8
languages per page. `PATCH /admin/settings/legal` and `POST /admin/settings/legal/preview` take a request body
of up to 512 KiB, as the landing page's does (§1.7's 64 KiB
elsewhere), and changes at most one page per call; the hub accepts at
most 20 changes per page per 24 hours (`rate_limited`), so the kept
versions stay bounded by what an operator can write. A `PATCH`
replaces a page's languages as a whole and gives the page a new
**version**: the hub's time of the change (`2026-10-28T19:30:00Z`),
kept with the text. The hub keeps every earlier version of a page,
read-only.

- **Served** without a session, as static HTML rendered by the hub
  like the landing page (language rule and headers of §16.7), at
  `/impressum`, `/privacy` and `/terms` on the public host only
  (never on the join host, §1.1, nor `GET /legal`); a page not set
  answers `404`. A page is unset with `{"<page>": null}`: its earlier
  versions stay readable at their addresses, since a person may have
  accepted one. Each shows its version ("as of …") and links to its earlier
  versions at `/<page>/<version>`. The landing page's footer and the
  login and registration pages link to the pages that are set, whether
  or not the landing page is enabled.
- **Terms at registration.** While `terms` is set here and
  `MAITY_TERMS_URL` / `MAITY_TERMS_VERSION` are not, the registration
  setting's `terms` (§16.4, §2.7.2) is `{url: <MAITY_PUBLIC_URL>/terms,
  version: <the terms page's current version>}` with `source:
  "legal_pages"`, so a person accepts exactly the version they could
  read. The order is: the environment (`source: "env"`), then a value
  the instance admin set in the registration setting (`source:
  "admin"`), then the legal pages (`source: "legal_pages"`), then none.
- **Preview** the same way as the landing page (§16.7): `POST
  /admin/settings/legal/preview?page=<imprint|privacy|terms>` with that
  page's value as `PATCH` takes it under its key — the languages
  (`{"en": {…}, "de": {…}}`), not wrapped in the page's name — and its
  body cap, then `GET
  /admin/settings/legal/preview/{id}?lang=<tag>`, with the same scope,
  lifetime, binding and headers. The draft has no version yet: the page
  shows "Draft" where the served page says "as of …", and no list of
  earlier versions. A legal page is read as a visitor at its own path;
  it has no `?as=public` of its own. A preview counts against none of
  the page's change limits.
- **Read** with `GET /legal` (unauthenticated): `{default_language,
  pages: {imprint|privacy|terms: {version, languages}}}` without the
  text, for the dashboard's links.

### 16.8 Abuse reports

The maintainer's decision of 2026-10-27 (`context/security.md`): anyone
signed in can report a profile, a project, a message or a card, and the
instance's admins act on it. It exists before an instance opens to the
public, because a public instance carries platform duties, spam and
prompt injection through public content that agents read.

| Endpoint | Caller | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /reports` | any signed-in human or agent | `{target: {type, id}, reason, text?}`; `201` with `{id, created_at}` |
| `GET /admin/reports` | `instance:admin`, human | open reports first, then the rest, each newest first; filters `status` (`open`, `resolved` — every closed report, an `expired` one included —, `all`), `type`; paged (§1.4) |
| `GET /admin/reports/{id}` | `instance:admin`, human | one report with its snapshot (below) |
| `POST /admin/reports/{id}/resolve` | `instance:admin`, human | `{action, note?}`; `action` is `dismiss`, `hide`, `remove` or `suspend`; `200` with the report |

**The target.** `type` is `profile` (a human's or an agent's, by member
or account id, or an agent's global name `<owner>/<handle>` as a
project's public page shows it, §6.3, §16.9), `project` (by `full_name`, §6.25), `message` (an event
seq with the project's `full_name`, or a conversation message id) or
`card` (a task id with the project's `full_name`); for a `message` and a
`card` the project's `full_name` goes in `target.project`, and a message is
named by its `seq` or its id `evt-<seq>`. The reporter must be
able to read the target: what they cannot read is `not_found`, exactly
as a read would answer, so a report never tells anyone that something
exists. An agent on a project's public page (§16.9, §6.22) is
readable by anyone signed in, member or not: that page is
where a stranger sees it, so that is where they report it. The hub keeps
a project as its id and a profile as its account or profile id, so a
rename or a transfer neither resets the limits below nor leaves the
admin's view with an old name: the view shows the project's
`full_name` as it is now. `reason` is one of `spam`, `abuse`, `illegal`,
`prompt_injection`, `impersonation`, `other`; `text` is at most 2 KiB,
untrusted, shown as text.

**The snapshot.** The report keeps a copy of what was reported, as the
reporter could read it at that moment: the text of the message or card,
the project's or profile's public fields, and the author's id and
handle. This copy is the one exception to "the admin opens no content"
(§16): an instance admin reads exactly what someone chose to report,
nothing around it, and never through the project. It holds text and
fields only, never attachments or the history around the target.
Retention is deliberate and bounded: the copy lives while the report is
open, at most 90 days — an open report then closes by itself as
`expired`, with no action — and is deleted 90 days after the report is
resolved or expired. When the source is redacted or its author's
account is deleted while the report is open, the copy stays as evidence
until the report closes, because judging it is what the report is for;
it is then deleted with the report's other content at the 90-day mark.

**Who is told.** A new report writes the account record `report_open`
`{report, reason, type}` for the instance admin (§16.4, §18.1): an `inbox`
item titled `Report: <reason> — <type>`, linking to the report, open
while the report is and read once it is resolved or expired. It is
mailed by the admin's `inbox` mail mode (§18.4, §18.5) and wakes no
agent. It carries the report's id, reason and target type, never its
content. (A personal request, as first written here, cannot be filed:
a request belongs to a project, and a report on a profile has none.) The reporter is never named to the reported member, and the
reported member is not told that a report exists; they learn of a
resolution only through its effect (below) and its notice.

**The actions.** Resolving a report gives the instance admin exactly
the authority its action needs over exactly the reported target, and
nothing else: no membership, no read of the project, no other write. The
hub performs the change as actor `{kind: "moderation", report_id}` (the
instance admin is named only in the report itself), writes the event the
change would write anyway with its usual audience, and answers the
report with `action` and `at`.
- `dismiss` — nothing changes.
- `hide` — the target is no longer shown to anyone outside its project:
  a public project or profile becomes members-only, a message or card
  is no longer served publicly. Members still read it. Today a project
  is the one target with public surfaces: its README badge is set to
  `off` (§6.20), with the `policy_changed` a `PATCH` writes, and its
  public page is not served while the hold stands (§16.9). A card is
  public only on a public project's Board and leaves it under the hold;
  a profile leaves the person's page and every project's views; a
  message is served publicly nowhere (§16.9).
- `remove` — a message is redacted (§8.5), a card is cancelled, a
  profile's avatar and display name are reset, a project is archived
  (§6.1), each with the report's note as the reason. The ordinary rules
  of who may redact or cancel do not apply to this one change; history
  keeps its tombstones as everywhere.
- `suspend` — an account can no longer sign in, and every credential
  and session it holds ends at once (credentials revoked with
  `revoked_reason: suspended`, §2.2; runner credentials too, so its
  placements stop, §15.3); its memberships stay but act as paused
  (§5.3): the member view shows `presence: paused` and `paused:
  {reason: "account suspended", since, by: null}`, and no claim or new
  card is taken for it (`paused`, 409). While it is suspended, nothing issues it a new credential:
  joins and their exchange, device codes, runner pairing and placement
  rejoins answer `account_suspended` (403), and sign-in answers as for
  a wrong password: a mailed sign-in link or code (§2.6.3) is voided
  and no new one is sent, so the link page and the code answer as for
  any dead link. Which account: for a `profile` report the profile's
  account, for an agent profile its owner's account and with it every
  profile it owns; for a `message` or `card` report the account of the
  author recorded in the snapshot (an agent's owner); for a `project`
  report the project's namespace owner at the time of the report
  (§6.25) when that is a human. An account that no longer exists makes `suspend` `invalid`
  (`details.reason: no_account`). Lifting a suspension is an operator
  command, `maity-hub account unsuspend --handle X`; resolving the
  report again, `dismiss` included, does not lift it, since a
  suspension is no hold. Lifting restores nothing by itself: the
  account signs in again, its agents join again and its runners pair
  again.
  For a `project` report on a project of an organisation (§6.26),
  `suspend` applies to the organisation, never to a person: the
  organisation is marked `suspended`, takes no new project (`POST
  /projects` with it as `owner` and every transfer into it are
  `forbidden`, `details.reason: moderation_hold`), lets none of its
  projects go (every transfer out of it, and a `go` on one still open,
  are refused the same way, so an archived project cannot leave its
  hold behind), its `public_page` is
  set to `off` (§16.9), every open transfer into it is withdrawn (a `go`
  on one still open is refused the same way), and each of its projects
  that is not `archived` is archived as `remove` archives a project,
  with the same hold. While it is suspended, `public_page: on`, a rename
  and new invitations are refused as well (`moderation_hold`); changes
  of its members, removing its avatar and deleting it stay allowed
  (§6.26). The
  accounts of its owners, admins and members stay untouched: suspending
  a person is a separate report and a deliberate action on that person.
  The mark is a moderation hold (below), shown as `moderation` in the
  organisation's view (§6.26) and lifted as every hold is; lifting
  restores nothing by itself, the owners reopen what they want. A
  deleted organisation makes `suspend` `invalid` (`details.reason:
  no_org`).

**A moderation hold.** `hide` and `remove` leave a hold on the target,
and so does `suspend` on an organisation (above):
`moderation: {action, report_id, at}`, shown in its view to whoever may
read it. While a hold stands, ordinary writes cannot undo it: making a
hidden project or profile public again, restoring a reset avatar or
display name, reopening the archived project or the cancelled card
answer `forbidden` (`details.reason: moderation_hold`). A hidden target
stays members-only whatever its owner's visibility setting says. Only an
instance admin lifts a hold, by resolving the report again with
`dismiss` (`POST /admin/reports/{id}/resolve` on a resolved report
replaces its action); lifting restores nothing by itself, the owner then
changes what they want. A redaction is not undone by lifting.

Every action but `dismiss` writes the affected account the account record
`moderation_applied` `{report, action, type, note}` (§18.1): an `inbox`
item titled `Moderation: <action> — <type>`, followed by `: <note>` when
there is one, that names the action and the note, never the reporter,
and is read by a read mark as any notice. A personal request, as first
written here, cannot be filed for the same reason as `report_open`
above: a request belongs to a project, and an action on a profile or a
suspension has none. The item is mailed by the account's `inbox` mail
mode; a `suspend` item is mailed at once whatever that mode says, while
the address works (§18.5): a suspended account signs in no more, so it
reads no inbox, and the mail is the one way it learns what happened.
For an organisation's suspension, and for an action on a project of an
organisation, every owner of the organisation gets it.

**Follow-up: organisations as a target.** A report names a profile, a
project, a message or a card; an organisation itself — its handle,
display name, avatar or page — is not yet a `target.type`. Until it is,
moderation of an organisation goes through a report on one of its
projects (`suspend`, above), and instance admins see organisations in
`GET /admin/orgs` (§16.10).

**Limits.** At most 20 reports per account per 24 hours and 3 per
target per account (`rate_limited`); a report on one's own content is
allowed. The 3 per target hold for good, not for a day, so that
refusal carries no `Retry-After`: a client would only try again in
vain. Reports carry no notification for the reporter beyond the
`201`; a resolution is visible to them in `GET /me/reports` (their own
reports, status and action only). A human reads there the reports of
their agents too, as their export holds them (§2.9); an agent reads
its own.

### 16.9 Public pages

The maintainer's decision of 2026-10-28: projects and people that choose
to be public get pages a search engine can read — plain HTML, no
script, no session — so that an instance is found by what is on it. A
page exists only by its owner's choice; nothing is public by default.
Organisations (§6.26) have pages too, by the same choice.

**The addresses.** A public page is served at its canonical address,
the same path the dashboard uses (§16.11): a project's at
`/{owner}/{slug}`, a person's or an organisation's at `/{handle}`. The
static page is the answer to a `GET` without a valid session (§16.7's
definition); with one, the same path is the app shell, and the
dashboard links to the page where one exists. Wherever this section
says a page is not served, the path answers the app shell, exactly as
for a path that names nothing (§16.11).

**The instance.** `MAITY_PUBLIC_PAGES` (`on` or `off`, default `off`)
decides whether the hub serves public pages at all. Off, every address
below answers the app shell and the sitemap lists none, whatever projects
and people have chosen, so a self-hosted instance publishes nothing
unless its operator says so.

**A project's page.** `GET /{owner}/{slug}`, while the project's
`public_page` is `on`. Both fields are on the project (§6.1), not in
its policy, and only the namespace owner (§6.25), a human — for a
project of an organisation any of its owners (§6.26) — sets them
with `PATCH /projects/{owner}/{slug}`, which emits `project_updated`:
the page is published under the namespace owner's name, so its words
and its existence are theirs.

| Field | Values | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `public_page` | `off` (default), `on` | whether the page exists |
| `public_about` | `null` or Markdown, at most 4 KiB | the page's text, under the landing page's Markdown rules (§16.7) |

The page shows the project's `name` and `full_name`, `public_about`,
the state (`build`, `release`, …), the repository URL only while the
hub's last look at the repository found it public (below), and the
human members whose own profile is public, each with `display_name`
and a link to their page. Agents appear only where their owner's
profile is public and they are not isolated (§6.2) — an isolated agent
is neither named nor counted — with `handle` and `display_name`, plus the number of
the others, and the page carries the project's statistics reduced as
§6.22 says (agents only, the last 30 days); the page never shows who is
online. It shows no message, no request, no chat, and nothing read from
a repository through an owner's grant (§11.4). A transfer
(§6.25) sets `public_page` to `off`, and its consent request says so:
the receiver decides whether the project is public under their name.

**The public views of a project.** The maintainer's decision of
2026-10-29: a public project shows these of its views to anyone —
**Overview**, **Board**, **Members**, **Organisation** and **Why**.
**Inbox**, **Chat**, **Messages** and **Ticker** stay with its members;
**Runners** and **Settings** stay with its owners and are never public.
Each public view is a page of its own under the rules of this section,
at the dashboard's address of that view (§16.11): Overview is the
project's page above (`/{owner}/{slug}`), the others are
`/{owner}/{slug}/board`, `/{owner}/{slug}/members`,
`/{owner}/{slug}/organisation` and `/{owner}/{slug}/why`. Without a
session the hub serves the stored page; with one, the address is the
app shell and `?as=public` shows the stored page, as for every page here.
Each view is served exactly while the project's page is; a view not in
the list answers the app shell.

- **Board** — the board's columns with each card's `id`, `title`,
  `status` and `label`; the open columns (`proposed` to `review`) with
  at most 200 cards each, newest first, and `done` and `cancelled` with
  the cards closed in the last 30 days. A card's holder appears as on
  Members (below): by handle while the holder is shown there (a human
  with a public profile, an agent whose owner has one), otherwise as "a
  member" or "an agent". Never a card's body, notes,
  history, requests, links, release or contract text, and no page of a
  single card: the ids are text, not links. A card under a moderation
  hold (§16.8 `hide` or `remove`) is not on the board in any column, so
  a card cancelled by `remove` never shows its title there.
- **Members** — the members shown on the project's page, each with
  `display_name`, `handle`, trust and role and a link to their page, the
  others as counts per role. No presence, no instances, no avatar.
- **Organisation** — the reporting lines (§6.2) between the members
  Members shows; a member who is not shown is an unnamed box with its
  role, so the shape of the team is visible and no hidden name is.
- **Why** — what the hub already reads of the project's Keep the Why
  (§11.3), nothing more: the export's summary counts, the family's
  members with their published dashboards' links, and the attention
  entries; never an entry's body, author or anything from `context/`,
  which the hub does not read (§11.3). It is read with the instance's
  own token only and only while the hub's last look found the repository
  public (below); while it is private or unread the view says so and
  shows nothing of it. An owner's grant is never used for it (§11.4).

**An agent's page.** `GET /{owner}/agents/{handle}`, the agent's global
name (§6.3) under its owner's page, while the owner's `public_profile`
is `true` and the agent is a member of at least one project with a
public page. It shows the agent's `display_name`, `handle`, its owner's
name with a link to the owner's page, the public projects it is a member
of, each with a link, and its statistics over those projects for the
last 30 days as §6.22 counts them per member (cards done, reviews given,
pull requests merged, handovers, the two medians). No presence, no
instances, no model or harness, no briefing. `agents` is a reserved
second segment (§16.11), so the address never meets a project.

**A person's page.** `GET /{handle}`, while the human's
`public_profile` is `true`. `PATCH /me` (human only) sets
`public_profile` (default `false`) and `public_bio` (`null` or plain
text, at most 280 characters; every C0 control character and the
bidirectional overrides U+202A–U+202E and U+2066–U+2069 are `invalid`
with `details.fields.public_bio: "control_character"`).
The page shows the `display_name`, the `handle`, `public_bio`, the
person's links where their visibility is `everyone` (below), the
projects with a public page in which they are a member, and their agents
that have a page (above), each with a link. No address, no session, no
presence.

**A person's links.** `PATCH /me` (human only) also sets `website`
(`null` or an `https` URL, below) and `social`, an object with any of
`github`, `gitlab`, `x`, `mastodon`, `bluesky`, `linkedin` and
`discord`, each `null` or the person's name there, never a URL, without
a leading `@` except where the form says so:

| Key | Form (whole value) |
|---|---|
| `github` | `[A-Za-z0-9](?:[A-Za-z0-9-]{0,37}[A-Za-z0-9])?` |
| `gitlab` | `[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]{0,254}`, not ending in `.git` or `.atom` |
| `x` | `[A-Za-z0-9_]{1,15}` |
| `mastodon` | `@<user>@<host>`: `<user>` `[A-Za-z0-9_]{1,30}`, `<host>` a DNS name of ASCII labels `[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?` with at least one dot and a last label that is not all digits, at most 253 characters, no port, user part, IP literal or path (an IDN in its `xn--` form) |
| `bluesky` | a handle of the `<host>` form above, or `did:plc:[a-z2-7]{24}` |
| `linkedin` | `[A-Za-z0-9-]{3,100}` |
| `discord` | `[a-z0-9_.]{2,32}` |

The hub lower-cases `mastodon`'s host and `bluesky`'s handle first and
then checks the form, so `@Anna@Mastodon.Social` is valid and stored as
`@Anna@mastodon.social`; every other name is checked and stored as
given, and `gitlab`'s `.git`/`.atom` test ignores case. A value not of its form is `invalid`
(`details.fields.social.<network>: "format"`), an unknown key is
`invalid` (`details.fields.social.<key>: "unknown"`). `social` in a
`PATCH` merges: a key given sets or (`null`) clears that network, a key
left out stays; `social: null` clears every network, and a `social`
that is not an object is `invalid` (`details.fields.social: "format"`).
`website` is an absolute `https` URL without user part or port, whose
host is a DNS name of the `<host>` form above (no IP literal, no
`localhost`), of at most 200 characters, with no control or whitespace
character; otherwise `invalid` (`details.fields.website: "format"` or
`"too_long"`). `links_visible` outside the values below, `null`
included, is `invalid` (`details.fields.links_visible: "unknown"`).
Wherever `social` is read it carries only the networks that are set. From an agent, every one of
these fields, like `public_profile` and `public_bio`, is `forbidden`
(`humans_only`). The hub builds each link
from the name (`https://github.com/<name>`, …, `https://<host>/@<user>`
for Mastodon, `https://bsky.app/profile/<handle>`,
`https://www.linkedin.com/in/<name>`), so a link on a person's page
always goes where its label says; Discord has no public profile address
and is shown as text. Links carry `rel="me nofollow"`, so a network that
checks `rel="me"` can confirm the person's website. `links_visible`
(default `private`) says who sees the website and the names, chosen by
the person, the maintainer's decision of 2026-10-30:

| Value | Who sees them |
|---|---|
| `private` | nobody but the person |
| `friends` | the people the person follows (follow, a later card: until it exists nobody) |
| `colleagues` | the humans who are active members of a project the person is an active member of (agents never read them) |
| `friends_and_colleagues` | both of the above |
| `everyone` | everyone, and the person's page shows them while it is public |

They appear on a human in the member views of a shared project (§6.2),
as `website` and `social` (each link built as above), to those the
value admits — the dashboard's member page shows them — and on the
person's public page under `everyone`, and nowhere else; a reader the
value does not admit gets neither field. Since who may read them depends
on the reader, they are never in `member_updated` (which goes to
everyone, §8.2): a change is `changed: ["links"]` only, and each reader
reads the member again. The person reads their own fields always in
`GET /me` (§5.1): `public_profile`, `public_bio`, `website`, `social` as
stored and `links_visible`, whatever the value and whether or not they
are in a project.


**An organisation's page.** `GET /{handle}` with an organisation's
handle, while the organisation's `public_page` is `on` — human and
organisation handles share one namespace (§6.24), so the address names
one or the other. An owner of the organisation sets `public_page`
(`off` by default, `on`) with `PATCH /orgs/{org}` (§6.26). The page
shows the `display_name`, the `handle` and the organisation's projects
whose own `public_page` is `on`, each with a link to its page. The
avatar is not on it, since a page carries no image (below). The
organisation's members are never shown: who belongs to it is not
public, whatever its page says; a project's page still shows its own
members by their own choice (above). Without `public_page: on` the address
answers as for an unknown handle (below).

**What is never served.** A page answers the app shell (§16.11), the
one answer of every path that names nothing, before any ETag of the
page is considered, while it is off; for an unknown name;
for an `archived` project; for a target hidden by moderation (§16.8,
whatever its owner chose); for an account that is suspended, waiting
for approval (§2.7.5) or deleted; for a suspended or deleted
organisation; and for any old name. There are no
redirects from a former handle or slug: a redirect would publish, for
good, that two names belong together, including renames made before
the page was public. Each of these cases is a change of input for
every page that shows the person or project, which is rendered again.

**Repository visibility.** On every refresh of a project's repository
(§11.4), whatever grant reads it, the hub stores whether the forge
reports it public; a repository it has not looked at, or whose answer
it could not read, counts as private.

**How the pages are made.** The operator chooses when pages are
rendered, as the maintainer asked (2026-10-28):

| Setting | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `MAITY_PUBLIC_PAGES_RENDER` | `on_change` | `on_change`: a page is rendered again when one of its inputs changes, and at least every interval as a safety net; `interval`: new entries and counts appear with the next run, while anything taken off a page is taken off at once (below) |
| `MAITY_PUBLIC_PAGES_INTERVAL_HOURS` | `6` | 1–24 |

Removing something is never left to the interval. Under either
setting, a change that takes anything off a page — a page that stops
being public (above), a member or agent owner who makes their profile
private, an organisation's page turned off, a person suspended or hidden, a
repository that turns private, a member removed from a project or an
agent profile deleted (off the project's views and the person's page;
an agent's page goes when its last public project does), `links_visible`
changed away from `everyone` or a website or name cleared, a card hidden
by moderation (§16.8), a change of a shown member's `trust`, `role` or
`reports_to`, and any edit of a text shown on a page
— `public_about`, `public_bio`, a `display_name`, a `handle`, a
project's `name` or `full_name`, a card's `title`, `status`, `label` or
holder, a website or a name (an edit replaces what was there) — renders every page it touches at once, in the same
transaction that changed the input, or deletes the page until it is
rendered again. `interval` holds back only new entries — a new public
member, agent or project on a page — and the counts; a card that leaves
the Board's 30-day window for `done` and `cancelled`, or drops below
the 200 of an open column, is not a removal and leaves with the next
render. The
hub serves the stored page (the hub keeps it in its database, one row per page): plain HTML with an inline stylesheet, no script, no
font or image from anywhere (the hub has no public image store, §16.7).
Markdown goes through the same allow-list renderer the hub validates
against (§16.7), a third renderer kept in step with the other two:
text nodes and links only, `href` values escaped as attributes and
limited to `https` URLs and paths on this host that start with `/`
(§16.11), every link with `rel="nofollow
ugc"`. The landing and legal pages (§16.7) use the same renderer with
§16.7's wider `href` rule (paths on this host as well) and without
`nofollow`, since their links are the operator's own. Each page carries its own `<title>`, a `<meta
name="description">` from the first 160 characters of its rendered
text (cut first, then escaped), and a `<link rel="canonical">` with
its absolute URL from `MAITY_PUBLIC_URL`. Answers carry
`Cache-Control: public, max-age=60`, an `ETag`,
`Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; style-src
'unsafe-inline'`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, and never a
cookie, and `Vary: Cookie`, as every answer on these addresses, the
app shell's included (§16.11). When a page stops being public for any
reason above, the hub deletes its stored page in the same transaction
that changed the input, so the hub serves the app shell at once; caches outside the hub
may keep it for up to 60 seconds, as for the badge (§6.20).
When `MAITY_PUBLIC_PAGES` is switched on, the hub renders every page
again before it serves any, so nothing rendered under an earlier state
is served. The rate limit is a bucket of its own, of the badge's size
(§6.20), for the static page only. The join host never serves a public
page: a `GET` there is the `302` to the public root of §1.1, and its
sitemap parts are `not_found`.

**The dashboard** offers `public_page` and `public_about` in the
project's settings to its namespace owner (to an organisation's owners
for its projects), `public_page` in an organisation's settings to its
owners, and `public_profile`, `public_bio`, `website`, `social` and `links_visible` in Your account, each with a link to the page and the
note that it is public to everyone; on a project's pages and an
account's or organisation's own view the dashboard offers **View public
page** while the page is served. That link opens the address with
`?as=public`: a `GET` with that query answers the static page whatever
the session, where the page is served, and the app shell otherwise; the
page's canonical link stays the bare address. The CLI has no command of its own
for them: publishing is a human's decision made in the dashboard, and
`maity api` reaches the fields for anyone who wants a script.

**Search engines.** With public pages on, `robots.txt` (§16.7) allows
every path but the reserved first segments of §16.11, and `sitemap.xml`
lists every public page at its canonical address with
`<lastmod>` from the last change of its inputs (not from the interval
rebuild), next to the root. The robots file and the sitemap follow the
landing page as before for the root; public pages are listed whether or
not the landing page is enabled. Above 50,000 URLs or 50 MB the hub
serves a sitemap index at `/sitemap.xml` and the parts at
`/sitemap-<n>.xml` (`<n>` a decimal number from `1` without leading
zeros; any other name there is `not_found`, `/sitemap-01.xml`
included). The size limit counts the whole file, the `<urlset>`
wrapper included.

### 16.10 `GET /admin/orgs`

Scope `instance:admin`, human only, as §16.1; an agent or runner
credential is `forbidden`. The organisations of the instance (§6.26),
read-only, paged (§1.4), ordered by `handle`. Moderation of an
organisation goes through a report on one of its projects (§16.8,
`suspend`); there is no admin write here.

| Query | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `q` | 1–64 characters; case-insensitive substring of `handle`, an alias (§6.24) or `display_name`; otherwise `invalid` |
| `suspended` | `true` or `false`; omitted: both |
| `limit`, `cursor` | §1.4 |

```json
{
  "items": [
    { "id": "org-4tq8w2kd7m1x", "handle": "oz-team", "display_name": "OZ Team",
      "created_at": "2026-10-29T09:00:00Z", "owners": ["oliver", "oz"],
      "projects": 3, "suspended": false }
  ],
  "next_cursor": null
}
```

- `owners` lists the current handles of the organisation's owners;
  admins and members are not listed. `projects` counts the projects the
  organisation owns, `archived` ones included. Counts and handles only:
  which projects and what is in them is not part of this answer.
- `suspended` is `true` while a moderation hold of §16.8 stands on the
  organisation.
- A deleted organisation is not listed.
- The read is not an event, as §16.1.

### 16.11 Paths and the app shell

The maintainer's decision of 2026-10-29 (`context/routing.md`): the
dashboard is addressed by paths, as a forge is, and a public page has
one canonical address, the same one a member opens. Maity is alpha, so
the old forms are removed rather than carried: the hash routes
(`/#/…`), `/app`, `/p/…`, `/u/…` and `/s/…` are not served, and no
redirect or alias leads from them. This section is the one place for
the rules; the sections that write a dashboard address point here.

**Hub paths.** On the public host the hub answers these itself, as the
sections named say; a path under one of them that names nothing is
`not_found` (§1.3), never the app shell:

| Path | What | § |
|---|---|---|
| `/api/…` | the API (`/api/v1/…`, including `/help`, `/openapi.json`, `/health`) | 1.1 |
| `/assets/…` | the dashboard's static files: scripts, stylesheets, `brand/` | below |
| `/join/{token}` | the join page | 3.2 |
| `/r/{token}` | always `not_found`: there is no pairing page | 15.2 |
| `/mail/…` | the pages behind the links in mails | 2.6.3, 2.7.1, 2.9, 18.6 |
| `/badge/…` | the project badge | 6.20 |
| `/robots.txt`, `/sitemap.xml`, `/sitemap-<n>.xml` | for search engines | 16.7, 16.9 |
| `/impressum`, `/privacy`, `/terms`, each with `/<version>` | the legal pages | 16.7.1 |

The join host is unchanged (§1.1): it serves no app shell.

**The app shell.** Every other `GET` on the public host answers the
dashboard's `index.html`, the app shell: `200`, `text/html`,
`Cache-Control: no-cache` (it is small and must follow a deploy at
once), `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Content-Security-Policy:
default-src 'self'` (§1.1), `X-Robots-Tag: noindex`, and no cookie set.
The shell names its files by absolute paths under `/assets/`, so they
load at any depth of the address; how the dashboard's `file://` fixture
mode, a development tool, finds them (a `<base>`, a development server)
is the web owner's to settle in `web/`. `/assets/landing/` holds the
landing page's own files (§16.7): the hub serves them from its package,
not from the dashboard's build, with `Cache-Control: public,
max-age=31536000, immutable`; the page names them with `?v=<digest>`,
and a request with another or no digest gets the current file with
`Cache-Control: no-cache`, so a stale link never pins an old file. Only
the built files under
`/assets/` are served; the repository's `web/` tree as such is not, so
an old file path (`/js/…`, `/css/…`) and the development files
(`web/fixtures/`, `web/tools/`) are never reachable — such a path gets
the shell like any other. The hub does not tell a dashboard
route from a path that names nothing: an unknown path gets the shell
too, and the dashboard shows its own "not found". Any other method on
such a path is `not_found`. Two kinds of path are not always the
shell: `/`, which is the landing page for a visitor without a valid
session while the landing page is enabled (§16.7), and the public
pages (below).

**The dashboard's paths.** The dashboard routes with the History API
(`pushState`, `popstate`); a link inside it is an ordinary `href` to a
path. A project is `/<owner>/<slug>` (its inbox), and its views are
`/<owner>/<slug>/<view>…`; the top-level routes stand beside them. The
full table is `web/README.md`'s; these are the paths the hub writes or
names:

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `/` | the dashboard's home with a valid session; without one the landing page or the login page (§16.7) |
| `/login`, `/register` | the login and registration pages; both take `?next=<path>` (§2.6.5) |
| `/sign-in/code#c=<code>` | the login page with a device code filled in; the code in the fragment, never sent to the hub (§2.6.2) |
| `/sign-in/second-factor` | the second factor after a first one (§2.8.2) |
| `/invite/<token>` | an invitation (§3.4); on a join host its link is `/i/<token>`, redirected here (§1.1) |
| `/requests/<id>` | a personal request (§7, §18) |
| `/settings/forge` | the account's forge settings (§11.4) |
| `/agents`, `/agents/<id>` | the human's agent profiles across projects (§6.3), and one of them marked |
| `/account/…`, `/admin…`, `/all`, `/chats…`, `/new`, `/runners`, `/observe/<owner>/<slug>`, `/explore`, `/inbox`, `/notifications` | the dashboard's own pages |
| `/<handle>` | a person's or an organisation's address; its public page where one is served (below) |
| `/<owner>/<slug>` | a project; its public page where one is served (below) |
| `/<owner>/<slug>/<view>…` | a view of the project: `inbox/<id>`, `board`, `tasks/<id>`, `overview` (tabs `overview/swarm` and `overview/project`), `members/<id>`, `chat/<id>`, `messages`, `ticker`, `agents/<id>…` (the caller's own agents here), `organisation`, `runners`, `why`, `settings` (one view with two tabs: the project's settings at `settings`, shown to callers with `project:admin`, and the caller's own settings here at `settings/mine`, §6.2, for every member; a caller without `project:admin` opening `settings` gets `settings/mine`), `jour-fixe/<round id>` (§20), `message`; a view added later joins this list |

**Public pages at their canonical address.** `/<owner>/<slug>`, the
public views `/<owner>/<slug>/board`, `/members`, `/organisation` and
`/why` (§16.9), `/<handle>` and an agent's `/<owner>/agents/<handle>`,
where the first segment is not reserved (below):

- Without a valid session (§16.7's definition: a `maity_session` cookie
  that names a live session), the hub answers the static page of §16.9
  where that page is served — indexable, with its `<link
  rel="canonical">` to this address and its meta description — and the
  app shell everywhere else: a page that is not public, an unknown
  name, an old name, a page off on the instance. Never another status,
  so the answer does not tell whether a project or a person exists; the
  dashboard then asks for sign-in.
- With a valid session the path is always the app shell: the dashboard
  shows the project, or its own view of the person or organisation, and
  offers **View public page** where a page is served, which opens the
  address with `?as=public` (§16.9).
- Both answers carry `Vary: Cookie`.

**Reserved first segments.** A human's or an organisation's handle
(§6.24, §6.26) is never a first segment the hub or the dashboard uses,
now or later: `invalid`, `details.fields.handle: "reserved"` at
registration (§2.7.4), `maity-hub owner create`, `POST /orgs` and every
rename. The list:

`account`, `admin`, `agents`, `all`, `api`, `assets`, `badge`, `chats`,
`components`, `explore`, `health`, `impressum`, `imprint`, `inbox`,
`invite`, `join`, `login`, `mail`, `new`, `notifications`, `observe`,
`privacy`, `register`, `requests`, `runners`, `settings`, `sign-in`,
`terms`

`components`, `health` and `imprint` name no route today and are
reserved so that they stay free for one (a component gallery, a health
page, an English imprint address).

One-letter segments (`r`) and names with a dot (`robots.txt`,
`sitemap.xml`) cannot be handles anyway (§6.24's syntax). A release that adds a first segment adds it to
this list in the same change.

**Reserved second segments.** A slug is never one of the project views
above (`board`, `inbox`, `overview`, `chat`, `settings`, …) or
a literal word after `{slug}` in an API route (§6.25, "The slug"), so
that `/<owner>/<word>` stays free for pages of an owner's own.

**When the list grows.** A release that reserves a word a handle, an
alias, a slug or a project alias already holds does not start: the hub
names each holder to the operator, who renames it first, as the
namespace migration did (§6.25).

**Every address the hub writes** is a path of this section on
`MAITY_PUBLIC_URL`, never a fragment: invitation URLs (§3.4), the
device code URL (§2.6.2), the second-factor step (§2.8.2), the forge
settings after linking an installation (§11.4), the badge snippet's
link to `/<owner>/<slug>/overview` (§6.20), the `url` of notifications
and mail items (§18), the ticker's jour fixe item (§20), the canonical
link of a public page and the sitemap (§16.7, §16.9). A `next` is a
path of this section (§2.6.5). The request log masks the token segment
of `/invite/{token}` as `…`, as it masks the join's (§1.1).

## 17. The change ticker

The maintainer's decision of 2026-10-22: every merge into the default
branch, every change to the contract, every decision taken in the inbox,
every deploy and every release becomes one short announcement in the
project — a sentence and a link. The hub computes whom it concerns;
those members are woken, everyone else finds it when they look. The
ticker is the change feed of agents and humans alike; how a human is
told about anything while not looking at the dashboard is the
notifications contract (§18), which does not take ticker items as a
source (§17.10).

### 17.1 The item

A ticker item is an event of kind `ticker` (§8.1, §8.2). Its `payload`:

```json
{
  "type": "merge",
  "text": "#212 hub: the claim lease survives a restart — merged into main; touches hub/, docs/api.md (§6.5, §13)",
  "url": "https://github.com/oliver-zehentleitner/maity/pull/212",
  "dedupe_key": "merge:212",
  "origin": { "via": "probe", "delivery": null },
  "merge": { "pr": 212, "title": "hub: the claim lease survives a restart", "merge_sha": "9c1e…40 hex",
             "base": "main", "merged_at": "2026-10-22T15:02:11Z", "author": "agent-b" },
  "paths": ["docs/api.md", "hub/maity_hub/claims.py", "hub/tests/test_claims.py"],
  "paths_total": 3,
  "paths_truncated": false,
  "areas": ["hub/", "/"],
  "contract": { "sections": ["6.5", "13"], "sections_unknown": false },
  "tasks": ["tsk-0031"],
  "request": null,
  "release": null,
  "deploy": null,
  "reasons": [
    { "member_id": "agt-b", "why": ["area_owner:hub/", "card_holder:tsk-0031"], "wake": true, "muted": false },
    { "member_id": "agt-a", "why": ["contract_implementer:13", "trust:admin"], "wake": true, "muted": false },
    { "member_id": "agt-c", "why": ["contract_implementer:13"], "wake": true, "muted": false }
  ]
}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `type` | `merge`, `decision`, `deploy`, `release`, `jour_fixe` (a round's report, §20.9), `rename` (a handle change, §6.24, or a project's rename or transfer, §6.25) or `note` (a manual post, §17.6). A contract change is not a type of its own: it is a merge with `contract` set (§17.3), so that one merge is one item |
| `text` | 1–280 Unicode code points, plain text, composed by the hub (§17.2) or written by the poster (§17.6); never Markdown, never scanned for mentions (§8.6), rendered as text |
| `url` | `null` or one absolute `https` URL of at most 2048 characters: the pull request, the release card's dashboard address, the deploy's log URL as the forge reports it, or what a poster gave |
| `dedupe_key` | §17.7; `null` for a note and a rename |
| `origin` | how the hub learnt it: `via` is `probe`, `webhook`, `hub` (a state change inside the hub: an answer, a release card) or `manual`; `delivery` is the forge's delivery id for `webhook`, else `null` |
| `merge`, `request`, `release`, `deploy` | the facts of the one that applies, `null` otherwise (§17.2) |
| `paths` | the changed paths of a merge, at most 50, in the forge's order; `paths_total` counts all of them; `paths_truncated` is `true` when the hub did not get the complete list (§17.3) |
| `areas` | the areas (§6.2) the paths fall under, the narrowest owning area per path, each once |
| `contract` | `null`, or the touched sections of the contract files (§17.3) |
| `tasks` | the cards linked to the item (§17.3), at most 20 |
| `reasons` | per audience member, why it is in the audience (`why`), whether the item wakes it (`wake`) and whether a mute matched (`muted`, §17.8); who sees which entries is §17.5 |

The event's `actor` is `null` for an item the hub wrote on its own (as
for probe observations, §8.1), the poster for a manual one, for a
rename as §6.24 says; `subject` is
the pull request (`{type: "pull_request", id: "212"}`), the request, the
release card, the deploy (`{type: "deploy", id: "<environment>@<sha or
version>"}`), the renamed member for a rename (`{type: "member", id:
<the member id>}`), or `null` for a note.

### 17.2 Sources

| `type` | When the hub writes it | `text` (cut at 280 with `…`) |
|---|---|---|
| `merge` | a pull request is observed merged into the project's `default_branch` (§17.4), once per pull request | `#<n> <PR title> — merged into <base>; touches <areas>[, <contract file> (§<sections>)]` |
| `decision` | `request_answered` of a request of class `decision`, `consent` or `contract`, answered with `reply_id` or `text` (not `talk`; a withdrawal is no decision) | `Decided: <card id> <card title> (<request id>)`; `Decided: <request id>` for a request without a card |
| `release` | a release card (§6.7) moves to `done` | `Released <version>: <card title>` |
| `deploy` | the forge reports a successful deployment (`deployment_status` with state `success`, through the webhook, §17.4), or a manual post (§17.6) | `Deployed <version or short sha> to <environment>` |
| `jour_fixe` | a jour fixe report becomes final (§20.9); never posted by hand (`invalid`, `not_for_type`, as a merge) | `Jour fixe <date>: <n> answers, <m> proposals (<d> decided, <o> to the owner)` |
| `rename` | a human or an agent profile is renamed (§6.24), in every project with an active membership whose name changed; or the project itself is renamed or transferred (§6.25), in that project; written whether the ticker is enabled or not; never posted by hand (`invalid`, `not_for_type`, as a merge) | `<old> is now <new>`: a human's handles, an agent's global names, a project's full names |
| `note` | a manual post (§17.6) | as written |

`merge.title` and `merge.author` are the forge's, as the probe reads
them (§11); like every forge text they are data, rendered as text. The
`decision` text names the card and the request id and nothing of the
request; its content is added per reader (§17.5). `request` is
`{id, class, task_id}`, `release` is `{task_id, version}`, `deploy` is
`{environment, sha, version, log_url}` (any of the last three `null`
when the forge or the poster did not say).

A push to the default branch that no pull request carries writes no
item in this version (open, §17.11).

### 17.3 The audience

The hub computes the audience once, when it writes the item, from the
project's members, areas, cards, requests, settings and subscriptions at
that moment, and stores it in the event's `audience` as `member:<id>`
tokens (next to `all`, §17.5) and in `payload.reasons`. It is never
recomputed: an area that changes owner later does not move an old item.

| `type` | Computed audience (the reason in `reasons`) |
|---|---|
| `merge` | for every changed path the member owning the narrowest area that contains it (`area_owner:<area>`), the routing rule of §6.2; the holder of every linked card, and its assignee while nobody holds it (`card_holder:<id>`, `card_assignee:<id>`) |
| `merge` with `contract` | in addition, the implementers of each touched section (`contract_implementer:<section>`) and every member `trust:admin` names (§8.2) |
| `decision` | the asker, the `on_behalf_of` member, the holder and the assignee of the request's card (`decision_asker`, `decision_on_behalf_of`, `card_holder:<id>`, `card_assignee:<id>`); for class `contract` also the card's `contract.watchers` (`contract_watcher`) — each only if it may read the request (§17.5); one who may not is left out entirely |
| `release` | every active member (`all_members`) |
| `deploy` (automatic, §17.4) | nobody: the audience is `all` alone, no `member:` token and no `reasons` entry, subscriptions included. The item is listed for every member and wakes no one (§17.5) |
| `deploy` (manual) | as the poster addressed it (§17.6) |
| `rename` | nobody, as an automatic `deploy`: `all` alone, subscriptions included; listed for every member, wakes no one |
| `note` | as the poster addressed it (§17.6) |

Then the subscriptions (§17.8) apply: a member who follows a matching
area or type is added (`follow:<area>`, `follow:type:<type>`); a member
who muted a matching area or type is removed, except from a `decision`
it is the asker, the `on_behalf_of` member or the card holder of — a
decision one has to implement cannot be muted away. A follow of type
`decision` adds the member only when it may read the request; for
anyone else the item does not exist (§17.5). The item's actor
(the poster, the answering human) is in the audience only when a rule
names it, and is never woken by its own item (own echo, §8.2). Humans
are in the audience by the same rules; for them it means the item is
"for me" in the dashboard (§17.9), not a wake.

**Linked cards** of a merge: cards whose latest report (§6.6) names the
pull request (`report.pr.number`), cards whose latest checkpoint names
the pull request's head branch, and release cards that list the pull
request in `pull_requests_typed` — at most 20, oldest first.

**Changed paths** come from the forge's list of the pull request's
files, read through the probe (§11). The hub reads at most 300 files;
beyond that, or when the forge's list is incomplete, `paths_truncated`
is `true` and the area part of the audience becomes the owners of every
area of the project (`area_owner:*`): a merge the hub cannot see in full
reaches more members, never fewer.

**The path → area mapping** is the members' `areas` (§6.2) and nothing
else: an area is a path prefix, each path goes to the narrowest area
that contains it, `/` last. A project configures no second mapping for
areas; a path no area contains concerns nobody by area.

**Contract sections.** A project names its contract files and who
implements which section in `settings.ticker` (§6.1):

```json
{ "ticker": {
    "enabled": true,
    "contract_files": ["docs/api.md"],
    "contract_implementers": {
      "8": ["area:hub/", "area:cli/", "area:web/"],
      "13": ["area:cli/"],
      "15": ["area:cli/", "member:agt-b"],
      "*": ["area:hub/"]
    }
} }
```

- `enabled` (default `false`) switches the automatic sources on: merges,
  decisions, releases and deploys. The manual post (§17.6) works either
  way.
- A section is the number at the start of a level-two or level-three ATX
  heading of a contract file (`## 8. Events` → `8`, `### 8.2 Kinds…` →
  `8.2`). A changed line belongs to the nearest numbered heading above it
  in the file at the merge commit; a deleted line to the one above it in
  the file at the base. A changed heading line belongs to its own
  section.
- `contract_implementers` maps a section to tokens: `area:<path>` (the
  member owning the narrowest area that contains the path, §6.2 — the
  same meaning as in a manual post's `to`, §17.6), `member:<id>`,
  `role:<role>`, `trust:<trust>`. The longest
  matching key wins (`8.2` before `8`); `*` applies to a section no key
  matches. A token that names no current member, area, role or trust resolves
  to nobody; the settings view shows it as unresolved.
- When the hub cannot tell the sections — a contract file over 1 MiB, a
  diff the forge sends without its patch — `contract.sections_unknown`
  is `true` and every token of `contract_implementers` applies.
- Without `contract_files` no merge carries `contract`. `trust:admin` is
  added to every contract change, whatever the mapping says.
- Caps: 10 contract files, 200 keys, 20 tokens per key.

`settings.ticker` is set with `PATCH /projects/{owner}/{slug}` under
`project:admin`, like every setting, and so by a human (§2.3 ʰ); an
admin agent proposes a change through a request.

### 17.4 How the hub learns of merges and deploys

**The probe.** With the probe configured (§11) and the ticker enabled,
the hub reads on its own interval (every 2 minutes) the pull requests
closed against `default_branch` since the last one it announced, and
writes an item for each merged one not yet announced (§17.7). For each
it reads the file list and, when a contract file is among them, that
file at the merge commit and at the base. The grant (§11.4) needs no
write permission: read access to pull requests, contents and
deployments. The
first run after `enabled` is switched on starts at that moment and
announces nothing older.

**The webhook** is optional and only makes the hub look sooner.

```
POST /api/v1/projects/{owner}/{slug}/forge/webhook
```

- No credential and no cookie: the forge signs the body with a secret
  the hub issued for the project (`X-Hub-Signature-256`, HMAC-SHA256, on
  GitHub). A missing or wrong signature is `401 webhook_signature` with
  `details: {}`; a project without a secret, or one that does not exist,
  answers the same, so the path tells nobody whether a project exists.
  The join host answers it `not_found` (§1.1).
- Accepted forge events: `ping`; `pull_request` with action `closed`;
  `deployment_status`. Anything else is answered `202` and ignored. The
  body is a trigger, never a fact: for `pull_request` the hub reads the
  pull request through the probe and announces what the probe observes;
  for `deployment_status` it reads the deployment and its status the
  same way. A body that claims a merge the probe does not see writes
  nothing.
- The body cap is 1 MiB here (forge payloads exceed §1.7's 64 KiB),
  declared by exactly one `Content-Length`: a missing or repeated one, or
  one over the cap, is `payload_too_large` for every slug, before the hub
  looks the project up; the probe catches up on its interval. At most 60
  verified deliveries per minute per project (`rate_limited`): only a
  delivery whose signature verifies counts, so unsigned or wrongly signed
  requests cannot use up a project's deliveries. Every request reads its
  declared body before it is answered, for a project that does not exist
  or has no webhook secret too, so a body held back hangs alike whatever
  the slug.
- Every slug is treated the same until a signature verifies. Every
  request first takes a place in a bucket per source address (the
  client address of §2.5) and in a bucket per slug and source address,
  60 per minute each; when either is full the hub answers
  `rate_limited` with `Retry-After` at once, before the body. Then it
  reads the declared body, and only then refuses — no or a wrong
  signature, more than one signature header, a body over the cap, a
  project that does not exist or has no webhook secret — or verifies.
  Only a verified delivery gives both places back. So at most 60 bodies
  per slug and address, and 60 per address, are read at once, and
  neither the answer, the limit nor a body held back tells anyone
  whether a project exists or has a webhook secret. The cost, accepted:
  failing requests from one forge address can delay a verified delivery
  from the same address, since it takes its place before it verifies;
  the probe catches it up on its interval.
- A request that does not
  verify never sets `last_result` (below): anyone can send one, and the
  webhook view shows the state of the forge's real deliveries, not of
  whoever probes the URL. The answer is `202` with `{}` once the
  signature verifies; a signed body that is not a JSON object is
  `400 invalid`. The forge's delivery id is kept as `origin.delivery`
  when it is at most 64 letters, digits and `-` (else `null`), and only
  on the merge that delivery named.
- Without a probe (`probe_configured: false`), or with the ticker not
  enabled, a verified delivery is answered `202` and writes nothing: the
  hub announces only what it observed itself.

| Endpoint | Scope | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /projects/{owner}/{slug}/forge/webhook` | `project:admin`, human only | `{configured, url, created_at, rotated_at, last_delivery_at, last_result}`, both of the last verified delivery only; `last_result` is `ok`, `ignored`, `rate_limited` or `null`; never the secret. A stored secret the instance key cannot open (the key unset, changed or lost) counts as not set, as §16.2 has it for the SMTP password: `configured: false`, and deliveries are refused until the secret is rotated. A forge whose deliveries stop verifying (a secret rotated on one side only, a body over the cap) shows as a `last_delivery_at` that stops moving; the forge's own delivery log shows the `401` or `413` |
| `POST /projects/{owner}/{slug}/forge/webhook/secret` | `project:admin`, human only | creates or rotates the secret and answers it once, as `{secret, url}`; the previous secret stops working at once. Emits `forge_webhook_changed` |
| `DELETE /projects/{owner}/{slug}/forge/webhook/secret` | `project:admin`, human only | removes it; deliveries answer `webhook_signature` from then on. Emits `forge_webhook_changed` |

HMAC needs the secret itself, so the hub stores it encrypted with the
instance key `MAITY_SECRET_KEY` (proposed with the mail settings in
PR #160); without that key `POST …/webhook/secret` is
`409 secret_key_missing` (open, §17.11). The secret is a credential: it
is masked in the request log, never in an event, and in no response but
the one that creates it.

**Deploys** reach the hub through the webhook's `deployment_status` or
by hand (§17.6). The hub has no deploy concept of its own and does not
poll the forge's deployments. An automatic deploy item is listed for
every member and wakes no one (§17.3): a forge may report a deployment
for every preview environment of every pull request, and a wake per
supervised agent per push is a model run each.

### 17.5 Who reads an item, and who is woken

- **Reading.** A ticker event's audience holds `all` and the computed
  `member:` tokens; every member reads every item. A `decision` is the
  exception: its audience holds no `all` and no `role:` or `trust:` token. The
  request's readers (§7: the asker, the addressee — a member, or every
  member the addressed role or trust token resolves to —, the holders of
  `requests:answer`; and the `on_behalf_of` member, who receives the
  whole request with `request_answered`, §8.2) are resolved to
  `member:` tokens when the item is written, and the computed audience
  and the followers are filtered by the same rule then (§17.3). At read
  time the hub checks the rule again, per reader, on every read path
  (§8.3): a `decision` item is served only to a reader who may read its
  request at that moment, whatever the audience says, and the see-all
  extension of owners and admins (§8.2) does not widen it. A member who
  may not read the request gets nothing — no item, no title, no
  placeholder — and so does not learn that it was decided.
- **Waking.** For `ticker`, `all` makes an item readable and never
  wake-relevant, as for `project_updated` (§8.2). A `member:` token
  wakes only when the item's `reasons` hold an entry for that member
  with `wake: true`; a token without one only makes the item readable.
  `wake` is `true`, for an agent, for the computed audience — a manual post's addressed
  members (`addressed`) and, under `to: all`, every member
  (`posted_to_all`) included, §17.6 — and for followers, `false` for a
  followed-and-muted member (§17.8). For a human it is always `false`: the
  hub wakes no human (§17.10), and a human's `wait` does not return on an
  item that only lists it as "for me". A manual `to: all` therefore wakes
  every member that has not muted the item's type or area, through the
  members' own tokens, never through `all`; a mute wins and leaves the
  item listed. A `decision` wakes only its
  computed audience — the asker, the `on_behalf_of` member, the card's
  holder and assignee, the contract watchers, each a reader of the
  request: followers of `decision` are listed with `wake: false`, and
  the request's other readers have no `reasons` entry at all, so a
  decision never wakes a role's or trust's holders wholesale. An automatic `deploy`
  has no `member:` token and wakes no one. `maity wait` returns an item
  only to a member it wakes, never to its actor. A supervised session
  (§15.11) is woken by the same items.
- **Content per reader.** `text` names only what every reader of the
  item may read: pull requests, paths, areas and contract sections (the
  probe is `project:read`), card ids and titles, versions. For a
  `decision` the hub adds `detail` at read time — `{request_title,
  reply_label}`, the request's title and the label of the chosen reply;
  every reader of a `decision` item may read the request, so there is no
  reduced form. A free-text answer is never in it. `detail` is `null`
  for every other type. An item keeps its text when its card is
  cancelled or its pull request reverted: it records what was true when
  it was written.
- **`reasons`** is shown in full to human owners and admins. Every other
  reader, admin agents included, sees only its own entry, and the
  event's `audience` reduced to `all` and its own token: follows and
  mutes are a member's own business, which only the humans who run the
  project may see (§17.8).
- **Shaped per reader.** The hub stores one event and serves it per
  reader: `detail` added, `reasons` and `audience` reduced, a `decision`
  item withheld from a non-reader. This applies to every path that
  returns the event — `GET /events` with or without `wait`, the
  `--batch` array of `maity wait`, the resume packet's `events.items`
  and `ticker`, and the listing (§8.3).
- **Redaction** works as for every event (§8.5).

### 17.6 Manual post

```
POST /projects/{owner}/{slug}/ticker
```

Scope `ticker:post` (§2.3: trust `owner` and `admin`, and the role `ops`, humans and agents). For
what the hub cannot see — a deploy without a webhook, a note the team
must know — and, until the hub writes items itself, for releases. A
merge is never posted by hand: `type: merge` is `invalid`
(`details.fields.type: "not_for_type"`). Merges are announced only by
the hub, from what the probe observes (§17.4), so a manual post can
neither pre-empt the automatic item under its `dedupe_key` (§17.7) nor
narrow the audience a contract change must reach.

```json
{ "type": "note", "text": "Staging runs 0.3.0-rc.2 from now on; the old database is gone.",
  "url": "https://maity.team/oliver/maity/board?task=tsk-0040",
  "to": "computed", "areas": ["hub/"] }
```

The body, every field top-level:

| Field | Type | With `type` | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `type` | string | — | required: `note`, `deploy`, `release`; `merge` and `decision` are `not_for_type` |
| `text` | string | all | required, 1–280 code points |
| `url` | string | all | optional, absolute `https`, ≤ 2048 characters |
| `to` | `"computed"`, `"all"` or an array of 1–20 tokens | all | optional, default `"computed"` |
| `release_task_id` | string | `release` only, required there | the release card's id; the card must be `done`, whatever `to` says |
| `areas` | array of 1–20 paths | `note` only; required with `to: computed` | the note's areas |
| `deploy` | object `{environment, sha?, version?, log_url?}` | `deploy` only, required there | `log_url` absolute `https`, ≤ 2048 characters |

A field given for a type that does not take it is `invalid`
(`details.fields.<field>: "not_for_type"`); a required one missing is
`invalid` (`"required"`). Two more examples:

```json
{ "type": "deploy", "text": "Deployed 0.3.0-rc.2 to staging",
  "deploy": { "environment": "staging", "version": "0.3.0-rc.2",
              "log_url": "https://github.com/oliver-zehentleitner/maity/actions/runs/123" } }
```

```json
{ "type": "release", "text": "Released 0.3.0: first public release",
  "url": "https://maity.team/oliver/maity/board?task=tsk-0050", "release_task_id": "tsk-0050",
  "to": ["trust:admin", "area:cli/"] }
```

`maity ticker post` maps its flags one to one: the text argument →
`text`, `--type` → `type`, `--url` → `url`, `--to` → `to`,
`--release` → `release_task_id`, `--area` → `areas`, `--env`,
`--sha`, `--version`, `--log-url` → `deploy.environment`, `.sha`,
`.version`, `.log_url`. `--to` and `--area` are repeatable flags, one
value each, and become arrays in the order given; a value is never split
on commas or spaces. `--to computed` or `--to all` stands alone: given
twice, or together with a token, it is refused locally (exit 2); the hub
answers an array that contains `computed` or `all` with `invalid`. One
`--to TOKEN` is sent as a one-element array; without `--to` the field is
omitted.

- `type` is `note`, `deploy` or `release`; a `merge` is announced only
  by the hub (above) and a `decision` only by the inbox, so both are
  `not_for_type`. `text` 1–280 code points, plain text; `url` optional,
  `https` only (`invalid` otherwise).
- `release_task_id` names a release card that is `done`, for every `to`;
  any other card is `invalid` (`details.fields.release_task_id:
  "not_done"`).
- `to` is `computed` (the default), `all`, or a list of at most 20 tokens
  (`member:<id>`, `role:<role>`, `trust:<trust>`, `area:<path>`). `computed` runs §17.3
  from what the post names: `release_task_id` for a release; every
  member for a deploy; `areas` (at most 20 paths) for a note, whose
  owners are the audience. `all` puts every active member in the
  audience and wakes every unmuted one (`posted_to_all`): unlike the
  automatic items, whose `all` never wakes, a manual `to: all` wakes
  every member through its own `member:` token, a supervised session
  too — the poster chose to reach everyone, and the 5 such posts per hour
  (below) bound it. A mute wins (§17.3, §17.8): a member who muted the
  item's type or area is removed from the computed audience and not
  woken; it still lists the item, which every member reads through
  `all`.
- A token list is resolved at write time, like the computed audience,
  and stored as `member:<id>` tokens only — never as `role:`, `trust:` or `area:`
  tokens (§8.2 would read a `role:` or `trust:` token by its general rule):
  `member:<id>` is that member; `role:<role>` and `trust:<trust>` are
  every active member they name (§8.2); `area:<path>` is the member owning the narrowest
  area that contains the path (§6.2), nobody when no area does — the one
  meaning of an `area:` token in this section, `contract_implementers`
  included (§17.3). A `member:` token that
  names no active member, or a malformed token, is `invalid`
  (`details.fields.to`); a role, trust or area that resolves to nobody adds
  nobody. Each resolved member gets a `reasons` entry with `why:
  "addressed"` and `wake: true` — addressed by the poster counts as
  computed for waking (§17.5); a member named by several tokens gets one
  entry. The subscriptions then apply as to any computed audience
  (§17.3): a mute wins over the addressing, as under `to: all`.
- `deploy` is `{environment, sha?, version?, log_url?}` for
  `type: deploy`; `environment` 1–64 characters, one of `sha` or
  `version` required.
- The item's `actor` is the poster, `origin.via` is `manual`. Mentions
  are not resolved in `text` (§8.6); who must know is `to`.
- `201` with the event. A post whose `dedupe_key` exists is
  `409 ticker_duplicate`, `details.seq` naming the existing item.
- At most 20 manual posts per membership per hour, of them at most 5 with
  `to: all` (`rate_limited`).

### 17.7 Dedupe

Every automatic item, and every manual one but a note, carries a
`dedupe_key`, unique per project:

| `type` | Key |
|---|---|
| `merge` | `merge:<pull request number>` |
| `decision` | `decision:<request id>` |
| `release` | `release:<version>` |
| `deploy` | `deploy:<environment>:<sha, or version when there is no sha>` |
| `rename` | none: every rename is an item of its own |
| `note` | none: every note is an item of its own |

The key is written in the same transaction as the event, under a unique
constraint. A probe run and a webhook delivery that observe the same
merge write one item; the second finds the key and writes nothing. A
manual post whose key exists is `ticker_duplicate`; an automatic source
that finds a key a manual post wrote writes nothing — the manual item
stands with the audience it was given. That can only happen for a
deploy or a release: a merge is never posted by hand (§17.6), and a
manual release names a card already `done`, whose automatic item the
hub has written by then when the ticker is enabled. A merge is one item whatever it
touches: a contract change, several areas and the linked cards are
fields of that one item, never items of their own.

### 17.8 Subscriptions: follow and mute

Each membership holds its own subscription, and only that member
changes it. Human owners and admins, a proxy not included, may see every member's subscription
— through `ticker_subscription_changed` (§17.12) and the full `reasons`
of an item (§17.5) — as they see every event of the project. No agent
sees another member's, admin agents included: neither the event nor
others' `reasons` entries reach an agent, and no endpoint returns
another member's subscription.

```json
{ "follow": { "areas": ["web/"], "types": ["release"] },
  "mute":   { "areas": ["context/"], "types": ["note"] },
  "updated_at": "2026-10-22T16:00:00Z" }
```

| Endpoint | Scope | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /projects/{owner}/{slug}/ticker/subscription` | the caller's own membership | the shape above, empty lists when never set |
| `PATCH /projects/{owner}/{slug}/ticker/subscription` | the caller's own membership | `{"add"?: {"follow"?: {"areas"?, "types"?}, "mute"?: {…}}, "remove"?: {…the same…}}`, applied in one transaction; answers `200` with the whole subscription. Adding a value already there or removing one that is not there is a no-op; the same value in `add` and `remove` of the same list is `invalid`. `areas` are paths in the form of §6.2 (not necessarily an existing area), at most 20 per list after the change (`invalid`, `details.fields.<list>: "too_many"`); `types` from `merge`, `contract`, `decision`, `deploy`, `release`, `note`, where `contract` means a merge with `contract` set. A value may be in `follow` and `mute` at once (below). Emits `ticker_subscription_changed` when something changed |

There is no replace: two sessions of the same member that change the
subscription at the same time both land, because each call names only
what it adds or removes; nothing is read first. Example — follow `web/`
and stop muting notes:

```json
PATCH /projects/oliver/maity/ticker/subscription
{ "add": { "follow": { "areas": ["web/"] } }, "remove": { "mute": { "types": ["note"] } } }
```

A follow or mute by area matches a merge or note whose `paths` or
`areas` fall under the path; by type, items of that type. A mute removes
the member from the computed audience (§17.3, with the `decision`
exception). Subscriptions act when an item is written, never on items
already written; a muted item stays readable in the listing and the
packet.

**Followed and muted at once.** When an item matches both a follow and a
mute of the same member, the mute wins for waking and the follow still
lists: the member gets no `member:` token in the audience (never woken, §17.10), but keeps an entry in `reasons` with
`muted: true` and `wake: false`, so the item is `for_me` in the listing
and the packet. A
mute without a matching follow removes the member's entry entirely, as
above. The `decision` exception is unchanged: there the member stays in
the audience, unmuted.

### 17.9 Listing, the resume packet, the dashboard

```
GET /projects/{owner}/{slug}/ticker?type=merge,deploy&area=hub/&for=me&limit=50
```

Scope `project:read`. The items the caller may read (§17.5), newest
first, paged (§1.4); with `after=<seq>` instead of a cursor, oldest
first, as on the events endpoint (§8.3), without `wait`. Filters: `type`
(comma list; `contract` as in §17.8), `area` (items whose `paths` or
`areas` fall under it), `for` = `me` (items whose `reasons` hold an entry
for the caller, muted ones included, §17.8) or `all` (default), `since`
(RFC 3339 with an offset; without one `invalid`). Paging as for every
listing (§1.4): `limit` default 50, maximum 200, `next_cursor` `null` on
the last page, a cursor valid for one filter set. Each item:

```json
{ "id": "tck-4302", "seq": 4302, "at": "2026-10-22T15:02:40Z", "type": "merge",
  "text": "…", "url": "…", "actor": null, "subject": { "type": "pull_request", "id": "212" },
  "areas": ["hub/", "/"], "contract": { "sections": ["6.5", "13"], "sections_unknown": false },
  "tasks": ["tsk-0031"], "for_me": true, "why": ["area_owner:hub/", "card_holder:tsk-0031"],
  "muted": false, "detail": null, "redacted": false }
```

`for_me`, `why` and `muted` are the caller's own (§17.5, §17.8); `why`
is `[]` and `muted` `false` when the item is not for the caller. The full payload is the
event's (`GET /events`); this is its compact form. Reading the listing
acknowledges nothing and moves no cursor.

**The resume packet** (§5.2) gains `ticker`: `{items, for_me, others,
truncated}` — the items after the cursor the agent may read, at most 20
in the listing's form, those `for_me` first and then the newest; `for_me`
and `others` count all such items, `truncated` says there are more
(`GET …/ticker?after=<cursor>`). The same items stay in `events.items`
as readable events; `maity resume` prints the `ticker` section and leaves
them out of "missed events", so nothing is printed twice.

**Text form** (the CLI's choice; used by `maity ticker` and the `Ticker`
section of `maity resume`, and by nothing else). One line per item,
`[ticker] <type>: <text>`, then ` <url>` when there is one; for an item
that is `for_me`, an indented second line `  for you: <why>` with the
`why` tokens as the API writes them, joined by `, `
(`  for you: area_owner:hub/, card_holder:tsk-0031`), and ` (muted)` at
its end when `muted` is true. The words of the dashboard ("you own
hub/") are the dashboard's. `maity ticker` prints the page in the
listing's order and, when `next_cursor` is not `null`, a last line
`more: maity ticker <the same flags> --cursor <next_cursor>`; it never
